title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試小錄序
文章之關於治道尚矣我
朝
列聖垂統人文化成興學設科以待天下之士薰陶琢磨
養育成就至于久而益盛故凡科舉程式之文必歸於
醇正典雅以成一代之制而動以古人自期士之英華發
於外者如此則其德之蘊諸中從可知焉洪惟
皇上嗣大寶之四年當天下大比之秋福建藩臬重臣遵承
明詔罔敢或怠維時兵部尚書孫原貞以
===
先朝老成來鎮是邦監察御史倪敬應灝以風紀之
重按治列郡董勵學校作興士類謂舉行
盛典期得真才以裨治道於是禮聘師儒參校文藝
至期監察御史敬職專監臨秉心至公糾督詳密
按察副使胡新僉事趙訪勤於綜理慎于防範右
參議李迪則提調於內右布政使石瑁按察使楊珏
副使徐朝宗左參議鄧履純僉事沈訥宋洵馬琬
布政司署司事都轉運鹽使司運使史潜綱維其外
合郡縣來試之士九百有竒取文之中式者一百三十
punctuated:
福建鄉試小錄序

文章之關於治道尚矣。我朝列聖垂統，人文化成，興學設科以待天下之士，薰陶琢磨，養育成就，至于久而益盛。故凡科舉程式之文，必歸於醇正典雅，以成一代之制，而動以古人自期。士之英華發於外者如此，則其德之蘊諸中從可知焉。洪惟皇上嗣大寶之四年，當天下大比之秋，福建藩臬重臣遵承明詔，罔敢或怠。維時兵部尚書孫原貞以先朝老成來鎮是邦，監察御史倪敬、應灝以風紀之重按治列郡，董勵學校，作興士類，謂舉行盛典，期得真才以裨治道，於是禮聘師儒，參校文藝。至期，監察御史敬職專監臨，秉心至公，糾督詳密；按察副使胡新、僉事趙訪勤於綜理，慎于防範；右參議李迪則提調於內；右布政使石瑁、按察使楊珏、副使徐朝宗、左參議鄧履純、僉事沈訥、宋洵、馬琬、布政司署司事都轉運鹽使司運使史潜綱維其外。合郡縣來試之士九百有竒，取文之中式者一百三十
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

Literary composition has long been of vital importance to the way of governance. In our dynasty, the successive sage emperors have handed down the imperial lineage, transforming and perfecting the realm through cultural education. They have promoted schools and established the civil service examinations to await the scholars of the empire, nurturing and polishing them, fostering and bringing them to fulfillment, so that with the passage of time this enterprise has grown ever more flourishing. Thus, all model compositions of the civil service examinations must return to what is pure, orthodox, refined, and classical, so as to form the institution of an entire era, while scholars at every turn take the ancients as their personal standard. When the finest blossoms of the scholars are manifested externally like this, the virtue stored within them can accordingly be known.

humbly reflecting on the fourth year since His Majesty succeeded to the Great Treasure, which corresponds to the autumn of the triennial Grand Comparison across the empire, the senior provincial administrative and judicial officials of Fujian respectfully obeyed the illustrious edict, none daring to be in the least remiss. At this time, the Minister of War Sun Yuanzhen 孫原貞, as a veteran statesman of a previous reign, had come to pacify and govern this region, while the Investigating Censors Ni Jing 倪敬 and Ying Hao 應灝, bearing the weighty responsibility of maintaining disciplinary standards, toured and governed the various prefectures, supervising and encouraging the schools and rousing the body of scholars. Declaring that in conducting this grand state ceremony they hoped to obtain true talent to aid the way of governance, they thereupon courteously engaged teachers and Confucian scholars to participate in evaluating the literary compositions.

When the appointed time arrived, Investigating Censor Jing [Ni Jing] held specific responsibility as Supervising Official, maintaining the utmost impartiality of mind and inspecting and supervising with meticulous thoroughness. Surveillance Vice Commissioner Hu Xin 胡新 and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Zhao Fang 趙訪 were diligent in overall management and cautious in taking precautions against irregularities. Right Administration Vice Commissioner Li Di 李迪 served as Proctor on the inside; meanwhile, Right Administration Commissioner Shi Mao 石瑁, Surveillance Commissioner Yang Jue 楊珏, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Xu Chaozong 徐朝宗, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Deng Lüchun 鄧履純, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Shen Ne 沈訥, Song Xun 宋洵, and Ma Wan 馬琬, as well as Salt Distribution Commissioner Shi Qian 史潜, acting in charge of the affairs of the Provincial Administration Commission, maintained general oversight on the outside. Together, the scholars who came from the prefectures and counties to take the examination numbered slightly over nine hundred, and those whose compositions met the standard and were selected numbered one hundred and thirty-…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
七人十預是選可謂榮矣旣刻小録僉謂大年忝司文
衡宜序其首惟文章為不朽之盛事今
朝廷稽古右文簡賢輔治士大夫通經學古纘言為文
以敷闡大猷潤色鴻業如日星麗而江河流彝鼎列
而金石奏昭回雲漢澤及庶物薦之郊廟感格神明
誠千載之遇也豈直夸一時而榮一鄉哉雖然予尚有
告焉古之人若臯夔稷契伊傅周召有聖賢之事功
吐辭為經垂教萬世諸士子發身賢科遭逢
聖明亦將慨然有志於斯乎養氣以配其道脩辭以立
===
其誠由是而治具張德業隆高山景行企而及之以無
忝斯科之舉景泰四年秋八月旣望
浙江杭州府仁和縣儒學教諭聶大年序
punctuated:
七人。士預是選，可謂榮矣。旣刻小録，僉謂大年忝司文衡，宜序其首。惟文章為不朽之盛事。今朝廷稽古右文，簡賢輔治，士大夫通經學古，纘言為文，以敷闡大猷，潤色鴻業，如日星麗而江河流，彝鼎列而金石奏，昭回雲漢，澤及庶物，薦之郊廟，感格神明，誠千載之遇也，豈直夸一時而榮一鄉哉？雖然，予尚有告焉。古之人若臯、夔、稷、契、伊、傅、周、召，有聖賢之事功，吐辭為經，垂教萬世。諸士子發身賢科，遭逢聖明，亦將慨然有志於斯乎？養氣以配其道，脩辭以立其誠，由是而治具張、德業隆，高山景行，企而及之，以無忝斯科之舉。
景泰四年秋八月旣望，浙江杭州府仁和縣儒學教諭聶大年序。
translation_en:
… seven men. For scholars[?] to be included in this selection may indeed be called an honor. Now that the examination record has been carved onto blocks for printing, everyone said that since I, Da-nian, had the undeserved honor of presiding over the literary balance as examiner, I ought to write a preface at its head.

Literature is an imperishable and grand enterprise. Today the imperial court investigates antiquity and esteems civil culture, selecting the worthy to assist in governance. Scholar-officials master the Classics and study the ancient ways, composing words into literature so as to set forth the great plan and adorn the grand imperial enterprise—shining brightly in the heavens like the sun and stars and flowing across the earth like the Yangtze and Yellow rivers, arrayed like sacrificial vessels and tripods and sounding forth like bronze bells and stone chimes, resplendent as the Milky Way in the sky, extending blessings to all things, and when presented at the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temples, moving the spirits and gods. Truly this is an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years! How could it merely be something to boast of for a brief moment or to bring glory to a single locality?

Even so, I still have words of advice. Among the men of antiquity—such as Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, Xie, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao—they possessed the achievements of sages and worthies; the words they uttered became Classics, handing down teachings for ten thousand generations. Now that you scholars have launched your careers through the recruitment of the worthy and encountered a sagely and enlightened ruler, will you not also be stirred with high ambition to emulate them? Nourish your vital breath so as to match the Way, and cultivate your words so as to establish your sincerity. Proceeding from this, the instruments of governance will be spread wide and your virtuous achievements will flourish; looking up to the high mountains and luminous conduct of the ancients, strive on tiptoe to reach them, so as not to bring shame upon your selection in this examination.

Written as a preface on the sixteenth day of the eighth month in the autumn of the fourth year of the Jingtai reign (September 18, 1453) by Nie Danian 聶大年, Instructor of the Confucian School of Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
第一場
四書
子張問士何如斯可謂之達矣子曰何哉爾所謂
達者子張對曰在邦必聞在家必聞子曰是聞
也非達也夫達也者質直而好義察言而觀色慮
以下人在邦必達在家必達夫聞也者色取仁而
行違居之不疑在邦必聞在家必聞
柔遠人則四方歸之懷諸侯則天下畏之
使之主祭而百神享之是天受之使之主事而事治
===
百姓安之是民受之也
易
大觀在上順而巽中正以觀天下觀盥而不薦有孚顒
若下觀而化也
有孚維心亨行有尚
初六允升大吉象曰允升大吉上合志也
夫易開物成務冒天下之道如斯而已者也是故聖人以
通天下之志以定天下之業以斷天下之疑
書
punctuated:
第一場

四書
子張問：「士何如斯可謂之達矣？」子曰：「何哉，爾所謂達者？」子張對曰：「在邦必聞，在家必聞。」子曰：「是聞也，非達也。夫達也者，質直而好義，察言而觀色，慮以下人，在邦必達，在家必達。夫聞也者，色取仁而行違，居之不疑，在邦必聞，在家必聞。」
柔遠人，則四方歸之；懷諸侯，則天下畏之。
使之主祭而百神享之，是天受之；使之主事而事治，百姓安之，是民受之也。

易
大觀在上，順而巽，中正以觀天下。觀，盥而不薦，有孚顒若，下觀而化也。
有孚，維心亨，行有尚。
初六，允升，大吉。象曰：允升大吉，上合志也。
夫易，開物成務，冒天下之道，如斯而已者也。是故聖人以通天下之志，以定天下之業，以斷天下之疑。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books (Sishu)
Zizhang asked: "What must a scholar-official (shi) be like before he can be called truly accomplished (da)?" The Master said: "What do you mean by what you call accomplished?" Zizhang replied: "In a state, he is sure to be renowned; in a noble family, he is sure to be renowned." The Master said: "That is renown (wen), not accomplishment (da). Now the man of true accomplishment is upright in his native substance and fond of righteousness; he examines people's words and observes their countenances, and is thoughtful in humbling himself before others. In a state he is sure to be accomplished, and in a noble family he is sure to be accomplished. As for the man of mere renown, he assumes the outward appearance of benevolence while his deeds violate it, and he dwells in this without a doubt. In a state he is sure to be renowned, and in a noble family he is sure to be renowned."
By treating men from afar with gentleness, the four quarters are drawn to him; by cherishing the feudal lords, the whole world holds him in awe.
When he was placed in charge of sacrifices and the hundred spirits enjoyed them, that showed Heaven accepted him; when he was placed in charge of affairs and affairs were well ordered and the common people were at peace with them, that showed the people accepted him.

Classic of Changes (Yi)
Great Contemplation (Guan) is above; docile and penetrating, central and correct, so as to be contemplated by all under heaven. "Contemplation: the ablution has been made, but not yet the offering; there is sincerity and an aspect of solemn dignity"—those below contemplate him and are transformed.
"There is sincerity; in the heart there is penetrative success, and action brings high esteem."
Six at the beginning: "Advancing (Sheng) with confidence; great good fortune." The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: "'Advancing with confidence, great good fortune': he is in harmony of purpose with those above."
Now the Changes opens up the resources of things, brings human affairs to completion, and encompasses all the ways under heaven—this and nothing more. Therefore the sages used it to penetrate the wills of all under heaven, to establish the enterprises of all under heaven, and to resolve the doubts of all under heaven.

Classic of Documents (Shu)

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
先王惟時懋敬厥德克配上帝今王嗣有令緒尚監茲
哉若升高必自下若陟遐必自邇無輕民事惟難無
安厥位惟危慎終于始有言逆于汝心必求諸道
有言遜于汝志必求諸非道嗚呼弗慮胡獲弗為
胡成一人元良萬邦以貞
非天私我有商惟天佑于一德非商求于下民惟民歸
于一德德惟一動罔不吉
惠不惠懋不懋
王厥有成命治民今休
===
詩
鳲鳩在桑其子七兮淑人君子其儀一兮其儀一兮心如
結兮
勉勉我王綱紀四方
申伯信邁王餞于郿申伯還南謝于誠歸王命召伯
徹申伯土疆以峙其糇式遄其行
庸鼓有斁萬舞有奕我有嘉客亦不夷懌自古在昔
先民有作溫恭朝夕執事有恪顧予烝嘗湯孫
之將
punctuated:
先王惟時懋敬厥德，克配上帝。今王嗣有令緒，尚監茲哉！若升高，必自下；若陟遐，必自邇。無輕民事惟難，無安厥位惟危。慎終于始。有言逆于汝心，必求諸道；有言遜于汝志，必求諸非道。嗚呼！弗慮胡獲？弗為胡成？一人元良，萬邦以貞。
非天私我有商，惟天佑于一德；非商求于下民，惟民歸于一德。德惟一，動罔不吉。
惠不惠，懋不懋。
王厥有成命，治民今休。
詩
鳲鳩在桑，其子七兮。淑人君子，其儀一兮。其儀一兮，心如結兮。
勉勉我王，綱紀四方。
申伯信邁，王餞于郿。申伯還南，謝于誠歸。王命召伯，徹申伯土疆，以峙其糇，式遄其行。
庸鼓有斁，萬舞有奕。我有嘉客，亦不夷懌。自古在昔，先民有作。溫恭朝夕，執事有恪。顧予烝嘗，湯孫之將。
translation_en:
"The former king thereupon strenuously revered his virtue, and so was able to be a counterpart to God on High. Now that Your Majesty has succeeded to this fine inheritance, look to this example! It is like ascending on high: one must begin from below; it is like travelling afar: one must begin from what is near. Do not slight the affairs of the people—think only of their difficulty; do not rest at ease in your position—think only of its peril. Be careful of the end at the beginning. When words run counter to your heart, you must seek whether they accord with the Way; when words conform smoothly to your will, you must seek whether they depart from the Way. Oh! Without anxious thought, what can be gained? Without action, what can be achieved? When the One Man is supremely good, the myriad states are thereby rectified."
"It was not that Heaven showed partiality to our Shang; Heaven solely aids pure and constant virtue. It was not that Shang sought the allegiance of the lower people; the people solely turn to pure and constant virtue. Where virtue is pure and constant, in every movement there is nothing that is not auspicious."
"Be kind to the unkind; encourage the unencouraged."
"Since the king has received the accomplished Mandate, in governing the people there will now be auspiciousness."

Classic of Poetry (Shi)
"The cuckoo is in the mulberry tree, and her young ones are seven. The virtuous man, the princely lord, is uniform in his deportment; uniform in his deportment, his heart is as if bound fast."
"Tireless is our king, bringing order to the four quarters."
"The Lord of Shen truly set forth, and the king gave him a farewell feast at Mei. The Lord of Shen turned south, genuinely returning to Xie. The king commanded the Lord of Shao to assess the lands and boundaries of the Lord of Shen, so as to store up his dry provisions and speed his journey."
"The large bells and drums ring out in harmony; the wan dances are grandly performed. We have admirable guests—how could they too not be pleased and delighted? From of old, in ancient times, the former people instituted this: be mild and reverent morning and night, and execute the sacrificial service with care. May He look upon our winter and autumn sacrifices, presented by the descendant of Tang!"

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
春秋
蔡人衛人陳人從王伐鄭桓公五年齊侯宋人陳人蔡人
邾人會于北杏莊公十三年會陳人蔡人楚人鄭人盟于
齊僖公十九年
王人子突救衛莊公六年城楚丘僖公二年
齊高子來盟閔公二年楚屈完來盟于師僖公四年宋司馬
華孫來盟文公十五年
公會晋侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衛子莒子盟于踐土僖
公二十八年同盟于亳城北襄公十一年
===
禮記
昔先王尚有德尊有道任有能舉賢而置之聚衆而誓之
是故因天事天因地事地因名山升中于天因吉土以
饗帝于郊
郊之祭也迎長日之至也大報天而主日也兆於南郊就陽
位也掃地而祭於其質也器用陶匏以象天地之性也
仁者仁此者也禮者履此者也義者宜此者也信者信此
者也強者強此者也
唯賢者能盡祭之義賢者之祭也必受其福
punctuated:
《春秋》
蔡人、衛人、陳人從王伐鄭，桓公五年；齊侯、宋人、陳人、蔡人、邾人會于北杏，莊公十三年；會陳人、蔡人、楚人、鄭人盟于齊，僖公十九年。
王人子突救衛，莊公六年；城楚丘，僖公二年。
齊高子來盟，閔公二年；楚屈完來盟于師，僖公四年；宋司馬華孫來盟，文公十五年。
公會晋侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衛子、莒子盟于踐土，僖公二十八年；同盟于亳城北，襄公十一年。

《禮記》
昔先王尚有德，尊有道，任有能，舉賢而置之，聚衆而誓之。
是故因天事天，因地事地，因名山升中于天，因吉土以饗帝于郊。
郊之祭也，迎長日之至也，大報天而主日也。兆於南郊，就陽位也；掃地而祭，於其質也；器用陶匏，以象天地之性也。
仁者仁此者也，禮者履此者也，義者宜此者也，信者信此者也，強者強此者也。
唯賢者能盡祭之義，賢者之祭也，必受其福。
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"Men of Cai, men of Wei, and men of Chen followed the King to attack Zheng" (Duke Huan, 5th year); "The Marquis of Qi, men of Song, men of Chen, men of Cai, and men of Zhu met at Beixing" (Duke Zhuang, 13th year); "[They] met men of Chen, men of Cai, men of Chu, and men of Zheng and made a covenant in Qi" (Duke Xi, 19th year).
"The King's man Zitu went to the rescue of Wei" (Duke Zhuang, 6th year); "[They] walled Chuqiu" (Duke Xi, 2nd year).
"Master Gao of Qi came to make a covenant" (Duke Min, 2nd year); "Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the armies" (Duke Xi, 4th year); "Hua Sun, Marshal of Song, came to make a covenant" (Duke Wen, 15th year).
"The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Heir of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju and made a covenant at Jiantu" (Duke Xi, 28th year); "[They] joined in a covenant north of the city of Bo" (Duke Xiang, 11th year).

Record of Rites (Liji)
"In antiquity, the former kings esteemed those who had virtue, honored those who possessed the Way, employed those who had ability, promoted the worthy and placed them in office, and assembled the multitude and bound them with an oath."
"Therefore, conforming to Heaven, they served Heaven; conforming to Earth, they served Earth; making use of famous mountains, they offered up the report of peaceful governance to Heaven; making use of auspicious ground, they presented offerings to the Supreme Ruler in the suburban sacrifice."
"The suburban sacrifice welcomes the arrival of the lengthening days; it is a great thanksgiving to Heaven, with the sun as its primary object. Its altar site is set in the southern suburb to take the position of yang; the ground is swept for the sacrifice to cleave to simplicity; the vessels used are of earthenware and gourds to symbolize the nature of Heaven and Earth."
"The humane person is one who embodies humanity in this; the person of ritual propriety is one who puts this into practice; the righteous person is one who acts fittingly in this; the trustworthy person is one who is true to this; the strong person is one who exerts strength in this."
"Only the worthy person can exhaust the meaning of sacrifice; in the sacrifice of a worthy person, he is certain to receive its blessings."

text:

策五道
問欽惟
太宗文皇帝萬幾之暇取古人為善獲報者百六十五人載之
於書名為善陰隲嘉惠臣民誠萬世之大寶也其間
punctuated:
第二塲
論：
聖位天德。

詔、誥、表〔内科一道〕：
擬漢文帝卻千里馬詔；
擬唐以陸贄為翰林學士誥；

第三塲
策五道

問：欽惟太宗文皇帝萬幾之暇，取古人為善獲報者百六十五人，載之於書，名《為善陰隲》，嘉惠臣民，誠萬世之大寶也。其間

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
有立定大計口不言功為治循良舉善而教出師不
殺臨政温仁敦義詳審平量護遺擇嫁還女仁惠
公直察誣興利經濟蠲輸其人可得而歴數歟夜燭
治書死獄求生三喪未舉麥舟相濟與夫燒券平糴
濟渡施歾息民活衆德化廉能其人亦可得而備言
歟有陰德者必有陽報諸士子游學庠序必講之
素明矣願詳陳之庶幾不負
聖人垂憲勸善之深意
問理數之學儒者所當知也其詳見於周子之太極通
===
書張子之西銘正蒙邵子之先天經世然其間微辭
奧旨不能無疑矣且太極一圖剖析精微易通一書
又所以法此圖者也謂圖書相為表裏者何所見歟
易有太極而圖加以無極豈太極之外復有所謂無
極者哉或謂古書有所謂太一有所謂太易太初太
始太素其與太極同歟異歟程子學於周子其圖親
得手授之傳何著書立言傳道解惑未甞有一言及
於圖之指趣歟西銘之旨程子謂其理一而分殊果
何見歟又謂其書與孟子性善之論同功或者疑
punctuated:
有立定大計、口不言功，為治循良、舉善而教，出師不殺、臨政温仁，敦義、詳審，平量、護遺，擇嫁、還女，仁惠、公直，察誣、興利，經濟、蠲輸，其人可得而歴數歟？夜燭治書、死獄求生，三喪未舉、麥舟相濟，與夫燒券、平糴，濟渡、施歾，息民、活衆，德化、廉能，其人亦可得而備言歟？有陰德者必有陽報，諸士子游學庠序，必講之素明矣。願詳陳之，庶幾不負聖人垂憲勸善之深意。

問：理數之學，儒者所當知也。其詳見於周子之《太極》、《通書》，張子之《西銘》、《正蒙》，邵子之《先天》、《經世》，然其間微辭奧旨，不能無疑矣。且《太極》一圖剖析精微，《易通》一書又所以法此圖者也，謂圖、書相為表裏者，何所見歟？《易》有太極，而圖加以無極，豈太極之外復有所謂無極者哉？或謂古書有所謂太一，有所謂太易、太初、太始、太素，其與太極同歟，異歟？程子學於周子，其圖親得手授之傳，何著書立言、傳道解惑，未甞有一言及於圖之指趣歟？《西銘》之旨，程子謂其理一而分殊，果何見歟？又謂其書與孟子性善之論同功，或者疑
translation_en:
… there are those who established great plans yet never spoke of their merit; who governed as model officials, promoting the good and instructing them; who led armies without killing and administered government with gentle benevolence; who esteemed righteousness and exercised careful deliberation; who leveled measures and protected what was left behind; who chose a husband for an orphan and returned a daughter; who showed benevolent kindness and public rectitude; who detected false accusations and promoted public benefit; who managed affairs to give relief and remitted taxes and transport obligations—can these individuals be enumerated one by one? Those who reviewed documents by candlelight at night and sought ways to spare lives in capital cases; who helped one with three unburied dead by giving a boatload of wheat; as well as those who burned debt tallies and sold grain at fair prices, provided ferry crossings and gave coffins to the dead, brought rest to the people and saved the multitude, transformed others through virtue and showed incorruptible ability—can these individuals also be recounted in full? Those who possess hidden virtue invariably receive manifest rewards. You scholars studying in the schools must have long discussed and understood this clearly. Please set it forth in detail, so as perhaps not to disappoint the Sage's profound intention in handing down models to encourage goodness.

Question: The learning of principle and number is something Confucian scholars ought to know. Its details appear in Master Zhou's [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤] Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu) and Penetrating the Book of Changes (Tongshu), Master Zhang's [Zhang Zai 張載] Western Inscription (Ximing) and Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng), and Master Shao's [Shao Yong 邵雍] Prior to Heaven (Xiantian) diagrams and Book of Supreme World-Ordering Principles (Huangji jingshi shu); yet among their subtle words and profound meanings, one cannot be without doubts. Moreover, the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate analyzes the subtle and minute, while the book Penetrating the Book of Changes (Yitong) is modeled upon this diagram; on what basis is it said that the diagram and the book form the exterior and interior of one another? The Book of Changes has the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji), yet the diagram adds the Ultimateless (Wuji) to it—could there really be a so-called Ultimateless outside the Supreme Ultimate? Some say that in ancient books there is what is called the Great One (Taiyi), and what are called the Great Change (Taiyi), the Great Inception (Taichu), the Great Beginning (Taishi), and the Great Simplicity (Taisu)—are these the same as or different from the Supreme Ultimate? The Masters Cheng [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤] studied under Master Zhou and personally received the transmission of his diagram from his own hand; why then, in writing books and establishing teachings, transmitting the Way and resolving doubts, did they never once mention a single word about the purport of the diagram? As for the meaning of the Western Inscription, Master Cheng said that its principle is one while its allotments are diverse—what indeed was his insight? He also said that this work is equal in merit to Mencius's [Mengzi 孟子] discourse on the goodness of human nature; yet some suspect…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
其流於兼愛何歟正蒙語造化則極乎日月寒暑之
變語鬼神則極乎二氣良能之妙語隂陽則一神两
化之論備語性命則太虛氣化之論詳其與太極易
通西銘同一理歟先天圖有變象比象感象應象有
往数来數隂數陽數者何歟經世之數起乎四無非發明
此圖者也二者皆以数言其與太極之理相戾歟然理與
數固未始相離也先儒何謂太極不如先天之大先天不
如太極之精歟然先天之易先儒指為心法而後来者
反名其書為考數其言孰是孰非歟諸君子窮究理
===
數之學必貫通矣願以朱子無極之辨通書之解西銘
正蒙之訓釋皇極經世之考正會合諸子之論同出乎
一揆可也
問廉退士君子之所尚也三代而下若子雲漢之大儒猶有
求媚取容甘於美新之作昌黎一代山斗一不得志至
三上宰相之書自餘何望焉有宋盛時上以禮義維其
俗下以廉耻律其身英風義槩凛凛相望故玉堂獻
記不入翰苑河平獻頌不留蘭臺不以私書至京師則
擢之御史不以私事干朝廷則處之諫諍其人可得而
punctuated:
其流於兼愛，何歟？《正蒙》語造化，則極乎日月寒暑之變；語鬼神，則極乎二氣良能之妙；語隂陽，則一神两化之論備；語性命，則太虛氣化之論詳。其與《太極》、《易通》、《西銘》同一理歟？《先天圖》有變象、比象、感象、應象，有往数、来數、隂數、陽數者，何歟？《經世》之數起乎四，無非發明此圖者也，二者皆以数言，其與《太極》之理相戾歟？然理與數固未始相離也，先儒何謂《太極》不如《先天》之大，《先天》不如《太極》之精歟？然先天之《易》，先儒指為心法，而後来者反名其書為考數，其言孰是孰非歟？諸君子窮究理數之學，必貫通矣，願以朱子無極之辨、《通書》之解、《西銘》《正蒙》之訓釋、《皇極經世》之考正，會合諸子之論，同出乎一揆可也。

問：廉退，士君子之所尚也。三代而下，若子雲，漢之大儒，猶有求媚取容，甘於《美新》之作；昌黎，一代山斗，一不得志，至三上宰相之書，自餘何望焉？有宋盛時，上以禮義維其俗，下以廉耻律其身，英風義槩，凛凛相望。故玉堂獻記，不入翰苑；河平獻頌，不留蘭臺。不以私書至京師，則擢之御史；不以私事干朝廷，則處之諫諍。其人可得而
translation_en:
… that it slips into Mohist universal love—why is this? When Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng) speaks of cosmic creation and transformation, it exhausts the changes of sun and moon, cold and heat; when it speaks of ghosts and spirits, it exhausts the marvels of the innate capacities of the two vital forces (qi); when it speaks of yin and yang, the discourse on the one spirit and dual transformations is complete; when it speaks of human nature and destiny, the discourse on the Great Vacuity (taixu) and the transformation of vital force is detailed. Do these share the exact same principle as the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taijitu), Penetrating the Book of Changes (Yitong), and the Western Inscription (Ximing)? What is the meaning of the Diagram of the Prior to Heaven (Xiantiantu) having images of change, images of comparison, images of stimulus, and images of response, as well as numbers of the past, numbers of the future, yin numbers, and yang numbers? The numbers in Supreme Principles Governing the World (Huangji jingshi) begin with four and do nothing other than elucidate this diagram. Both speak in terms of numbers—do they contradict the principle of the Supreme Ultimate? Yet principle and number have never been separate from the beginning; why then did earlier Confucians say that the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate is not as grand as the Prior to Heaven, and the Prior to Heaven is not as refined as the Supreme Ultimate? Moreover, earlier Confucians pointed to the Changes of the Prior to Heaven as the method of the mind, whereas later scholars conversely named that book an investigation of numbers—which of these statements is right and which is wrong? You gentlemen have thoroughly investigated the learning of principle and number and must have achieved a comprehensive understanding of it. We hope you will take Master Zhu's [Zhu Xi 朱熹] debate on the Ultimateless, his explanations of Penetrating the Book of Changes (Tongshu), his commentaries on the Western Inscription and Correcting Youthful Ignorance, and his critical corrections to Supreme Principles Governing the World, and synthesize the discourses of these various masters to show how they all issue from a single standard.

Question: Integrity and modest withdrawal are what scholar-gentlemen esteem. From the Three Dynasties downward, even someone like Ziyun [Yang Xiong 揚雄], a great Confucian of the Han, sought to flatter and curry favor, willingly composing the essay Praising the Xin Dynasty (Meixin); and Changli [Han Yu 韓愈], the mountain and北斗 [towering exemplar] of his generation, as soon as his ambitions were frustrated, went so far as to submit three letters to the Grand Councillors—what then could be expected of the rest? During the flourishing era of the Song dynasty, those above maintained customs through ritual and righteousness, and those below disciplined themselves through integrity and a sense of shame; their heroic spirit and righteous mettle stood in awe-inspiring succession to one another. Thus, one who presented a record for the Jade Hall was not admitted into the Hanlin Academy, and one who presented an ode on the pacification of the Yellow River was not retained in the Orchid Terrace [Historiography Institute / Palace Library]. One who sent no private letters to the capital was promoted to Censor, and one who did not petition the court on private matters was placed in a remonstrance post. Can these men be…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
悉數歟兩及相門俱却以素定一謁大資則却以不求有安
於靜退而彥博薦之不通問訊而温公薦之其人可得
而詳陳歟方登強仕脫然勇退未及掛冠遽爾請老者
謂誰他若十年不求磨勘者有焉十五年退居者亦有
焉以至禮部第一人庭唱抗聲舊例也而不肯自陳進
士第一科求試館職舊制也而不肯召試者可指其人
歟之數子者合乎聖人之中道者誰歟可為後人矜
式者又誰歟千載而下亦有難免士大夫之清議者歟
諸士子為我詳陳之
===
問錢幣之利國益民其來久矣然鑄於歷山莊山小宰聽
稱責以傅別昉於何代歟又有鑄筴之錢八銖之行或
輕而三銖或重而半兩有以一當二以一當三當五十當十
大錢有折二之令當三之請又有造白鹿以為皮幣委
錢以為飛錢與夫交引之制質劑之法其輕重迭勝
當直屢更何者有便於民何者有病於下歟我
朝自國初鑄錢并前代之錢與寶鈔兼行其法甚善行之已
久然懋遷之徒往往樂於用錢而艱於用鈔雖屢禁之
未見其從其故果安在歟伊欲使鈔法流通以便民用
punctuated:
悉數歟？兩及相門，俱却以素定；一謁大資，則却以不求。有安於靜退而彥博薦之，不通問訊而温公薦之，其人可得而詳陳歟？方登強仕，脫然勇退；未及掛冠，遽爾請老者謂誰？他若十年不求磨勘者有焉，十五年退居者亦有焉。以至禮部第一人，庭唱抗聲，舊例也，而不肯自陳；進士第一科，求試館職，舊制也，而不肯召試者，可指其人歟？之數子者，合乎聖人之中道者誰歟？可為後人矜式者又誰歟？千載而下，亦有難免士大夫之清議者歟？諸士子為我詳陳之。
問：錢幣之利國益民，其來久矣。然鑄於歷山、莊山，小宰聽稱責以傅別，昉於何代歟？又有鑄筴之錢，八銖之行，或輕而三銖，或重而半兩。有以一當二、以一當三、當五十、當十大錢，有折二之令、當三之請。又有造白鹿以為皮幣，委錢以為飛錢，與夫交引之制、質劑之法。其輕重迭勝，當直屢更，何者有便於民？何者有病於下歟？我朝自國初鑄錢，并前代之錢與寶鈔兼行，其法甚善，行之已久。然懋遷之徒，往往樂於用錢而艱於用鈔，雖屢禁之，未見其從，其故果安在歟？伊欲使鈔法流通以便民用，
translation_en:
… enumerate them all? There was one who twice approached the gate of the Grand Councilor and refused both times on the grounds that one's fate is predetermined; and one who paid a single call on the Grand Counselor (dazi) and refused to seek advancement. There was one who rested content in quiet retirement and was recommended by Wen Yanbo 文彥博, and one who never sent greetings by letter and was recommended by Sima Guang 司馬光 (Duke Wen 溫公)—can these men be set forth in detail? Who were those who, having just reached the age of forty for vigorous service, resolutely withdrew in retirement, or who, before reaching the age of hanging up one's cap, suddenly begged to retire on account of age? As for others, there was one who for ten years did not seek a performance evaluation (mokan), and there was also one who lived in retirement for fifteen years. Even down to the first-place graduate of the Ministry of Rites—for whom raising his voice to answer at the court roll-call was the old precedent, yet he refused to step forward and declare himself—and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the first tier—for whom requesting to be tested for an Historiography Institute post (guanzhi) was the old system, yet he refused to be summoned for the test—can you point out who these men were? Among these several gentlemen, who conformed to the Mean of the sages? Who again may serve as models to be revered by later generations? And a thousand years later, are there also some among them who can hardly escape the pure criticism (qingyi) of scholar-officials? Gentlemen, set this forth in detail for me.

Question: That coin and currency profit the state and benefit the people is of long standing. Yet casting coins at Mount Li 歷山 and Mount Zhuang 莊山, and the Vice Minister of State (xiaozai) hearing cases of loans by means of tally bonds (fubie)—in what eras did these originate? There were also the casting of elm-pod (jia) coins and the circulation of eight-zhu coins, sometimes lightened to three-zhu and sometimes weighted to half-liang (banliang). There were large coins valued at one for two, one for three, one for fifty, and one for ten; and there were ordinances for two-cash equivalence (zhe'er) and petitions for three-cash equivalence (dangsan). There were also the making of white deerskin into hide currency (pibi), the depositing of cash to create flying cash (feiqian), as well as the system of exchange vouchers (jiaoyin) and the method of deeds of sale (zhiji). As light and heavy currencies alternately prevailed and their face values were repeatedly changed, which of them were convenient for the people, and which were harmful to those below? Since the founding of the state, our Dynasty has cast coins and circulated them alongside coins of former dynasties and Precious Bills (baochao); the method is admirable and has been practiced for a long time. Yet merchants and traders are often happy to use coins and reluctant to use paper notes; although this has been repeatedly prohibited, they are not seen to obey—where indeed does the reason lie? If one wishes to make the paper currency system circulate smoothly so as to be convenient for the people's use, …

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
何道以處之歟請著于篇以觀通濟之學
問兵戎國之大事書言詰爾戎兵張皇六師此制治保邦文
武並用之良法士君子不可以不講也周制三軍周禮六軍
軒轅五行陣風后八陣其後孫子孔明陣勢各八與李靖
之六花十二陣其目可得而悉舉歟將有三等五材五愼
五危三道二急三官三威四機五鼓五教五習五事五法五
間五攻七政四種三術九地其詳可得而備言與我
朝擇將用兵之法超軼前代內而衛國都外而捍疆埸士氣銳而
鎧仗精伊欲盡行師之道如前所陳何陣勢可用於此
===
邊荒遠之地何機策可施於蠻海巖嶮之邦料敵制勝
隨時應機諸士子必有定見願明言之毋諉曰軍旅之事
未之學也
punctuated:
何道以處之歟？請著于篇，以觀通濟之學。

問：兵戎，國之大事。《書》言「詰爾戎兵」、「張皇六師」，此制治保邦、文武並用之良法，士君子不可以不講也。周制三軍，《周禮》六軍，軒轅五行陣，風后八陣，其後孫子、孔明陣勢各八，與李靖之六花、十二陣，其目可得而悉舉歟？將有三等、五材、五愼、五危、三道、二急、三官、三威、四機、五鼓、五教、五習、五事、五法、五間、五攻、七政、四種、三術、九地，其詳可得而備言與？我朝擇將用兵之法，超軼前代，內而衛國都，外而捍疆埸，士氣銳而鎧仗精。伊欲盡行師之道，如前所陳，何陣勢可用於此邊荒遠之地？何機策可施於蠻海巖嶮之邦？料敵制勝，隨時應機，諸士子必有定見。願明言之，毋諉曰「軍旅之事，未之學也」。
translation_en:
…what method should be used to manage it? Please set this forth in your essay, so that we may observe your learning in practical statecraft and relief.

Question: Military affairs are a great matter of the state. The Book of Documents (Shu) speaks of "putting your weapons and armor in order" and "magnifying the Six Armies." This is an excellent method for establishing order and securing the state through the combined use of civil and military means, which scholar-gentlemen cannot fail to study. The Zhou system had Three Armies, and the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) had Six Armies; Xuanyuan [the Yellow Emperor] had the Five Phases Formation, and Fenghou had the Eight Formations; thereafter, Sunzi [Sun Wu] and Kongming [Zhuge Liang] each had eight battle formations, along with Li Jing's Six-Petal and Twelve Formations—can the specific items of these be enumerated in full? Regarding generals and warfare, there are the three grades, five qualities, five cautions, five dangers, three ways, two urgencies, three offices, three awes, four opportunities, five drums, five instructions, five drills, five fundamental factors, five methods, five types of spies, five attacks, seven administrations, four types, three stratagems, and nine terrains—can the details of these be fully explained? Our Dynasty's methods of selecting generals and employing troops surpass those of former eras: internally defending the imperial capital, and externally guarding the frontiers, with high troop morale and fine armor and weapons. If we wish to exhaust the principles of conducting military campaigns as set forth above, which battle formations can be used in these remote frontier lands, and what tactical strategies can be applied in regions of southern non-Chinese peoples, seas, and precipitous defiles? In assessing the enemy to achieve victory and responding to opportunities according to the times, you gentlemen must have settled views. Please state them clearly, and do not excuse yourselves by saying, "As for military affairs, I have not studied them."

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
第十八名許善繼福清縣儒士詩
第十九名鄭紀仙遊縣學增廣生書
第二十名龔鑑福州府學生春秋
第二十一名陳汝珪永福縣學生易
第二十二名周轍興化府增廣生詩
第二十三名劉璋南平縣學生書
第二十四名徐軫福州府學生禮記
第二十五名陳璽福清縣學生詩
第二十六名林秄莆田縣學生書
===

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
四書義
子張問士何如斯可謂之達矣子曰何哉爾所謂達者子張對曰
在邦必聞在家必聞子曰是聞也非達也夫達也者質直而好義
察言而觀色慮以下人在邦必達在家必達夫聞也者色取仁而行
違居之不疑在邦必聞在家必聞
周瑛
考試官學正楊批此題問答頭緒多作者冗泛殊無可觀
惟此作鋪序簡明辭理胥稱必有學之
士宜表而出之
===
考試官教諭聶批此題似易而難作者往往雜襲惟此
篇分別詳明辭不煩而理自到所謂醇
正典雅者置之首選公論攸歸
賢者問士之達聖人詰之以發其意賢者以聞為達聖人辨之而詳其實夫聞
達相似而誠偽不同聖人既因賢者之問而反詰之得不因賢者之對明辨而詳
告之歟思昔子張以堂堂之資有務外之行一旦問於聖人若曰士之為士果何
何如而可謂之達乎子張意在得行於外夫子盖已知其發問之意故反詰之
若曰達之為義非徒得於外而實本諸中爾將以得於外者謂之達乎抑
將以本諸中者謂之達乎於是子張答之以為外而在邦而名譽有以聞于
punctuated:
四書義

子張問：「士何如斯可謂之達矣？」子曰：「何哉，爾所謂達者？」子張對曰：「在邦必聞，在家必聞。」子曰：「是聞也，非達也。夫達也者，質直而好義，察言而觀色，慮以下人。在邦必達，在家必達。夫聞也者，色取仁而行違，居之不疑。在邦必聞，在家必聞。」

周瑛

考試官學正楊批：此題問答頭緒多，作者冗泛，殊無可觀。惟此作鋪序簡明，辭理胥稱，必有學之士，宜表而出之。

考試官教諭聶批：此題似易而難，作者往往雜襲。惟此篇分別詳明，辭不煩而理自到，所謂醇正典雅者。置之首選，公論攸歸。

賢者問士之達，聖人詰之以發其意；賢者以聞為達，聖人辨之而詳其實。夫聞達相似而誠偽不同，聖人既因賢者之問而反詰之，得不因賢者之對明辨而詳告之歟？思昔子張以堂堂之資，有務外之行，一旦問於聖人，若曰：「士之為士，果何何如而可謂之達乎？」子張意在得行於外，夫子盖已知其發問之意，故反詰之，若曰：「達之為義，非徒得於外，而實本諸中。爾將以得於外者謂之達乎？抑將以本諸中者謂之達乎？」於是子張答之，以為外而在邦，而名譽有以聞于
translation_en:
Expositions on the Four Books

Zizhang asked, "What must a gentleman be like before he can be called truly influential (da)?" The Master said, "What do you mean by what you call influential?" Zizhang replied, "Being sure to be renowned in the state, and sure to be renowned in a noble family." The Master said, "That is renown (wen), not influence (da). Now the man of influence is upright in substance and fond of righteousness; he examines people's words and observes their countenances, and is thoughtful in humbling himself before others. In the state he is sure to be influential, and in a noble family he is sure to be influential. As for the man of renown, he assumes the outward appearance of benevolence while his actions violate it, and he rests in this without a doubt. In the state he is sure to be renowned, and in a noble family he is sure to be renowned."

Zhou Ying 周瑛

Comment by Examiner Yang, Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng): This topic has many threads of question and answer, and the writers were wordy anddiffuse, offering nothing worth reading. Only this composition is concise and clear in its exposition, with diction and principle equally well-matched. He must be a scholar of learning, and it is fitting to single him out for distinction.

Comment by Examiner Nie, District Director of Studies (jiaoyu): This topic seems easy yet is difficult, and writers often produced muddled and derivative work. Only this essay draws distinctions clearly and in detail; its words are not prolix, yet its reasoning naturally hits the mark—what may be called pure, orthodox, and refined. Placing him at the head of the list accords with public opinion.

A worthy asks about the influence of a gentleman, and the Sage questions him in return to bring out his meaning; the worthy takes renown to be influence, and the Sage distinguishes between them and explains their reality in detail. Now renown and influence resemble each other, yet their genuineness and falsity are different. Since the Sage already questioned the worthy in return on account of his question, how could he not, on account of the worthy's reply, clearly distinguish between them and instruct him in detail? Consider how in the past Zizhang, with his imposing bearing, had a tendency to strive after externals. One day he asked the Sage, as if to say: "For a gentleman to be a gentleman, just how [note: character 何 repeated in text] must he be before he can be called influential?" Zizhang's mind was set on making his way in the external world. The Master had already perceived the intent behind his question, and therefore questioned him in return, as if to say: "The meaning of influence is not merely attaining success externally, but is in fact rooted within. Do you call that which is attained externally 'influence'? Or do you call that which is rooted within 'influence'?" Thereupon Zizhang answered him, taking it to mean that externally, in the state, one's reputation is such as to be heard of in…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
邦焉內而在家而名譽有以聞於家焉子張以聞為達如是夫子得不明辨
之乎故謂夫爾之所言在邦必聞謂之聞斯可矣夫既明辨之得不詳言之乎故又謂
在家必聞謂之達則非也謂之聞斯可矣夫既明辨之得不詳言之乎故又謂
夫達也者內主忠信而所行合宜審於接物而卑以自牧此皆德脩於己而人信之
故行之於邦而無所窒礙行之於家而無所凝滯豈非達之謂乎至若聞也
者善其顏色以取於仁而行實背之又自以為是而無所忌憚此不務實而
專務求名者故謂著於邦而實德則病於己譽雖隆於家而實行則歉
於心豈非聞之謂歟噫以聞而為達此賢者所以有務外之失辨聞之非達
此聖人所以救賢者之失夫子之言不既深切而著明乎大抵子張之學病在
===
乎不務實夫子告之皆篤實之事充乎內而發乎外者也至於他日問行夫
子告以言忠信行篤敬學干禄夫子又告以言寡悔無非所以救其失也
厥後子張有執德不弘信道不篤焉能為有無之言盖亦有得於夫子教
誨之力歟
使之主祭而百神享之是天受之使之主事而事治百姓安之是民受
之也
許評
考試官學正楊批此題似乎易而措辭實難作者不失
之泛則失之晦惟此篇破承明白講詳實
punctuated:
邦焉，內而在家而名譽有以聞於家焉。」子張以聞為達如是，夫子得不明辨之乎？故謂：「夫爾之所言在邦必聞，謂之聞斯可矣。夫既明辨之，得不詳言之乎？故又謂在家必聞，謂之達則非也，謂之聞斯可矣。」夫既明辨之，得不詳言之乎？故又謂：「夫達也者，內主忠信而所行合宜，審於接物而卑以自牧，此皆德脩於己而人信之，故行之於邦而無所窒礙，行之於家而無所凝滯，豈非達之謂乎？至若聞也者，善其顏色以取於仁，而行實背之，又自以為是而無所忌憚，此不務實而專務求名者。故謂著於邦而實德則病於己，譽雖隆於家而實行則歉於心，豈非聞之謂歟？」噫！以聞而為達，此賢者所以有務外之失；辨聞之非達，此聖人所以救賢者之失。夫子之言，不既深切而著明乎？大抵子張之學，病在乎不務實；夫子告之，皆篤實之事，充乎內而發乎外者也。至於他日問行，夫子告以「言忠信，行篤敬」；學干禄，夫子又告以「言寡悔」，無非所以救其失也。厥後子張有「執德不弘，信道不篤，焉能為有無」之言，盖亦有得於夫子教誨之力歟！

許評
考試官學正楊批：此題似乎易而措辭實難，作者不失之泛則失之晦。惟此篇破承明白，講詳實，
translation_en:
… the state, and internally, when in a noble family, one's reputation makes one renowned in the family." Since Zizhang 子張 mistook renown (wen 聞) for true distinction (da 達) in this manner, how could the Master not clearly distinguish between them? Therefore, he said: "As for what you call inevitably being heard of in the state, [and—text garbled by printer's dittography: 'it may be called renown. Having clearly distinguished it, how could he not speak of it in detail? Therefore he further said:'] inevitably being heard of in the family, to call this distinction is wrong; it may simply be called renown." Having clearly distinguished between them, how could he not explain them in detail? Therefore, he further said: "As for true distinction, inwardly one holds fast to loyalty and trustworthiness while one's actions accord with what is right, and one is attentive in dealing with others while humbling oneself in self-cultivation. In all this, virtue is cultivated within oneself and others trust in it; thus, when practiced in the state there is no obstruction, and when practiced in the family there is no stagnation. Is this not what is meant by distinction? As for renown, one puts on a specious countenance to lay claim to benevolence while one's actions actually contradict it, and moreover considers oneself completely in the right without any misgivings. Such a person does not strive for substance, but exclusively seeks reputation. Therefore, although his name [?] is prominent in the state, his actual virtue is defective within himself; and although his praise is lofty in the family, his actual conduct leaves his heart wanting. Is this not what is meant by renown?" Alas! Mistaking renown for distinction was why the worthy fell into the error of pursuing externalities; distinguishing renown from distinction was how the Sage remedied the worthy's error. Were not the Master's words profoundly incisive and luminously clear? On the whole, the flaw in Zizhang's learning lay in not striving for substance; what the Master taught him were all matters of earnest substance, filled within and manifested without. Later, when he asked about getting one's way in conduct, the Master told him to "be loyal and trustworthy in speech, and earnest and reverent in conduct"; when he studied with a view to official emolument, the Master again told him to "speak so as to rarely have cause for regret"—all of which were meant to remedy his failings. Afterward, Zizhang uttered the words: "If a man holds to virtue without breadth, and believes in the Way without earnestness, how can he be counted as amounting to anything or nothing?" Surely this too was gained from the power of the Master's instruction!

"When he was put in charge of sacrifices, the hundred spirits enjoyed them: this showed that Heaven accepted him. When he was put in charge of affairs, affairs were well ordered and the hundred surnames were at peace with them: this showed that the people accepted him." [Mencius 5A.5]
Xu Ping 許評.
Comment by Examiner and Confucian School Director (xuezheng) Yang 楊: This topic seems easy, yet phrasing it well is actually difficult; writers either err on the side of vagueness or on the side of obscurity. Only this essay has a clear opening and continuation, and an exposition that is detailed and substantial; …

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
置之前列孰曰不宜
考試官教諭聶批此題明白易見而作者不詳上下文意故
多講貫不明惟此篇實而工簡而切盖深
於本領之學者況三場俱優髙薦何忝
聖人祀神而神格治事而民安此可見天人之受也盖主祭而神享主事而民
安此聖人所以為天人所受也大賢即舜之行事以見天示以與之之意至矣且夫天之
為天至公無私未易得其受也今也舜之德足以典乎神天堯則薦之于天而使
之主百神之祭焉舜也達其精明之德以類上帝以禋六宗而上帝六宗莫不
洋洋左右來格而來享致其誠恪之心以望山川以徧群神而山川群神莫不
===
昭昭如在是歆而是承則神無有不享者矣夫神既享其祭則薦之於天
而天受之可知矣至若天下之事萬有不齊未易致其治也今舜之德足以
君臨天下堯則暴之于民而使治天下之事焉舜也于五典則慎徽之于百揆
度之由是五典克從而百揆時叙于四門而賓之于大麓而相之由是四門既穆
而風雨不迷則事又無不治者矣事既治矣民其有不安乎殆見黎民於變相
親相睦於四方風動之時百姓昭明相遜相順於萬國咸寧之日則民亦無有
不安焉夫事治於舜而民安於舜則暴之於民而民受之可見矣吁薦於
天而天受之則舜之有天下也乃天與之而非堯與之矣暴於民而民受之則
舜之有天下也乃人與之而非堯與之矣雖然舜之有天下豈獨堯之薦於
punctuated:
置之前列，孰曰不宜？
考試官教諭聶批：此題明白易見，而作者不詳上下文意，故多講貫不明。惟此篇實而工，簡而切，盖深於本領之學者。況三場俱優，髙薦何忝？
聖人祀神而神格，治事而民安，此可見天人之受也。盖主祭而神享，主事而民安，此聖人所以為天人所受也。大賢即舜之行事，以見天示以與之之意至矣。且夫天之為天，至公無私，未易得其受也。今也舜之德足以典乎神天，堯則薦之于天，而使之主百神之祭焉。舜也達其精明之德，以類上帝，以禋六宗，而上帝、六宗莫不洋洋左右，來格而來享；致其誠恪之心，以望山川，以徧群神，而山川、群神莫不昭昭如在，是歆而是承，則神無有不享者矣。夫神既享其祭，則薦之於天而天受之，可知矣。至若天下之事，萬有不齊，未易致其治也。今舜之德足以君臨天下，堯則暴之于民，而使治天下之事焉。舜也于五典則慎徽之，于百揆度之，由是五典克從而百揆時叙；于四門而賓之，于大麓而相之，由是四門既穆而風雨不迷，則事又無不治者矣。事既治矣，民其有不安乎？殆見黎民於變，相親相睦於四方風動之時；百姓昭明，相遜相順於萬國咸寧之日，則民亦無有不安焉。夫事治於舜而民安於舜，則暴之於民而民受之，可見矣。吁！薦於天而天受之，則舜之有天下也，乃天與之，而非堯與之矣；暴於民而民受之，則舜之有天下也，乃人與之，而非堯與之矣。雖然，舜之有天下，豈獨堯之薦於
translation_en:
… To place it in the front ranks—who would say that is inappropriate?
Examiner and County Director of Studies Nie commented: The meaning of this topic is clear and easy to see, yet writers do not carefully examine the preceding and following context, so their expositions often lack coherence and clarity. Only this essay is substantial and skillful, concise and to the point; indeed, it comes from a scholar profound in fundamental learning. Moreover, since all three sessions of his examination were excellent, how could a high recommendation be undeserved?
When the sage sacrifices to the spirits and the spirits arrive, and when he governs affairs and the people are at peace, by this one can see his acceptance by Heaven and humanity. Indeed, presiding over sacrifices so that the spirits enjoy them, and presiding over affairs so that the people are at peace—this is how the sage comes to be accepted by Heaven and humanity. The great worthy [Mencius] looked to the deeds of Shun to show how thoroughly Heaven manifested its intent to give the empire to him. Moreover, Heaven as Heaven is supremely impartial and selfless; it is not easy to win its acceptance. Now, Shun's virtue was sufficient to take charge of the spirits and Heaven, so Yao presented him to Heaven and had him preside over the sacrifices to the hundred spirits. Shun extended his pure and luminous virtue to perform the special sacrifice (lei) to the Lord on High and the pure sacrifice (yin) to the Six Honored Ones, and neither the Lord on High nor the Six Honored Ones failed to hover majestically to his left and right, coming to arrive and coming to enjoy the offerings; he devoted his sincere and reverent heart to perform the distant sacrifice (wang) to the mountains and rivers and to sacrifice all around to the multitude of spirits, and neither the mountains and rivers nor the multitude of spirits failed to be brightly manifest as if present in person, savoring and receiving the offerings—thus there were no spirits that did not enjoy them. Once the spirits enjoyed his sacrifices, that he was presented to Heaven and Heaven accepted him could be known. As for the affairs of the world, in their myriad varieties and inequalities, it is not easy to bring them to order. Now, Shun's virtue was sufficient to rule over the world as sovereign, so Yao manifested him to the people and had him govern the affairs of the world. With regard to the Five Teachings, Shun cautiously beautified them; with regard to the General百揆 (General百揆, general administration /百揆百官), he measured them, and consequently the Five Teachings were capaz of being followed and the general administration was timely and orderly; at the four gates he received the guests, and at the great foothill forest he assisted in the inspection, and consequently the four gates were harmonious and he did not lose his way amid violent wind and rain—thus there were no affairs that were not well governed. Once affairs were well governed, how could the people not be at peace? One could almost see the black-haired people transforming, loving and living in harmony with one another at a time when the four quarters were moved as by the wind; and the hundred surnames becoming illustrious, yielding and deferring to one another in the days when all the myriad states were at peace—thus among the people, too, there were none who were not at peace. Since affairs were governed through Shun and the people were at peace through Shun, that he was manifested to the people and the people accepted him could be seen. Ah! Presented to Heaven and accepted by Heaven, Shun's possessing the empire was given to him by Heaven, and not given to him by Yao; manifested to the people and accepted by the people, Shun's possessing the empire was given to him by humanity, and not given to him by Yao. Even so, in Shun's possessing the empire, was it merely that Yao presented him to…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
天暴於民而天與民受之而已觀夫避於南河之南而天下諸侯朝覲之畢歸
訟獄謳歌之咸至益以見天命人心不能舎舜而他適焉是則尭固無心於
與舜舜亦豈有心於得天下哉
易義
大觀在上順而巽中正以觀天下觀盥而不薦有孚顒若下觀而化也
李冀
同考試官教諭徐批題本正大平易作者不失之泛則失之
畧此篇析理分明行文醇正宜表出之
考試官學正楊批發明彖傳之義無餘蘊矣初考取允當
===
考試官教諭聶批辭足以貫彖傳之旨義深得乎程朱
之蘊蓋用功於易學者置之高選公論歸焉
脩德位之隆足以示乎下極誠敬之至有以化乎人此聖人體易而為觀也蓋聖
人之為觀必本乎德位之兼隆也自非極誠敬之全又何以致其化於人哉吾夫
子以是釋觀之彖其義精矣今夫觀之為卦二陽在上四陰在下九五一爻
以陽剛之德居至尊之位為觀於上而為下所觀其為觀也大矣故以其德
而言則下坤為順上巽為巽順焉而無所乖戾巽焉而無所拂逆巽而且順
是以立軌範於天下矣五居上卦之中為得中五以陽居陽位為得正中
焉而無過不及正焉而無所偏倚中而又正足以示儀刑于四海矣然聖人
punctuated:
天，暴於民，而天與民受之而已。觀夫避於南河之南，而天下諸侯朝覲之畢歸，訟獄謳歌之咸至，益以見天命人心不能舎舜而他適焉。是則尭固無心於與舜，舜亦豈有心於得天下哉！

易義
大觀在上，順而巽，中正以觀天下。觀，盥而不薦，有孚顒若，下觀而化也。
李冀
同考試官教諭徐批：題本正大平易，作者不失之泛則失之畧。此篇析理分明，行文醇正，宜表出之。
考試官學正楊批：發明彖傳之義，無餘蘊矣。初考取允當。
考試官教諭聶批：辭足以貫彖傳之旨，義深得乎程朱之蘊。蓋用功於易學者，置之高選，公論歸焉。

脩德位之隆，足以示乎下；極誠敬之至，有以化乎人。此聖人體易而為觀也。蓋聖人之為觀，必本乎德位之兼隆也；自非極誠敬之全，又何以致其化於人哉？吾夫子以是釋觀之彖，其義精矣。今夫觀之為卦，二陽在上，四陰在下，九五一爻，以陽剛之德，居至尊之位，為觀於上，而為下所觀，其為觀也大矣。故以其德而言，則下坤為順，上巽為巽。順焉而無所乖戾，巽焉而無所拂逆；巽而且順，是以立軌範於天下矣。五居上卦之中為得中，五以陽居陽位為得正。中焉而無過不及，正焉而無所偏倚；中而又正，足以示儀刑于四海矣。然聖人
translation_en:
… Heaven and presented him to the people, and Heaven and the people accepted him? Observe how, when he withdrew to the south of the Nan River, the feudal lords of the realm going for court audiences all turned to him, and litigants and singers of praise all came to him; this further shows that the Mandate of Heaven and the hearts of the people could not abandon Shun and go elsewhere. Thus Yao indeed had no personal intention of giving the realm to Shun, and how could Shun have had any personal intention of gaining the realm!

Exposition on the Book of Changes (Yijing)
"A great manifestation is above; docile and compliant, central and correct to be a manifestation to the world. 'Contemplation: the ablution has been made, but not yet the offering; there is sincerity and an aspect of solemn dignity'—those below look upon it and are transformed."
Li Ji

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor (jiaoyu): The topic itself is grand, upright, and straightforward; writers either err on the side of vagueness or on the side of brevity. This essay analyzes the principles clearly and its style is pure and orthodox; it deserves to be singled out for praise.
Comment by Examiner Yang, Director of Studies (xuezheng): It elucidates the meaning of the Commentary on the Judgments (Tuanzhuan) without leaving any subtle depth unexplored. The initial selection is entirely fitting.
Comment by Examiner Nie, Instructor (jiaoyu): Its language suffices to thread together the purport of the Commentary on the Judgments, and its meaning deeply grasps the profound teachings of Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi. Clearly this is someone who has devoted serious effort to the study of the Changes; placing him high among the selected candidates accords with impartial public opinion.

Cultivating the eminence of virtue and position suffices to display a model to those below; reaching the utmost of sincerity and reverence provides the means to transform others. This is how the sage embodies the Changes and acts as a manifestation (guan). Indeed, for the sage to act as a manifestation, it must be rooted in the combined eminence of both virtue and position; yet if he does not also reach the perfection of sincerity and reverence, how could he bring about transformation in others? Our Master Confucius explained the Judgment of the hexagram Guan (Contemplation/Manifestation) in these terms, and its meaning is profound indeed. Now, in the hexagram Guan, two yang lines are above and four yin lines are below. The single line of Nine in the Fifth place, with the virtue of yang firmness, occupies the position of supreme honor; it serves as a manifestation above and is looked up to by those below—great indeed is its manifestation! Therefore, speaking in terms of its hexagram virtues, the lower trigram Kun is docility, and the upper trigram Xun is compliance. Being docile, there is nothing perverse; being compliant, there is nothing refractory. Being both compliant and docile, it suffices to establish a standard for the world. The fifth line occupies the center of the upper trigram, which is attaining the mean; the fifth line as a yang line occupies a yang position, which is attaining correctness. Being central, there is neither excess nor deficiency; being correct, there is no partiality or bias. Being both central and correct, it suffices to display an exemplary model to the Four Seas. Yet the sage…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
不以德位兼隆為足尤以誠敬未至為憂故必萃精誠于一心常如始祭而盥
手之時純嚴敬于一念恒若未薦而獻腥之際而吾心之誠足以感人心之誠
將見在下之人盡其孚誠顯然仰聖人之軌範莫不相率而化成焉致其
恪敬竦然瞻聖人之儀刑莫不相觀而興起焉若舜之恭已南面而四方
風動文王之不大聲色而萬邦作孚是已大抵德位者觀示天下之本誠敬
者感化人心之要非德位之隆固無以示於人非誠敬之至又何以化乎人哉
抑觀之為卦上巽下坤而成體文王旣繫其辭吾夫子於此旣以卦體卦
德釋觀名義下觀而化釋卦辭矣至於下文又曰觀天之神道而四時不
忒聖人以神道設教而天下服是又極言為觀之道也吁文王之易有功
===
於伏羲而孔子之易又有功於羲文也歟
初六允升大吉象曰允升大吉上合志也
林迪
同考官教諭徐批本房作此題者固多而明實者少此
篇詞理簡當深得爻象之旨真作手也
考試官學正楊批剖析分明辭理通暢深得周孔二聖之旨
高薦奚忝
考試官教諭聶批此題作者於爻象之旨往往欠明惟此篇
詞簡潔而理精當允如初考宜在選列
punctuated:
不以德位兼隆為足，尤以誠敬未至為憂。故必萃精誠于一心，常如始祭而盥手之時；純嚴敬于一念，恒若未薦而獻腥之際。而吾心之誠，足以感人心之誠。將見在下之人，盡其孚誠，顯然仰聖人之軌範，莫不相率而化成焉；致其恪敬，竦然瞻聖人之儀刑，莫不相觀而興起焉。若舜之恭已南面而四方風動，文王之不大聲色而萬邦作孚，是已。大抵德位者，觀示天下之本；誠敬者，感化人心之要。非德位之隆，固無以示於人；非誠敬之至，又何以化乎人哉？抑觀之為卦，上巽下坤而成體，文王旣繫其辭，吾夫子於此，旣以卦體、卦德釋觀名義，「下觀而化」釋卦辭矣。至於下文，又曰：「觀天之神道，而四時不忒；聖人以神道設教，而天下服。」是又極言為觀之道也。吁！文王之《易》有功於伏羲，而孔子之《易》又有功於羲、文也歟！
「初六：允升，大吉。《象》曰：允升大吉，上合志也。」
林迪
同考官教諭徐批：本房作此題者固多，而明實者少。此篇詞理簡當，深得爻、象之旨，真作手也。
考試官學正楊批：剖析分明，辭理通暢，深得周、孔二聖之旨，高薦奚忝？
考試官教諭聶批：此題作者於爻、象之旨往往欠明，惟此篇詞簡潔而理精當，允如初考，宜在選列。
translation_en:
… does not consider it sufficient merely to possess both exalted virtue and high position, and is especially concerned lest his sincerity and reverence have not reached the utmost. Therefore, he must concentrate pure sincerity in a single mind, always as if at the moment of washing the hands at the beginning of a sacrifice; and he must keep strict reverence pure in a single thought, constantly as if at the time just before offering the raw flesh upon the altar. Then the sincerity of his own mind suffices to move the sincerity of others' minds. One will see that those below exhaust their trusting sincerity, manifestly looking up to the sage's standard, with none failing to follow one another and be transformed into completion; they extend their scrupulous reverence, awe-struck as they gaze upon the sage's model, with none failing to observe one another and be roused to action. Such was Shun holding himself in reverence and facing south while the four quarters were moved as by the wind, or King Wen not making a great display of sound and appearance while all the myriad states were inspired with trust. In general, virtue and position are the foundation for displaying a model to all under heaven, while sincerity and reverence are the essential means for moving and transforming human hearts. Without exalted virtue and position, there is indeed nothing by which to display oneself to others; yet without the utmost sincerity and reverence, how could one transform others? Furthermore, as for the hexagram Guan (Contemplation), its structure is formed with Xun above and Kun below. After King Wen appended his judgment to it, our Master [Confucius] here explained the meaning of the name Guan in terms of the hexagram's structure and virtues, and explained the hexagram judgment with the words "those below observe and are transformed." Coming to the text that follows, he further said: "Contemplating the mysterious way of Heaven, the four seasons do not err; the sage establishes his teachings in accordance with the mysterious way, and all under heaven submit." This is to speak to the utmost of the way of serving as a model for contemplation. Ah! Does not the Classic of Changes (Yi) of King Wen render great service to Fuxi, and the Changes of Confucius in turn render great service to Fuxi and King Wen!

"Initial Six: Advancing upward with confidence, great good fortune. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: 'Advancing upward with confidence, great good fortune'—one's will accords with those above."
By Lin Di 林迪.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Xu 徐: "In my examination ward, those who wrote on this topic were indeed many, yet few were clear and substantive. This essay is concise and apt in both diction and reasoning, deeply grasping the purport of the line statement and the Commentary on the Images. He is truly a master hand!"
Comment by Examiner Director of Studies (xuezheng) Yang 楊: "The analysis is distinct and clear, and the diction and reasoning flow smoothly, deeply grasping the purport of the two sages, the Duke of Zhou and Confucius. How could a high recommendation be undeserved?"
Comment by Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Nie 聶: "Writers on this topic often lacked clarity regarding the purport of the line statement and the Commentary on the Images. Only this essay is concise in diction and precise in reasoning. Confirming the initial evaluation, it deserves to be placed among the selected."

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
陰信陽而上進爻旣著其占之吉象復申其志之同盖陰非從陽不能以
自升也今升之初六旣信從於陽而與之同升則能升而復獲吉矣爻象
聖人得不著其占之吉于前而申其志之同于後哉且夫升之初六居巽之
下上無應援當升之時柔不能以自升故信於九二之陽而九二亦信之以
同升焉處下卦之初弱不能以自進惟從於九二之剛而九二亦允之以偕
進焉升不徒升升則遂夫揚于王庭之願矣非若姤之繫于金柅也吉
孰大焉進不徒進進則遂夫共惟帝臣之心矣非若屯之乘馬班如也
善孰過焉夫周公係爻著占其義如此吾夫子於小象復申言之以為
初六之所以允升而大吉者由其與上合志也上謂九二合志者志无不同
===
也上有南征之心初六亦有南征之心上與初六位雖有高下之殊而
其心則相與昭合而無間二有作賓之志初六亦有作賓之志初六與二質
雖有剛柔之異而其志則相與交孚而為一聲應氣求初之心即上之心
鶴鳴子和二之志即初之志夫如是則其獲乎大吉也宜哉抑論上坤下
巽伏羲名升之卦也元亨用見大人勿恤南征吉文王彖升之辭也至於
初六周公則以允升大吉著其爻孔子復以上合志也由其象無非發明卦
爻所以為升之義也吁羲文周孔同此心也畫卦繫辭同此理也孰
謂文王之易非伏羲之易而周孔之易非羲文之易也歟
書義
punctuated:
陰信陽而上進，爻旣著其占之吉，象復申其志之同。盖陰非從陽，不能以自升也。今《升》之初六，旣信從於陽，而與之同升，則能升而復獲吉矣。爻、象聖人得不著其占之吉于前，而申其志之同于後哉？且夫《升》之初六，居巽之下，上無應援，當升之時，柔不能以自升，故信於九二之陽，而九二亦信之以同升焉；處下卦之初，弱不能以自進，惟從於九二之剛，而九二亦允之以偕進焉。升不徒升，升則遂夫揚于王庭之願矣，非若《姤》之「繫于金柅」也，吉孰大焉！進不徒進，進則遂夫共惟帝臣之心矣，非若《屯》之「乘馬班如」也，善孰過焉！夫周公係爻著占，其義如此。吾夫子於《小象》復申言之，以為初六之所以「允升」而「大吉」者，由其與「上合志」也。上，謂九二；合志者，志无不同也。上有「南征」之心，初六亦有「南征」之心，上與初六，位雖有高下之殊，而其心則相與昭合而無間；二有「作賓」之志，初六亦有「作賓」之志，初六與二，質雖有剛柔之異，而其志則相與交孚而為一。聲應氣求，初之心即上之心；鶴鳴子和，二之志即初之志。夫如是，則其獲乎「大吉」也宜哉！抑論上坤下巽，伏羲名《升》之卦也；「元亨，用見大人，勿恤，南征吉」，文王彖《升》之辭也。至於初六，周公則以「允升，大吉」著其爻，孔子復以「上合志也」由其象，無非發明卦爻所以為《升》之義也。吁！羲、文、周、孔同此心也，畫卦、繫辭同此理也。孰謂文王之《易》非伏羲之《易》，而周、孔之《易》非羲、文之《易》也歟！

書義
translation_en:
When the yin line trusts in the yang lines and advances upward, the line statement first sets forth the auspiciousness of its prognostication, and the Commentary on the Images (Xiang) further explains the unity of their aspirations. For unless yin follows yang, it cannot ascend by itself. Now, since the First Six of the Sheng ("Pushing Upward") hexagram trusts in and follows the yang lines and ascends together with them, it is able to ascend and moreover obtains good fortune. How could the sages who composed the line statements and the Commentary on the Images not make clear the auspiciousness of its prognostication beforehand, and further explain the unity of their aspirations afterward?

Moreover, the First Six of Sheng dwells at the bottom of the Xun trigram and has no corresponding line above to assist it. At the time of ascending, being yielding, it cannot ascend on its own; therefore it places its trust in the yang of the Second Nine, and the Second Nine likewise trusts it so that they ascend together. Occupying the beginning of the lower trigram, being weak, it cannot advance on its own; it simply follows the firmness of the Second Nine, and the Second Nine likewise consents to advance together with it. Its ascending is not a mere ascending: by ascending, it fulfills the wish of "making proclamation in the king's court," unlike the First Six of Gou ("Encountering") which is "tied to a metal brake"—what good fortune could be greater than this! Its advancing is not a mere advancing: by advancing, it fulfills the aspiration of serving together as the sovereign's ministers, unlike the lines of Zhun ("Difficulty at the Beginning") with their "mounted horses hesitating to go forward"—what goodness could surpass this!

Such is the meaning of the Duke of Zhou's appending the line statement to reveal the prognostication. Our Master Confucius in the Commentary on the Lesser Images (Xiaoxiang) further elaborated on it, holding that the reason the First Six "pushes upward with confidence" and has "great good fortune" is that it "shares the aspiration of those above." "Those above" refers to the Second Nine; "sharing the aspiration" means that their aspirations are in no way different. The line above has the intention of "going forward to the south," and the First Six also has the intention of "going forward to the south." Although the line above and the First Six differ in high and low position, their minds are in bright harmony without any gap. The Second line has the aspiration to "be the guest of the king," and the First Six also has the aspiration to "be the guest of the king." Although the First Six and the Second line differ in firm and yielding nature, their aspirations are in mutual trust and become one. Like sound echoing and vital breath seeking its kind, the mind of the First line is the mind of the line above; like the crane calling and its young answering, the aspiration of the Second line is the aspiration of the First line. Being thus, is it not fitting that it obtains "great good fortune"!

Furthermore, let us consider that Kun above and Xun below is the hexagram that Fuxi named Sheng; "Supreme success; it is fitting to see the great man; do not worry; going forward to the south brings good fortune" is the Judgment (Tuan) that King Wen wrote for Sheng. Coming to the First Six, the Duke of Zhou revealed its line with the words "Pushing upward with confidence, great good fortune," and Confucius in turn deduced [reading 申 for 由?] its Image with the words "It shares the aspiration of those above"—all of which serve nothing other than to elucidate the meaning of why the hexagram and its lines constitute Sheng. Ah! Fuxi, King Wen, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius shared this same mind; drawing the hexagrams and appending the statements shared this same principle. Who would say that the Changes (Yi) of King Wen is not the Changes of Fuxi, or that the Changes of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius is not the Changes of Fuxi and King Wen?

Essays on the Book of Documents (Shu yi)

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
先王惟時懋敬厥德克配上帝今王嗣有令緒尚監茲哉若升高必
自下若陟遐必自邇無輕民事惟難無安厥位惟危慎終于
始有言逆于汝心必求諸道有言遜于汝志必求諸非道嗚呼
弗慮胡獲弗為胡成一人元良萬邦以貞
許評
同考試官教諭鮑批此題伊尹之告君忠愛懇切所以戒
勉之不足復嗟嘆以期望之諸篇即其言
而沒其意者多矣惟此簡而切文而實宜冠本經
考試官學正楊批此題伊尹戒勉其君累言不足非作者不
===
能盡之惟此篇破承簡切講貫詳明則大
臣忠藎之意宛如也允宜高薦
考試官教諭聶批此題作者多矣然破或不能包括講或
失之疎略此篇分截明講貫備可以想見
當時老臣告君之意宜在選列
聖德盛而後王之取法者有其序情之偏而後王之當矯者非一端故必盡
知行之功而致大善之效也夫先王之德固後王所當法也大臣旣喻以進德
有序而矯乎情之偏又安得不勉以知行兼盡而致大善之效哉在昔伊尹
之告太甲若曰德者人所同得而昧焉者衆惟先王成湯顧諟明命而
punctuated:
先王惟時懋敬厥德，克配上帝。今王嗣有令緒，尚監茲哉！若升高，必自下；若陟遐，必自邇。無輕民事惟難，無安厥位惟危。慎終于始。有言逆于汝心，必求諸道；有言遜于汝志，必求諸非道。嗚呼！弗慮胡獲？弗為胡成？一人元良，萬邦以貞。

許評
同考試官教諭鮑批：此題伊尹之告君，忠愛懇切，所以戒勉之不足，復嗟嘆以期望之。諸篇即其言而沒其意者多矣，惟此簡而切、文而實，宜冠本經。
考試官學正楊批：此題伊尹戒勉其君，累言不足，非作者不能盡之。惟此篇破承簡切，講貫詳明，則大臣忠藎之意宛如也，允宜高薦。
考試官教諭聶批：此題作者多矣，然破或不能包括，講或失之疎略。此篇分截明，講貫備，可以想見當時老臣告君之意，宜在選列。

聖德盛而後王之取法者有其序，情之偏而後王之當矯者非一端，故必盡知行之功而致大善之效也。夫先王之德，固後王所當法也；大臣旣喻以進德有序，而矯乎情之偏，又安得不勉以知行兼盡，而致大善之效哉！在昔伊尹之告太甲，若曰：德者，人所同得，而昧焉者衆。惟先王成湯，顧諟明命而
translation_en:
"The Former King therefore strove to revere his virtue, and so was able to be a counterpart to High Heaven. Now, Your Majesty has succeeded to this fine heritage; may you take this as your mirror! It is like ascending to a height, which must begin from below; it is like travelling to a distant place, which must begin from what is near. Do not slight the affairs of the people—think only of their difficulty; do not rest at ease in your position—think only of its peril. Be careful of the end at the beginning. When words go against your heart, you must seek whether they conform to the Way; when words flatter your will, you must seek whether they depart from the Way. Oh! Without thought, how can anything be gained? Without action, how can anything be achieved? When the One Man is supremely good, the myriad states are thereby rectified."

Xu Ping
Associate Examiner and Instructor Bao comments: In this passage, Yi Yin's counsel to his ruler is loyal, affectionate, and earnestly sincere; finding his admonitions and encouragements insufficient, he further sighs in exclamation to express his hopes for him. Many of the other essays follow his words while losing sight of his deeper intent; this one alone is concise yet incisive, refined yet substantial, and deserves to stand first in this Classic.
Examiner and Director of Studies Yang comments: On this topic, where Yi Yin admonishes and encourages his ruler with repeated words that still feel insufficient, none but a true master of composition could fully bring out its meaning. Only this essay has an opening and continuation that are concise and to the point, and an exposition that is thorough and clear, making the loyal devotion of the great minister vividly present; it truly deserves a high recommendation.
Examiner and Instructor Nie comments: Many candidates wrote on this topic, yet their openings sometimes failed to encompass the whole passage, and their expositions sometimes erred on the side of sketchiness. This essay divides the sections clearly and expounds the meaning completely, allowing one to envision the intent of the veteran minister counseling his ruler at the time; it deserves to be placed among the selected essays.

Because the sage's virtue was flourishing, there is a proper sequence by which a later king takes him as a model; because human inclinations are partial, there is more than one aspect in which a later king must correct himself; therefore, he must exhaust the effort of both knowledge and action in order to bring about the effect of supreme goodness. Now, the virtue of the Former King is assuredly what a later king ought to take as his model. Once the great minister has illustrated that advancing in virtue has its sequence and that partiality of inclination must be corrected, how could he not also urge him to exhaust both knowledge and action so as to achieve the effect of supreme goodness? In antiquity, when Yi Yin counseled Tai Jia, it was as if he said: Virtue is what all men alike obtain, yet those who are darkened with respect to it are many. Only our Former King, Tang the Successful, kept his eyes ever upon the bright mandate of Heaven, and…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
懋德之功為不息昧爽丕顯而敬德之心為無間夫先王懋敬其德如此是
故彼蒼者天而其德則與之合焉皇矣上帝而其德則與之配焉今王嗣
先王之令緒庶幾不愆不忘而監其懋德可也紹先王之大業必是儀是
式而法其敬德可也然觀法先王非一蹴所能至譬如人之陟遐其初必自
乎下苟不自下其何以升乎高哉譬如人之陟遐其初必自乎迩苟不自
迩其何以行乎遠哉夫進德之喻既告矣而又謂彼民事者王政所係無
以為輕而當思其難焉君位者萬幾所關無以為安而當思其危焉
人情孰不欲善終乎然始之不謹而能善其終者寡矣故圖終守
成之道必謹於即政臨民之初焉至若鯁直之言人所難受汝則必求
===
諸道不可以逆心而拒之巽順之言人所易從汝則必求諸非道不可
以遜志而聽之夫矯情之偏既陳矣而其意猶未已焉於是發之聲
嗟形諸氣嘆蓋謂進德之序矯情之偏不謹思之則心與理不相涵
何所得乎不篤行之則身與事不相安何所成乎誠能思之謹而行
之篤則仁極其仁而天下之仁無以加義極其義而天下之義無以尚則
一人元良也為何如將見君仁莫不仁而庶邦悉歸於正君義莫不義而
天下咸由於善則萬邦以貞也又何似噫伊尹欲太甲之法祖既喻而
戒之於先復勉而期之於後何其忠愛之至歟抑考伊尹作太甲三
篇上篇作於太甲有過之時不欲激之而微轉其機故其辭婉中篇
punctuated: 懋德之功為不息，昧爽丕顯而敬德之心為無間。夫先王懋敬其德如此，是故彼蒼者天，而其德則與之合焉；皇矣上帝，而其德則與之配焉。今王嗣先王之令緒，庶幾不愆不忘，而監其懋德可也；紹先王之大業，必是儀是式，而法其敬德可也。然觀法先王，非一蹴所能至。譬如人之陟遐，其初必自乎下，苟不自下，其何以升乎高哉？譬如人之陟遐，其初必自乎迩，苟不自迩，其何以行乎遠哉？夫進德之喻既告矣，而又謂彼民事者，王政所係，無以為輕而當思其難焉；君位者，萬幾所關，無以為安而當思其危焉。人情孰不欲善終乎？然始之不謹，而能善其終者寡矣，故圖終守成之道，必謹於即政臨民之初焉。至若鯁直之言，人所難受，汝則必求諸道，不可以逆心而拒之；巽順之言，人所易從，汝則必求諸非道，不可以遜志而聽之。夫矯情之偏既陳矣，而其意猶未已焉，於是發之聲嗟，形諸氣嘆，蓋謂進德之序、矯情之偏，不謹思之，則心與理不相涵，何所得乎？不篤行之，則身與事不相安，何所成乎？誠能思之謹而行之篤，則仁極其仁，而天下之仁無以加；義極其義，而天下之義無以尚，則「一人元良」也為何如？將見君仁莫不仁，而庶邦悉歸於正；君義莫不義，而天下咸由於善，則「萬邦以貞」也又何似？噫！伊尹欲太甲之法祖，既喻而戒之於先，復勉而期之於後，何其忠愛之至歟！抑考伊尹作《太甲》三篇：上篇作於太甲有過之時，不欲激之而微轉其機，故其辭婉；中篇
translation_en: …his effort in striving after virtue was unceasing; in the pre-dawn twilight he was greatly manifest, and his mind of revering virtue knew no interruption. Now, the Former King strove after and revered his virtue in such a manner; therefore, as for the azure Heaven, his virtue was in harmony with it; as for the august Lord on High, his virtue was a match for Him. Now that the King succeeds to the fine heritage of the Former King, may he neither err nor forget, and take the Former King's striving after virtue as his mirror; in continuing the great enterprise of the Former King, he must take him as model and pattern, and emulate his reverence for virtue. Yet observing and emulating the Former King is not something that can be reached at a single bound. It is like a person ascending to a distant height: at the beginning he must start from what is low; if he does not start from what is low, how can he rise to what is high? It is like a person ascending to a distant height [sic, traveling afar]: at the beginning he must start from what is near; if he does not start from what is near, how can he travel to what is far? Having already imparted the metaphor for advancing in virtue, he further said that the affairs of the people are what kingly governance depends upon—do not regard them as light, but reflect upon their difficulty; the ruler's position is what the myriad affairs hinge upon—do not regard it as secure, but reflect upon its peril. In human sentiment, who does not wish to have a good end? Yet those who are not careful at the beginning and still manage to bring about a good end are few; therefore, the way of planning for the end and preserving the achievement must be attended to with caution at the very outset of assuming governance and facing the people. As for blunt and upright words, which are hard for people to accept, you must seek their basis in the Way and must not reject them because they go against your mind; as for compliant and flattering words, which are easy for people to follow, you must examine how they depart from the Way and must not listen to them because they defer to your will. Having thus set forth the correction of biased inclinations, his meaning was still not exhausted; thereupon he gave voice to sighs and expressed it in lamentation. For he meant that regarding the sequence of advancing in virtue and the correction of biased inclinations, if one does not reflect upon them carefully, the mind and principle will not imbue each other—what then will be gained? If one does not practice them earnestly, the person and the affair will not rest securely with each other—what then will be accomplished? If indeed one can reflect carefully and practice earnestly, then benevolence will reach the utmost of benevolence and nothing in the world will surpass it in benevolence, and righteousness will reach the utmost of righteousness and nothing in the world will exceed it in righteousness—how great then will be the "supreme goodness of the One Man"! One will then see that when the ruler is benevolent, none will not be benevolent, and the numerous states will all return to rectitude; when the ruler is righteous, none will not be righteous, and all under Heaven will follow goodness—what then will "the myriad states being rectified" be like! Alas! Yi Yin wished Tai Jia to emulate his ancestor; having first enlightened and admonished him, he again exhorted and placed his hopes in him afterward—how supreme was his loyalty and devotion! Moreover, if we examine the three chapters of Tai Jia composed by Yi Yin: the first chapter was written when Tai Jia was in error, and since Yi Yin did not wish to provoke him but rather to subtly turn his tendencies, its words are gentle; the middle chapter…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
作於悔過之初深自喜慰故其辭温此篇作於改過之後慮其或不克終
故其辭深以厲可謂善於告君者矣厥後太甲克終厥德非伊尹訓
迪之力而疇歟
王厥有成命治民今休
許評
同考試官教諭鮑批題意雖平易而講貫潔要者鮮此
篇理有發明詞無冗泛非熟於經者不
能也
考試官學正楊批辭達意周發明期望宅洛之效殆無
===
餘蘊誠佳作也
考試官教諭聶批書經二百餘卷作者固多此篇尤簡
潔有理誠銕中之錚錚者
天命固於上治化美於下此大臣期君治洛之效也盖洛邑之作繫於天
人大矣人君能紹上帝服土中則天命之固治化之美有不期而然者矣
召公舉周公之言以告成王其意不既深乎且夫洛為天地之中人君所
以凝天命者在是今王而宅天下之中紹上帝之治將見天監厥德用
集大命保佑命之自天中之眷顧之已隆者愈隆而弗替付托之已重
者益重而無窮鞏基圖于於萬斯年之永者豈基圖之永乎寔天
punctuated:
作於悔過之初，深自喜慰，故其辭温；此篇作於改過之後，慮其或不克終，故其辭深以厲，可謂善於告君者矣。厥後太甲克終厥德，非伊尹訓迪之力而疇歟？
王厥有成命，治民今休。
許評。
同考試官教諭鮑批：題意雖平易，而講貫潔要者鮮。此篇理有發明，詞無冗泛，非熟於經者不能也。
考試官學正楊批：辭達意周，發明期望宅洛之效，殆無餘蘊，誠佳作也。
考試官教諭聶批：書經二百餘卷，作者固多，此篇尤簡潔有理，誠銕中之錚錚者。
天命固於上，治化美於下，此大臣期君治洛之效也。盖洛邑之作，繫於天人大矣。人君能紹上帝、服土中，則天命之固、治化之美，有不期而然者矣。召公舉周公之言以告成王，其意不既深乎？且夫洛為天地之中，人君所以凝天命者在是。今王而宅天下之中，紹上帝之治，將見天監厥德，用集大命，保佑命之，自天中之。眷顧之已隆者愈隆而弗替，付托之已重者益重而無窮。鞏基圖于於萬斯年之永者，豈基圖之永乎？寔天
translation_en:
…was composed at the beginning of his repentance, when Yi Yin felt deep joy and relief, and thus its words are warm; this section was composed after he had reformed his faults, out of concern that he might not carry his virtue through to the end, and thus its words are profound and stern. He may truly be called one skilled in counseling his ruler! That Taijia was subsequently able to maintain his virtue to the end—to whom else was it owing if not to the power of Yi Yin's instruction and guidance?

"The king shall have a settled mandate, and in governing the people there will now be auspicious peace." [Book of Documents, "Announcement of Shao" (Shao gao)]
By Xu Ping 許評.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Bao 鮑 comments: Although the meaning of the topic is plain and straightforward, few are able to explicate it concisely and to the point. This essay brings clarity to the principles and contains no verbose or superficial phrasing; none could have written it who was not thoroughly versed in the Classic.
Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor Yang 楊 comments: The diction is expressive and the meaning comprehensive. In elucidating the anticipated effects of taking up residence in Luo, it leaves almost nothing unexplored; it is truly a fine piece of work.
Examiner, Instructor Nie 聶 comments: Among more than two hundred papers on the Book of Documents (Shujing), there are certainly many capable writers, yet this essay is especially concise and well-reasoned—truly the finest clanging metal among iron.

When the Mandate of Heaven is secured above, governance and moral transformation flourish in beauty below—such is the effect a great minister anticipates from his ruler governing from Luo. For the building of the city of Luo was of immense consequence to both Heaven and man. If a ruler can succeed to the work of the Lord on High and govern from the center of the land, then the security of the Mandate of Heaven and the beauty of governance and moral transformation will come about as a matter of course. When the Duke of Shao cited the words of the Duke of Zhou to counsel King Cheng, was his intention not profound indeed? Moreover, Luo is at the center of Heaven and Earth, and it is here that the ruler consolidates the Mandate of Heaven. Now, if the king takes up his dwelling at the center of All under Heaven and continues the governance of the Lord on High, one will see Heaven look down upon his virtue and thereby bring together the great Mandate, protecting, aiding, and ordaining him, renewing [reading 中 for 申?] it from Heaven. The favor that is already abundant will grow ever more abundant without ceasing; the charge that is already weighty will grow ever weightier without end. Consolidating the dynastic foundation for the perpetuity of ten thousand years—is this merely the perpetuity of the foundation? In truth, it is the perpetuity of Heaven's…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
命之永一成而不變耳奠國祚於萬有千歲之久者豈國祚之久歟實
帝命之久一定而不易耳王者之有天成命如此何莫非紹上帝之所致
乎洛為四方都會之所人君所以固人心者於是今王中天下而立定四海
之民殆見禮樂教化之昭明有以措斯世於平康綱紀文章之宣布有
以致篤萬方之化服父子兄弟各止其所而黎民有於変之休所謂五
品不遜者無有也農工商賈各安其業而下民有祗叶之美所謂一夫不獲
者無有也王者治民今休如此何莫而非服土中之所致歟抑考洛邑既
成成王始政召公因周公之歸作書以告成王上文既以紹上帝服土中為言
而此又舉周公之語以告之以見作洛所以配上帝奉祭祀凝天命成治功
===
其重如此蓋下文將自進其敬德祈天之言必先引周公之語以啟其端
也召公之忠愛何其至歟
詩義
申伯信邁王餞于郿申伯還南謝于誠歸王命召伯徹申伯土疆以
峙其粻式遄其行
周瑛
同考試官教諭羅批詩經近三百卷作者多為此題所窘
惟此篇寫出宣王愛舅之情言用贈言
之美正合題意而且文辭豐潤誠所舂葩
punctuated:
命之永，一成而不變耳；奠國祚於萬有千歲之久者，豈國祚之久歟？實帝命之久，一定而不易耳。王者之有天成命如此，何莫非紹上帝之所致乎？洛為四方都會之所，人君所以固人心者於是。今王中天下而立，定四海之民，殆見禮樂教化之昭明，有以措斯世於平康；綱紀文章之宣布，有以致篤萬方之化服。父子兄弟，各止其所，而黎民有「於変」之休，所謂「五品不遜」者無有也；農工商賈，各安其業，而下民有祗叶之美，所謂「一夫不獲」者無有也。王者治民今休如此，何莫而非服土中之所致歟？抑考洛邑既成，成王始政，召公因周公之歸，作書以告成王。上文既以「紹上帝、服土中」為言，而此又舉周公之語以告之，以見作洛所以配上帝、奉祭祀、凝天命、成治功，其重如此。蓋下文將自進其敬德祈天之言，必先引周公之語以啟其端也。召公之忠愛，何其至歟！

詩義
「申伯信邁，王餞于郿。申伯還南，謝于誠歸。王命召伯，徹申伯土疆，以峙其粻，式遄其行。」
周瑛
同考試官教諭羅批：《詩經》近三百卷，作者多為此題所窘。惟此篇寫出宣王愛舅之情，言用贈言之美，正合題意，而且文辭豐潤，誠所舂葩
translation_en:
…[Heaven's] mandate being everlasting, once established and never changing; and to settle the dynastic fortune for ten thousand and a thousand years—is it merely the longevity of the dynastic fortune? In truth, it is the longevity of the Sovereign on High's mandate, once fixed and never altered! That the true king possesses Heaven's settled mandate in such a way—how could any of this not be brought about by continuing the work of the Sovereign on High? Luo is the metropolis where the four quarters converge, and it is here that the ruler secures the hearts of the people. Now, when the King stands at the center of the realm and settles the people within the four seas, one shall surely see the brilliant manifestation of rites, music, instruction, and transformation, wherewith this world is placed in peace and tranquility; and the promulgation of moral norms, institutions, and cultural forms, wherewith the myriad regions are brought to sincere transformation and submission. Fathers, sons, elder brothers, and younger brothers each rest in their proper place, and the black-haired people enjoy the blessing of "Oh! how they are transformed," so that what is called "the five categories of relationships being unharmonious" does not exist; farmers, artisans, and merchants each rest content in their occupations, and the common people possess the virtue of reverent harmony, so that what is called "a single man failing to find his place" does not exist. That the true king's governance of the people achieves such present blessings—how could any of this not be brought about by governing from the center of the land? Moreover, if we examine the matter, after the city of Luo was completed and King Cheng began his personal rule, the Duke of Shao took the occasion of the Duke of Zhou's return to compose this document to counsel King Cheng. Above, he had already spoken of "continuing the work of the Sovereign on High and governing from the center of the land," and here he again cites the words of the Duke of Zhou to instruct him, so as to show that the building of Luo was the means to serve as counterpart to the Sovereign on High, offer sacrifices, consolidate Heaven's mandate, and accomplish the work of governance—so great was its importance. For in the text below he was about to advance his own words on revering virtue and praying to Heaven, and thus he had first to cite the words of the Duke of Zhou to open the way. How supreme indeed was the loyal affection of the Duke of Shao!

Expositions on the Classic of Odes (Shijing)
"The Earl of Shen truly set forth; the King gave him a farewell feast at Mei. The Earl of Shen turned south, and to Xie he truly went home. The King commanded the Earl of Shao to tithe the Earl of Shen's lands and borders, so as to store up his dry provisions, and thus speed his journey."
Zhou Ying 周瑛
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Luo: Among the nearly three hundred examination papers on the Classic of Odes, most writers were stymied by this topic. Only this essay captures King Xuan's affection for his maternal uncle and expresses the beauty of presenting parting words [?], which accords precisely with the meaning of the topic. Moreover, its diction is rich and lustrous; truly it is what [is called] spring blossoms [?]…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
滿林者也宜冠本經
考試官學正楊批吟咏性情作者鮮得惟此篇簡而明
文而實形容詩人詠賢君待臣之意宛然
在目盖深得葩經之㫖者也
考試官教諭聶批此題作者多於信邁誠歸処失其本
㫖惟此篇辭㫖有法文采燁然讀之倡三嘆
觀王者因親臣之歸國旣致餞而有以果其行當觀王者命大臣之治土
復致備而有以速其行盖王者於親臣之出封不惟致餞而欲其行之果而
又致備以資其行之速則其待親臣之厚為何如哉昔者申伯出封于
===
謝尹吉甫作詩送之謂夫申伯為王之元舅析圭儋爵非一日而未得果
於行也膏車秣馬非一朝而未得遂其往也今也申伯信為邁矣王在
岐周可不往餞于郿而送之乎吾知肆筵設席而禮意之甚隆路車乘
黃而贈賄之甚厚其致餞也為何如王者旣致餞矣則伯申之行豈有不
果者乎吾知四牡業業而載馳載驅於南方之道徒御嘽嘽而將翔於謝
邑之郊向也行有未果今則信於行矣向也歸有未遂今則誠於歸矣然
使道路儲蓄之不備又豈無淹留之患哉故王命召伯不徒命也于以徹
申伯之土而使土地之適均于以徹申伯之疆而俾疆界之是正將見什一之征
有以充道路之委積賦稅之入有以峙廬市之餼糧夫然後今日之五
punctuated:
滿林者也。宜冠本經。
考試官學正楊批：吟咏性情，作者鮮得。惟此篇簡而明，文而實，形容詩人詠賢君待臣之意，宛然在目，盖深得《葩經》之㫖者也。
考試官教諭聶批：此題作者多於「信邁」、「誠歸」処失其本㫖。惟此篇辭㫖有法，文采燁然，讀之倡三嘆。
觀王者因親臣之歸國，旣致餞而有以果其行；當觀王者命大臣之治土，復致備而有以速其行。盖王者於親臣之出封，不惟致餞而欲其行之果，而又致備以資其行之速，則其待親臣之厚為何如哉！昔者申伯出封于謝，尹吉甫作詩送之。謂夫申伯為王之元舅，析圭儋爵非一日，而未得果於行也；膏車秣馬非一朝，而未得遂其往也。今也申伯信為邁矣，王在岐周，可不往餞于郿而送之乎？吾知肆筵設席而禮意之甚隆，路車乘黃而贈賄之甚厚，其致餞也為何如！王者旣致餞矣，則伯申之行豈有不果者乎？吾知四牡業業，而載馳載驅於南方之道；徒御嘽嘽，而將翔於謝邑之郊。向也行有未果，今則信於行矣；向也歸有未遂，今則誠於歸矣。然使道路儲蓄之不備，又豈無淹留之患哉？故王命召伯，不徒命也，于以徹申伯之土，而使土地之適均；于以徹申伯之疆，而俾疆界之是正。將見什一之征，有以充道路之委積；賦稅之入，有以峙廬市之餼糧。夫然後今日之五
translation_en:
…[spring blossoms?] filling the forest. It ought to top the essays on this Classic.

Comment by Examiner Yang, Subprefectural/Departmental Director of Studies: In chanting of human nature and emotion, examinees rarely grasp the essence. Only this essay is concise yet clear, refined yet substantive. It depicts the poet's intent in singing of how a worthy ruler treats his minister so vividly that it seems right before one's eyes; indeed, the author has deeply grasped the purport of the Classic of Odes.

Comment by Examiner Nie, County Director of Studies: On this topic, most examinees missed the original purport at the phrases "truly setting forth" and "sincerely returning." Only this essay is methodical in its diction and purport, and resplendent in its literary brilliance; reading it leads one to intone it with repeated sighs of admiration.

When we observe how the true king, upon his kinsman-minister's return to his state, held a farewell banquet and thereby brought his departure to fruition, we ought also to observe how the true king commanded a grand minister to regulate the lands, further making provisions and thereby hastening his journey. Indeed, when a kinsman-minister went out to his fief, the true king not only held a farewell banquet desiring that his departure be resolute, but also made provisions to aid the speed of his journey—how generous, then, was his treatment of his kinsman-minister!

In antiquity, when the Earl of Shen went out to be enfeoffed at Xie, Yin Jifu composed an ode to see him off. He meant to say that the Earl of Shen, as the King's eldest maternal uncle, had been granted his jade tablet and had borne his noble rank for more than a single day, yet had not been able to carry out his departure; he had greased his carriage wheels and fed his horses grain for more than a single morning, yet had not been able to fulfill his journey. Now, the Earl of Shen was truly setting forth; since the King was at Qizhou, how could he not go to give him a farewell banquet at Mei and see him off? We know that mats and seats were spread out with the utmost ceremonial courtesy, and a state carriage and team of bays were presented as most generous parting gifts—how grand was that farewell banquet!

Once the true king had held the farewell banquet, how could the departure of the Earl of Shen [sic: text inverts characters as Bo Shen] not be carried through? We know that his four steeds were strong and imposing, galloping and driving along the southern road, and his footmen and charioteers were numerous and at ease, about to soar into the outskirts of the city of Xie. Previously, his departure had not been carried through, but now he was truly on his way; previously, his return to his fief had not been fulfilled, but now he was sincerely returning.

Yet if the stores and provisions along the road had not been prepared, how could there not have been the trouble of delay along the way? Therefore, when the King gave his command to the Earl of Shao, it was no empty command: by it he taxed the Earl of Shen's lands on the mutual-aid system so as to make the land allotments evenly balanced, and by it he laid out the Earl of Shen's boundaries so as to make the borders properly rectified. Thus one would see the one-tenth levy suffice to fill the stores accumulated along the roads, and the revenue from land taxes suffice to lay up grain provisions at the roadside lodges and markets. Only after this could today's fifty…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
十里而今日之行無所留明日之五十里而明日之行無所滯其行之速
為何如哉宣王之待元舅其恩意之周浹綜理之微密如此詩人形諸咏
歌不亦宜乎抑考申伯之於周其生也有所自其出也有所為觀其所謂
維嶽降神生甫及申則申伯之生旣鍾嶽神之秀矣所謂四國于蕃四
方于宣則申伯之出又足以為王國之翰矣宣王得大臣之賢而致中興
之盛豈不於斯而可見乎
庸鼓有斁萬舞有奕我有嘉客亦不夷懌自古在昔先民有作
溫恭朝夕執事有恪顧予烝嘗湯孫之將
吳繹思
===
同考試官教諭羅批此篇前言祭之始此言祭之終場中作者
