皆不能分析題意又於自古在昔先民處不
能發明惟此得之允宜表出
考試官學正楊批形容商人盡樂與敬之實而致仰先王
来享之意洋洋盈耳誠可羡也
考試官教諭聶批美盛德告成功藹然當時之氣象作
者固如是夫
樂足以感先代之後敬足以紹先世之傳此後王所以冀先王之享祭也夫宗
廟之祭固尚夫樂而尤本乎敬也今也樂之盛旣足以感乎人敬之行又
punctuated:
十里，而今日之行無所留；明日之五十里，而明日之行無所滯，其行之速為何如哉！宣王之待元舅，其恩意之周浹、綜理之微密如此，詩人形諸咏歌，不亦宜乎？抑考申伯之於周，其生也有所自，其出也有所為。觀其所謂「維嶽降神，生甫及申」，則申伯之生，旣鍾嶽神之秀矣；所謂「四國于蕃，四方于宣」，則申伯之出，又足以為王國之翰矣。宣王得大臣之賢，而致中興之盛，豈不於斯而可見乎？

「庸鼓有斁，萬舞有奕。我有嘉客，亦不夷懌。自古在昔，先民有作。溫恭朝夕，執事有恪。顧予烝嘗，湯孫之將。」
吳繹思
〔同考試官教諭羅批：此篇前言祭之始，此言祭之終。場中作者皆不能分析題意，又於「自古在昔先民」處不能發明，惟此得之，允宜表出。〕
〔考試官學正楊批：形容商人盡樂與敬之實，而致仰先王来享之意，洋洋盈耳，誠可羡也。〕
〔考試官教諭聶批：「美盛德，告成功」，藹然當時之氣象，作者固如是夫！〕

樂足以感先代之後，敬足以紹先世之傳，此後王所以冀先王之享祭也。夫宗廟之祭，固尚夫樂，而尤本乎敬也。今也樂之盛旣足以感乎人，敬之行又
translation_en:
… [fifty] li today, so that today's march suffers no delay; and fifty li tomorrow, so that tomorrow's march meets no hindrance—how swift is his journey! That King Xuan treated his principal maternal uncle with such all-pervading kindness and such meticulous planning—was it not fitting that the poet gave it form in song? Moreover, if we examine the Earl of Shen's relation to Zhou, his birth had its origin, and his going forth into service had its achievement. Looking at the lines, "The lofty mountains sent down a spirit, who gave birth to Fu and Shen," the Earl of Shen at his birth was already endowed with the finest essence of the mountain spirit; and in the lines, "To the four states he is a screen, to the four quarters he spreads royal virtue," the Earl of Shen in his going forth was furthermore worthy to serve as a bulwark of the royal house. Can we not see right here how King Xuan obtained worthy great ministers and brought about the flourishing of his restoration?

"The large bells and drums ring out in abundance; the myriad dances are grandly ordered. We have admirable guests, who also are pleased and delighted. From of old, in ancient times, the former men set the example: mild and reverent morning and evening, performing the service with respect. May he look favorably upon our winter and autumn sacrifices, offered by the descendant of Tang!" (Book of Odes, Shang Hymns, "Na")
Wu Yisi 吳繹思
[Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Luo 羅: Earlier in this ode it speaks of the beginning of the sacrifice, whereas here it speaks of the conclusion of the sacrifice. None of the candidates in the examination hall were able to analyze the meaning of the topic, nor could they elucidate the phrase "From of old, in ancient times, the former men." Only this essay grasped it; it truly deserves to be singled out for publication.]
[Comment by Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Yang 楊: It vividly depicts the substance of how the men of Shang exhausted both music and reverence, and conveys their longing for the former king to come and enjoy the offering. It fills the ears with rich resonance and is truly admirable.]
[Comment by Examiner Instructor Nie 聶: "Praising abundant virtue and announcing accomplished merit"—it gently breathes the very atmosphere of that era. Such is indeed the work of a true writer!]

When music suffices to move the descendants of former dynasties, and reverence suffices to continue the transmission from former generations, this is whereby the later king hopes that the former king will enjoy the sacrifice. Now, the sacrifices in the ancestral temple certainly esteem music, yet they are even more fundamentally rooted in reverence. Now that the splendor of the music already suffices to move men, and the practice of reverence furthermore…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
有以傳於古宜乎商人冀先王之眷顧焉馬是詩祀成湯之樂也且夫金屬
曰庸革屬曰鼓而謂之有斁則疾徐有節清濁相宣斁斁然其盛矣
羽籥曰文干戚曰舞萬舞而謂之有奕則綴兆可觀儀文不紊奕奕
然有序矣樂舞之盛如此是以先代之後助祭之賓聞鐘鼓之音莫
不欣然而有和樂之意覩萬舞之容莫不怡然而有喜悅之心則樂之
感乎人者為何如哉然樂既感乎人而敬豈不傳於古乎且不徒曰自古
而必曰在昔則此敬之行非一人矣不徒曰在昔而必曰先民則是敬之行
非一日矣古人朝夕必溫恭也吾則溫恭於朝夕之間無一時之或怠焉古
人執事必有恪也吾則恪敬於執事之際無一事之敢慢焉其敬之法於
===
古人者又何如哉夫樂既盛矣敬既至矣固足以感格先王之神矣而
湯孫之心尤不敢以是而自足也謂夫成湯於冥冥之中其庶幾顧
我冬烝之祭乎是祭也乃湯孫所親奉而非攝以他人也烈祖於昭
昭之際其庶幾顧我秋嘗之祀乎是祀也乃湯孫所躬主而非委之於
他職也拳拳焉致其丁寧之意懇懇焉冀其眷顧之深先王有不來
格乎抑是詩商人祀成湯而作也然有樂焉必有禮有禮焉必有樂其
所謂庸鼓有斁萬舞有奕則樂之和為可知所謂溫恭朝夕執事
有恪則禮之謹為可見樂本於和禮本於敬此商人之禮樂所以為盛
也歟此其所以美盛德而告成功也歟
punctuated: 有以傳於古，宜乎商人冀先王之眷顧焉。馬是詩，祀成湯之樂也。且夫金屬曰庸，革屬曰鼓，而謂之「有斁」，則疾徐有節，清濁相宣，斁斁然其盛矣；羽籥曰文，干戚曰舞，「萬舞」而謂之「有奕」，則綴兆可觀，儀文不紊，奕奕然有序矣。樂舞之盛如此，是以先代之後、助祭之賓，聞鐘鼓之音，莫不欣然而有和樂之意；覩萬舞之容，莫不怡然而有喜悅之心。則樂之感乎人者為何如哉！然樂既感乎人，而敬豈不傳於古乎？且不徒曰「自古」而必曰「在昔」，則此敬之行非一人矣；不徒曰「在昔」而必曰「先民」，則是敬之行非一日矣。古人朝夕必溫恭也，吾則溫恭於朝夕之間，無一時之或怠焉；古人執事必有恪也，吾則恪敬於執事之際，無一事之敢慢焉。其敬之法於古人者又何如哉！夫樂既盛矣，敬既至矣，固足以感格先王之神矣，而湯孫之心尤不敢以是而自足也。謂夫成湯於冥冥之中，其庶幾顧我冬烝之祭乎？是祭也，乃湯孫所親奉，而非攝以他人也。烈祖於昭昭之際，其庶幾顧我秋嘗之祀乎？是祀也，乃湯孫所躬主，而非委之於他職也。拳拳焉致其丁寧之意，懇懇焉冀其眷顧之深，先王有不來格乎？抑是詩，商人祀成湯而作也。然有樂焉必有禮，有禮焉必有樂。其所謂「庸鼓有斁，萬舞有奕」，則樂之和為可知；所謂「溫恭朝夕，執事有恪」，則禮之謹為可見。樂本於和，禮本於敬，此商人之禮樂所以為盛也歟！此其所以美盛德而告成功也歟！
translation_en: … has been transmitted from antiquity, it is only fitting that the people of Shang hoped for the favor and regard of their former king. This ode [Na 那, from the Shang Hymns of the Book of Odes] is the music for sacrificing to Cheng Tang 成湯. Now, instruments of metal are called large bells (yong 庸), and those of hide are called drums (gu 鼓); when they are described as "resounding and prolonged" (you yi 有斁), it means their tempo is well-regulated and their clear and resonant tones complement one another—how grandly and continuously they sound! Dances with feathers and flutes are called civil, and those with shields and axes are called martial [reading 舞 as 武]; when the "all-embracing dance" (wan wu 萬舞) is described as "orderly and grand" (you yi 有奕), it means the dancing positions are a sight to behold and the ceremonial forms are unconfused—how gracefully and methodically they proceed! Because the music and dance were so magnificent, when the descendants of former dynasties, who came as guests to assist in the sacrifice, heard the sound of the bells and drums, none failed to feel joyful and harmonious; when they beheld the movements of the all-embracing dance, none failed to feel pleased and delighted. How profound, then, was the power of this music to move men! Yet if the music moved men, was not the reverence also transmitted from antiquity? Moreover, the ode does not merely say "from antiquity" (zi gu 自古), but insists on saying "in bygone times" (zai xi 在昔), showing that the practice of this reverence was not limited to a single person; it does not merely say "in bygone times," but insists on saying "among the former people" (xian min 先民), showing that the practice of this reverence was not the work of a single day. The ancients were unfailingly mild and reverent morning and evening; we, too, are mild and reverent from morning to evening, never slackening for a single moment. The ancients were unfailingly respectful in discharging their duties; we, too, are respectful and reverent when discharging our duties, never daring to be negligent in a single matter. How thorough, too, was their modeling of reverence upon the ancients! Now, once the music was so magnificent and the reverence so utmost, it was certainly sufficient to move and reach the spirit of the former king; yet the heart of Tang's descendant still dared not rest content with this. He thought: in the unseen realm, might Cheng Tang perhaps look with favor upon our winter sacrifice (zheng 烝)? For this sacrifice is personally offered by Tang's descendant, not delegated to another. In his radiant presence above, might the Illustrious Ancestor perhaps look with favor upon our autumn sacrifice (chang 嘗)? For this sacrifice is personally presided over by Tang's descendant, not entrusted to another official. Earnestly he conveys his repeated entreaties, and sincerely he hopes for his deep regard—how could the former king fail to come and be present? Furthermore, this ode was composed by the people of Shang for sacrificing to Cheng Tang. Yet where there is music, there must be ritual; and where there is ritual, there must be music. From the lines "The large bells and drums resound; the all-embracing dance is orderly and grand," the harmony of their music can be known; from the lines "Mild and reverent morning and evening, respectful in discharging duties," the carefulness of their ritual can be seen. Music is rooted in harmony, and ritual is rooted in reverence—is this not why the ritual and music of the people of Shang were so flourishing? And is this not how they praised flourishing virtue and announced the accomplishment of great works?

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
春秋義
齊高子來盟閔公二年楚屈完來盟于師僖公四年宋司馬華
孫來盟文公十五年
陳郕
同考試官訓導彭批此題作者往往失旨獨此篇詞嚴義
正超出衆作非深於属辞此事之教者
不能也宜冠本經
考試官學正楊批經旨詳明允如初考
考試官教諭聶批來盟一也而予奪不同此篇乃見作
===
手宜冠本經
春秋予大夫得奉使之宜而不予大夫遂私交之好此司馬華孫之來所
所以不可與高子屈完而例論也春秋同以來盟書之而予奪存乎事
焉且夫古者人臣出境有可以安社稷利國家則專之可也今也高子
以齊之大夫閔公二年慶父稔惡魯國曠年無君齊桓遣高子至魯
以覘國之虛實非有安危繼絕一定之計也屈完以楚之大夫僖公
四年齊桓伐楚八國同次于陘楚成使屈完如師以觀齊之強弱初
無請盟服義不易之命也然高子至不以兼國廣地為心惟以平
難善隣為美而僖公之位以定屈完來不恃方城漢水之險請夫
punctuated:
《春秋》義

「齊高子來盟。」（閔公二年）「楚屈完來盟于師。」（僖公四年）「宋司馬華孫來盟。」（文公十五年）

陳郕

同考試官訓導彭批：「此題作者往往失旨，獨此篇詞嚴義正，超出衆作。非深於属辞此事之教者，不能也。宜冠本經。」
考試官學正楊批：「經旨詳明，允如初考。」
考試官教諭聶批：「來盟一也，而予奪不同。此篇乃見作手，宜冠本經。」

《春秋》予大夫得奉使之宜，而不予大夫遂私交之好，此司馬華孫之來，所所以不可與高子、屈完而例論也。《春秋》同以「來盟」書之，而予奪存乎事焉。且夫古者人臣出境，有可以安社稷、利國家，則專之可也。今也高子以齊之大夫，閔公二年慶父稔惡，魯國曠年無君，齊桓遣高子至魯，以覘國之虛實，非有安危繼絕一定之計也。屈完以楚之大夫，僖公四年齊桓伐楚，八國同次于陘，楚成使屈完如師，以觀齊之強弱，初無請盟服義不易之命也。然高子至，不以兼國廣地為心，惟以平難善隣為美，而僖公之位以定；屈完來，不恃方城、漢水之險，請夫
translation_en:
Exposition on the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"Master Gao of Qi came and made a covenant" (2nd year of Duke Min). "Qu Wan of Chu came to the army and made a covenant" (4th year of Duke Xi). "Hua Sun, Minister of War of Song, came and made a covenant" (15th year of Duke Wen).

Chen Cheng

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Peng: "Writers on this topic often miss the main purport, yet this essay alone uses strict language and upholds righteous principles, surpassing the work of all others. None could have written this who was not deeply versed in the teaching of 'linking expressions and arranging events' (shuci bishi) of the Annals. It deserves to be placed first in this Classic."
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Yang: "The purport of the Classic is explained in clear detail; I concur with the initial examiner's assessment."
Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Nie: "'Coming and making a covenant' is the same in each case, yet the praise and blame differ. This essay reveals the hand of a master and deserves to be placed first in this Classic."

The Spring and Autumn Annals praises Great Officers for achieving what is appropriate in executing a mission, and does not praise Great Officers for fulfilling friendly relations through private intercourse. This is why the coming of Hua Sun, the Minister of War, cannot be discussed on the same footing as Master Gao and Qu Wan. The Spring and Autumn Annals records all of them alike as "came and made a covenant," yet praise and blame reside in the events themselves. Now in antiquity, when a subject went beyond the borders of his state, if there was something by which he could bring peace to the altars of soil and grain and benefit the state, it was permissible for him to act on his own authority. Here, as for Master Gao as a Great Officer of Qi: in the second year of Duke Min, when Qingfu had accumulated wickedness and the state of Lu had gone a whole year without a ruler, Duke Huan of Qi sent Master Gao to Lu to spy out the weakness or strength of the state, without having any settled plan to pacify danger and restore an interrupted line. And as for Qu Wan as a Great Officer of Chu: in the fourth year of Duke Xi, when Duke Huan of Qi attacked Chu and the armies of eight states encamped together at Xing, King Cheng of Chu sent Qu Wan to the army to observe the strength or weakness of Qi, originally without any unalterable command to request a covenant and submit to righteousness. Yet when Master Gao arrived, he did not set his mind on annexing the state and expanding territory, but regarded only quelling disorder and befriending a neighbor as admirable, and thus the position of Duke Xi was settled; when Qu Wan came, he did not rely on the strategic barriers of the Fangcheng mountains and the Han River, but requested…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
徵與同好之言而召陵之禮以成盟出於己而無專制之嫌事適乎宜
而得出疆之義春秋於二子之來皆不稱使所以予其得奉使之宜也為
何如若夫人臣義無私交大夫非君命不越境乃禮制之常也今也華孫
以司馬之官世秉宋國之政不輔其君以弭穆襄之禍謀自免討私為
盟魯之舉敢辱君謀禮非不恭也而非利國家之謀承命亞旅詞
非不善也而非安社稷之計其來也樹黨與以自固而國君不聞其盟
也結隣好以自安而君命未請無君之心以兆不臣之念以長比之高子
之盟固倍蓰之相遠矣較諸屈完之來又豈徑庭之可侔哉春秋於
華孫之來不稱使者所以著其私交之罪也又何如吁三子之得失不
===
同春秋之書法則一所謂美惡不嫌於同詞見矣大抵春秋一經之中來
盟不稱使者三而華孫之來固不足論矣然高子今日之安魯固可
美矣而前日于防之盟魯未免有抗尊之失屈完今日之服齊固可
嘉矣而後日楚人之滅黃未嘗有格君之善合而觀之思過半矣
公會晉侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衛子莒子盟于踐土僖公二十八年
同盟于亳城北襄公十一年
陳廷玉
同考試官訓導彭批此題本平易而作者多戾經旨惟此篇文
理通暢深合題意故表而出之
punctuated:
徵與同好之言，而召陵之禮以成。盟出於己，而無專制之嫌；事適乎宜，而得出疆之義。《春秋》於二子之來，皆不稱「使」，所以予其得奉使之宜也為何如！若夫人臣義無私交，大夫非君命不越境，乃禮制之常也。今也華孫以司馬之官，世秉宋國之政，不輔其君以弭穆、襄之禍，謀自免討，私為盟魯之舉。「敢辱君謀」，禮非不恭也，而非利國家之謀；「承命亞旅」，詞非不善也，而非安社稷之計。其來也，樹黨與以自固，而國君不聞；其盟也，結隣好以自安，而君命未請。無君之心以兆，不臣之念以長。比之高子之盟，固倍蓰之相遠矣；較諸屈完之來，又豈徑庭之可侔哉？《春秋》於華孫之來不稱「使」者，所以著其私交之罪也又何如！吁！三子之得失不同，《春秋》之書法則一，所謂美惡不嫌於同詞見矣。大抵《春秋》一經之中，「來盟」不稱「使」者三，而華孫之來，固不足論矣。然高子今日之安魯，固可美矣，而前日于防之盟，魯未免有抗尊之失；屈完今日之服齊，固可嘉矣，而後日楚人之滅黃，未嘗有格君之善。合而觀之，思過半矣。

公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衛子、莒子盟于踐土（僖公二十八年）；同盟于亳城北（襄公十一年）。
陳廷玉
同考試官訓導彭批：此題本平易，而作者多戾經旨。惟此篇文理通暢，深合題意，故表而出之。
translation_en:
… words of seeking shared amity, and thus the ritual protocols at Shaoling were accomplished. Though the covenants originated from themselves, they incurred no suspicion of acting arbitrarily; their actions suited what was appropriate, and they fulfilled the righteous duty of an envoy who has crossed his state's borders. In recording the arrival of these two men, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) in neither case designates them as "sent as envoy" (shi)—how great indeed is its approval of their having achieved what was appropriate to their mission!

As for the principle that a subject in righteousness has no private foreign relations, and that a Great Officer does not cross the borders without his ruler's command, this is the constant rule of ritual institutions. Now Hua Sun, holding the office of Minister of War (Sima) and hereditarily wielding the government of the state of Song, did not assist his ruler in quelling the disasters of the lineages of Mu and Xiang, but instead schemed to exempt himself from punishment and privately undertook the act of making a covenant with Lu. His saying "I dare not disgrace your lordship's counsel" was not lacking in ritual respect, yet it was no plan for benefiting the state; his saying "I have received instructions from the secondary officers" was not lacking in fine phrasing, yet it was no design for securing the altars of soil and grain. In coming, he planted partisan alliances tostrengthen himself while his ruler heard nothing of it; in making the covenant, he contracted neighborly amity to secure himself while never requesting his ruler's command. A heart that disregarded his ruler was thereby portended, and thoughts unbefitting a subject thereby grew. Compared to the covenant of Master Gao (Gaozi), it is already fivefold removed; measured against the coming of Qu Wan, how could the disparity be merely as wide as a courtyard and passage? That the Spring and Autumn Annals does not designate Hua Sun as "sent as envoy" when he came—how severe indeed is its exposure of his crime of engaging in private foreign relations!

Alas! The merits and faults of the three men are different, yet the historiographical rule of the Spring and Autumn Annals is one and the same; here may be seen what is meant by not hesitating to use identical wording for both the admirable and the wicked. On the whole, within the entire classic of the Spring and Autumn Annals, there are three instances of "coming to make a covenant" without the designation "sent as envoy," and the coming of Hua Sun is certainly not worth discussing. Yet while Master Gao's pacifying of Lu on this day was certainly admirable, in the earlier covenant at Fang, Lu was not free from the fault of defying a superior; and while Qu Wan's submission to Qi on this day was certainly praiseworthy, when the men of Chu later destroyed Huang, he never showed the virtue of rectifying his ruler's mind. If one views them together, more than half will be understood.

"The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju, and made a covenant at Jiantu" (28th year of Duke Xi); "They made a covenant together north of the capital of Bo" (11th year of Duke Xiang).
Chen Tingyu

Comment by Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor (Xundao) Peng: This topic is inherently plain and accessible, yet most writers violated the purport of the Classic. Only this essay is fluent in style and coherent in reasoning, deeply matching the meaning of the topic; therefore I have singled it out for distinction.

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正楊批文暢理明初考取之當也
考試官教諭聶批二公皆獎王室春秋所嘉此篇深
合本旨宜在選列
繼霸者講信以獎王室固可美復霸者講信以獎王室亦可嘉此文
悼之尊王春秋得不備書而並予之哉且夫踐土之盟果何盟乎盖晉文
獎王而有是舉也于斯之時因天王之下勞合列國以講好獻俘衡雍而
昭敵愾之功要言王庭而伸尊獎之誠展夫出入三覲之敬致夫天威
咫尺之恭水木本源之油然而興江漢朝宗之義藹然而著則晉文獎
王之功為何如耶若夫亳北之盟又何盟乎盖晉悼獎王而有是役也
===
當是之時因鄭人之行成率諸侯以同歃大侯小伯咸知以獎王為
心友邦家君皆知以獎王為務尊周室於旣卑之時收人心於渙
散之際上天下澤之分由是而明衣裳冠冕之念由是而起則晉悼獎
王之義又何如耶吁即踐土之盟于以見晉文獎王之功顯即亳北之盟
于以見晉悼獎王之義著春秋備書而並予之意昭昭矣雖然論
霸者之功不可不論其過晉文今日踐土之獎王固可美矣然後日會
于溫而請王出狩盟翟泉而上替下陵又豈可美乎晉悼今日亳北
之獎王亦可嘉矣然前日盟雞澤而瀆慢王臣會邢丘而委政大夫
又豈可嘉乎讀經者得不有慨於斯
punctuated:
考試官學正楊批：文暢理明，初考取之，當也。
考試官教諭聶批：二公皆獎王室，《春秋》所嘉。此篇深合本旨，宜在選列。
繼霸者講信以獎王室，固可美；復霸者講信以獎王室，亦可嘉。此文、悼之尊王，《春秋》得不備書而並予之哉？且夫踐土之盟，果何盟乎？盖晉文獎王而有是舉也。于斯之時，因天王之下勞，合列國以講好。獻俘衡雍，而昭敵愾之功；要言王庭，而伸尊獎之誠。展夫出入三覲之敬，致夫天威咫尺之恭。水木本源之油然而興，江漢朝宗之義藹然而著，則晉文獎王之功為何如耶？若夫亳北之盟，又何盟乎？盖晉悼獎王而有是役也。當是之時，因鄭人之行成，率諸侯以同歃。大侯小伯，咸知以獎王為心；友邦家君，皆知以獎王為務。尊周室於旣卑之時，收人心於渙散之際。上天下澤之分由是而明，衣裳冠冕之念由是而起，則晉悼獎王之義又何如耶？吁！即踐土之盟，于以見晉文獎王之功顯；即亳北之盟，于以見晉悼獎王之義著。《春秋》備書而並予之意，昭昭矣。雖然，論霸者之功，不可不論其過。晉文今日踐土之獎王，固可美矣；然後日會于溫而請王出狩，盟翟泉而上替下陵，又豈可美乎？晉悼今日亳北之獎王，亦可嘉矣；然前日盟雞澤而瀆慢王臣，會邢丘而委政大夫，又豈可嘉乎？讀經者得不有慨於斯！
translation_en:
Examiner and Subprefectural/Departmental Director of Studies Yang comments: The writing is fluent and the reasoning clear; the initial examiner's selection of it is fitting.
Examiner and District Director of Studies Nie comments: Both dukes supported the royal house, which the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) commends. This essay deeply accords with the fundamental purport and deserves to be placed among the selected.
When one who succeeded to the hegemony cultivated good faith in order to support the royal house, it was certainly praiseworthy; when one who restored the hegemony cultivated good faith in order to support the royal house, it was likewise commendable. In this honoring of the king by Duke Wen and Duke Dao, how could the Spring and Autumn Annals not record it in full and grant approval to both? Now, what sort of covenant was the covenant at Jiantu? It was an action undertaken because Duke Wen of Jin was supporting the king. At that time, on account of the Heavenly King descending to reward his troops, he brought together the various states to cultivate friendly relations. Presenting captives at Hengyong, he displayed the merit of opposing the king's enemies; plighting his word in the royal court, he extended his sincerity in honoring and supporting the throne. He demonstrated the reverence of thrice having audience upon entering and leaving, and showed the respect due to the Heavenly majesty just a foot away. When the sense of water's source and a tree's root welled up spontaneously, and the righteousness of the Jiang and Han rivers paying court to the sea became abundantly manifest, how great indeed was the merit of Duke Wen of Jin in supporting the king! As for the covenant north of Bo, what sort of covenant was it? It was a campaign undertaken because Duke Dao of Jin was supporting the king. At that time, on account of the men of Zheng suing for peace, he led the feudal lords to smear their lips with blood together in covenant. Great marquises and lesser earls all knew to take supporting the king as their mind; the rulers of friendly states all knew to take supporting the king as their duty. He honored the house of Zhou at a time when it had already fallen low, and gathered men's allegiance at a moment when it had scattered. The distinction of heaven above and marsh below was thereby made clear, and the mindfulness of ritual robes and ceremonial caps thereby arose—how great indeed was the righteousness of Duke Dao of Jin in supporting the king! Ah! From the covenant at Jiantu, one sees the splendor of the merit of Duke Wen of Jin in supporting the king; from the covenant north of Bo, one sees the prominence of the righteousness of Duke Dao of Jin in supporting the king. The intention of the Spring and Autumn Annals in recording both in full and granting approval to both is crystal clear. Even so, in discussing the merits of hegemons, one cannot fail to discuss their faults. That Duke Wen of Jin today at Jiantu supported the king is certainly praiseworthy; yet later, when he met at Wen and requested the king to go out on a hunting tour, and covenanted at Diquan where superiors were disregarded and inferiors encroached upon them—how could that also be praiseworthy? That Duke Dao of Jin today north of Bo supported the king is likewise commendable; yet earlier, when he covenanted at Jize and treated the king's minister with disrespect, and met at Xingqiu and entrusted governance to the grandees—how could that also be commendable? How can readers of the Classic not sigh over this!

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
禮記義
仁者仁此者也禮者履此者也義者宜此者也信者信此者也強
者強此者也
鄧珙
同考試官教諭黎批此篇之作雅而不浮澹而有味必熟
於禮者一薦奚忝
考試官學正楊批發明衆德成孝之理極是宜登選列
考噰官教諭聶批無冗長之嗣有簡澹之味初考得之
高薦宜矣
===
德具於人雖殊德施於孝則一夫孝之行雖大必資衆德以成之也使
人之德有一而不施於孝又何以盡事親之道哉見於祭義之篇其旨如
此今夫在人之行莫大於事親之孝孝行之成必由於衆德之資是故
仁主於愛愛莫大於愛親人能盡其愛親之心則仁之施不失其序然
仁非先施於孝豈得謂仁之德乎禮主於敬敬莫先於敬親人能行
其敬親之禮則禮之用必踐其實然禮非能履於孝豈得謂禮之德
乎至若合宜之謂義苟不順其理之當然而陷親於不義則義之德
必虧是義也者不過宜於孝而已以實之謂信苟不能實矣其心之所
發而事親以不誠則信之德必妄是信也者不過實於孝而已然曰仁
punctuated:
禮記義

「仁者，仁此者也；禮者，履此者也；義者，宜此者也；信者，信此者也；強者，強此者也。」

鄧珙

同考試官教諭黎批：此篇之作，雅而不浮，澹而有味，必熟於《禮》者。一薦奚忝？
考試官學正楊批：發明衆德成孝之理極是，宜登選列。
考噰官教諭聶批：無冗長之嗣，有簡澹之味。初考得之，高薦宜矣。

德具於人雖殊，德施於孝則一。夫孝之行雖大，必資衆德以成之也。使人之德有一而不施於孝，又何以盡事親之道哉？見於《祭義》之篇，其旨如此。今夫在人之行，莫大於事親之孝；孝行之成，必由於衆德之資。是故仁主於愛，愛莫大於愛親。人能盡其愛親之心，則仁之施不失其序；然仁非先施於孝，豈得謂仁之德乎？禮主於敬，敬莫先於敬親。人能行其敬親之禮，則禮之用必踐其實；然禮非能履於孝，豈得謂禮之德乎？至若合宜之謂義，苟不順其理之當然，而陷親於不義，則義之德必虧，是義也者，不過宜於孝而已；以實之謂信，苟不能實矣其心之所發，而事親以不誠，則信之德必妄，是信也者，不過實於孝而已。然曰仁、
translation_en:
Exposition on the Record of Rites (Liji)

"Benevolence is to treat this with benevolence; ritual propriety is to tread this in practice; righteousness is to make this fitting; trustworthiness is to be true to this; strength is to be strong in this."

Deng Gong 鄧珙

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Li comments: The composition of this essay is refined without being superficial, and understated yet rich in flavor; the author must be well-versed in the Record of Rites. What shame could there be in recommending it?
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Yang comments: It elucidates the principle that the multitude of virtues brings filial piety to completion most aptly; he ought to be placed on the list of those selected.
Examiner [?] and County Director of Studies Nie comments: Free of verbose expressions [?], it possesses a concise and understated flavor. Having been selected in the initial reading, it is fitting that it be highly recommended.

Although the virtues endowed in human beings are distinct, in their application to filial piety they are one. Now, great though the practice of filial piety is, it must rely upon the multitude of virtues in order to be brought to completion. If even one of a person's virtues were not applied to filial piety, how could one exhaust the Way of serving one's parents? As seen in the "Meaning of Sacrifices" ("Jiyi") chapter, such is its purport. Now, among human actions, none is greater than filial piety in serving one's parents; and the completion of filial conduct must come from the aid of the multitude of virtues. Therefore, benevolence centers on love, and no love is greater than loving one's parents. When a person can exhaust his heart in loving his parents, the application of benevolence does not lose its proper order; yet if benevolence is not first applied to filial piety, how could it be called the virtue of benevolence? Ritual propriety centers on reverence, and no reverence comes before revering one's parents. When a person can carry out the rites of revering his parents, the function of ritual propriety will surely fulfill its substance; yet if ritual propriety cannot be trodden in filial piety, how could it be called the virtue of ritual propriety? As for righteousness, which means conforming to what is fitting: if one does not follow what is naturally right in principle and thereby lets one's parents fall into unrighteousness, then the virtue of righteousness will surely be impaired; thus righteousness is nothing more than doing what is fitting in filial piety. And as for trustworthiness, which means acting with substance: if one cannot make substantive [?] what issues from one's heart and thus serves one's parents without sincerity, then the virtue of trustworthiness will surely be false; thus trustworthiness is nothing more than being substantive in filial piety. Yet what are called benevolence…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
曰禮固行於孝矣尤必始終一心而無始勤終怠之失則可謂之強以強此孝
焉曰義曰信亦施於孝矣尤必先後一致而有自強不息之意斯可謂之
強此孝焉吁資衆德以成一孝賴一勇以全衆德則人子事親之道不其至
歟大抵孝者衆德之本人心同然之理也置之而塞乎天地溥之而横乎
四海者此孝也施諸後世而無朝夕者亦此孝也昔吾夫子謂其為德
之本而教之所由生夫豈不信
唯賢者能盡祭之義賢者之祭也必受其福
張德瑄
同考試官教諭黎批祭統題講雖可為而破難下手此作
===
講旣詳贍而破尤簡健本經之冠匪此其誰
考試官學正揚批此題義與福字作者多不能識惟此
篇體認得實宜冠本經
考試官教諭聶批說者於祭必受福處多指五福惟此
篇甚合本旨其亦熟於禮者乎
觀君子之於祭以其義獨能盡而福必能受也盖無所不順者福之名
以物將心者祭之義君子之於祭旣能獨盡其義則其於祭之前豈
不能必受其福哉今夫祭禮之行貴乎有心而後有物也但世之忘
其心者固多徇於物者不少惟君子之祭感春雨之旣濡其怵惕之
punctuated:
曰禮，固行於孝矣，尤必始終一心，而無始勤終怠之失，則可謂之強，以強此孝焉；曰義曰信，亦施於孝矣，尤必先後一致，而有自強不息之意，斯可謂之強此孝焉。吁！資衆德以成一孝，賴一勇以全衆德，則人子事親之道，不其至歟？大抵孝者，衆德之本，人心同然之理也。置之而塞乎天地，溥之而横乎四海者，此孝也；施諸後世而無朝夕者，亦此孝也。昔吾夫子謂其為德之本，而教之所由生，夫豈不信！

唯賢者能盡祭之義，賢者之祭也，必受其福。
張德瑄
同考試官教諭黎批：祭統題講雖可為，而破難下手。此作講旣詳贍，而破尤簡健，本經之冠，匪此其誰？
考試官學正揚批：此題義與福字，作者多不能識，惟此篇體認得實，宜冠本經。
考試官教諭聶批：說者於「祭必受福」處，多指五福，惟此篇甚合本旨，其亦熟於《禮》者乎！

觀君子之於祭，以其義獨能盡，而福必能受也。盖無所不順者，福之名；以物將心者，祭之義。君子之於祭，旣能獨盡其義，則其於祭之前，豈不能必受其福哉？今夫祭禮之行，貴乎有心而後有物也。但世之忘其心者固多，徇於物者不少。惟君子之祭，感春雨之旣濡，其怵惕之
translation_en:
… and propriety are indeed practiced in filial piety, yet one must especially remain of one mind from beginning to end, without the fault of being diligent at first and lax at the end; then it may be called strength, wherewith to strengthen this filial piety. Righteousness and trustworthiness are likewise applied in filial piety, yet one must especially be consistent from first to last, possessing the intent of unceasing self-strengthening; thus it may be called strengthening this filial piety. Ah! Relying on the multitude of virtues to accomplish a single filial piety, and depending on a single courage to perfect the multitude of virtues—is not the way a filial son serves his parents thereby brought to its utmost? In general, filial piety is the root of all virtues and the principle shared alike by human hearts. Set it up and it fills heaven and earth; spread it out and it extends across the four seas—such is this filial piety. Hand it down to future generations and it knows no end, morning or evening—such too is this filial piety. In the past, when our Master said that it is the root of virtue and that from which teaching is born, how could that not be trustworthy!

"Only the worthy man can exhaust the meaning of sacrifice; in his sacrifice the worthy man is certain to receive its blessing."
By Zhang Dexuan 張德瑄.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Li 黎 comments: On this topic from the "Summary of Sacrifices" (Jitong 祭統), although the exposition is manageable, the opening statement of the theme (po 破) is difficult to tackle. In this composition, the exposition is detailed and rich, while the opening statement is especially concise and vigorous. As the first-place essay in this Classic, if not this one, then whose?
Examiner and Director of Studies Yang 揚 comments: Most writers fail to grasp the characters "meaning" (yi 義) and "blessing" (fu 福) in this topic. Only this essay comprehends them with true substance; it deserves to stand first in this Classic.
Examiner and Instructor Nie 聶 comments: In explaining the passage "in sacrifice one is certain to receive blessing," commentators mostly refer to the Five Blessings. Only this essay accords very closely with the original purport; is the author not deeply versed in the Book of Rites (Li 禮)?

Look at the gentleman in relation to sacrifice: because he alone can exhaust its meaning, he is certain to receive its blessing. For "having nothing in which one does not act in accordance" is the definition of blessing, and "conveying the heart's intent by means of offerings" is the meaning of sacrifice. Since in sacrifice the gentleman alone is able to exhaust its meaning, how could he not be certain to receive its blessing even prior to the sacrifice? Now, in the performance of sacrificial rites, what is valued is first having the heart's intent and only afterward the material offerings. Yet in the world, those who forget their heart's intent are certainly many, and those who merely pursue external offerings are not few. Only in the sacrifice of the gentleman, moved when the spring rains have moistened the earth, his feeling of awe and alarm…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
心油然以生感霜露之既降其悽愴之心盡然以動於是奉之以三
牲之俎以表此心之誠陳之以八簋之實以將此心之敬發於心而奉其物此
豈衆人之所能奉其物以將其心實乃君子之所獨夫君子之能祭如此
必其於祭之前雖鬼神極其幽也則致其誠信而上有以順乎鬼神矣雖
君長極其尊也則與其忠敬而外有以順於君長矣內焉順於親而
親無不安外焉順於道而道無不達幽明人鬼無一事之不順外道內
親無一順之不備君子於祭之必受其福也如此夫豈世之所謂永受
胡福介爾景福之可比哉抑觀祭祀之禮至不一也有以多為貴者有
以少為貴者以多為貴者以其外心也以少為貴者以其內心也此之
===
所謂能盡祭之義者是由內而之外彼之所謂以多為貴者是因文
以見本學者誠能以內為尊以外為樂則本文兼舉而內外不遺百
順之名豈不必受於已哉
論
聖位天德 龔沅
同考試官教諭羅 批超出衆作可為論中之魁者也
考試官學正楊 批作者妄認題意不愜人心忽得此卷
辭理兼該議論正大不啻若聆黃鍾
太簇之交奏也
punctuated:
心油然以生；感霜露之既降，其悽愴之心盡然以動。於是奉之以三牲之俎，以表此心之誠；陳之以八簋之實，以將此心之敬。發於心而奉其物，此豈衆人之所能？奉其物以將其心，實乃君子之所獨。夫君子之能祭如此，必其於祭之前，雖鬼神極其幽也，則致其誠信而上有以順乎鬼神矣；雖君長極其尊也，則與其忠敬而外有以順於君長矣。內焉順於親而親無不安，外焉順於道而道無不達。幽明人鬼，無一事之不順；外道內親，無一順之不備。君子於祭之必受其福也如此，夫豈世之所謂「永受胡福」、「介爾景福」之可比哉？抑觀祭祀之禮，至不一也。有以多為貴者，有以少為貴者。以多為貴者，以其外心也；以少為貴者，以其內心也。此之所謂能盡祭之義者，是由內而之外；彼之所謂以多為貴者，是因文以見本。學者誠能以內為尊，以外為樂，則本文兼舉而內外不遺，百順之名豈不必受於已哉？

論
聖位天德 龔沅
同考試官教諭羅批：超出衆作，可為論中之魁者也。
考試官學正楊批：作者妄認題意，不愜人心。忽得此卷，辭理兼該，議論正大，不啻若聆黃鍾、太簇之交奏也。
translation_en:
…[apprehensive] heart arises spontaneously; moved when frost and dew have fallen, his sorrowful heart is deeply stirred [reading 盡 as 憯/慘]. Thereupon he presents the sacrificial stands of the three livestock to manifest the sincerity of this heart, and sets forth the contents of the eight grain-vessels to convey the reverence of this heart. To issue from the heart and thus present the offerings—how could the multitude be capable of this? To present the offerings in order to convey the heart is truly unique to the noble man. Now, since the noble man is able to sacrifice in this manner, it must be that prior to the sacrifice—even though spirits and gods are utterly unseen—he has extended his sincerity and trustworthiness so that above he is in harmony with spirits and gods; and even though ruler and superiors are utterly exalted, he has given his loyalty and reverence [or: practiced loyalty and reverence] so that outwardly he is in harmony with ruler and superiors. Inwardly, he is in harmony with his parents so that his parents are never ill at ease; outwardly, he is in harmony with the Way so that the Way is never obstructed. Across the unseen and the seen, among men and spirits, there is not a single matter that is not in harmony; between the Way without and parents within, there is not a single harmony that is not complete. Such is the certainty with which the noble man receives blessing in sacrifice—how could it be compared to what the world calls "forever receiving longevous blessing" or "increasing your great blessing"? Moreover, if we observe the rites of sacrifice, they are most varied. There are those in which abundance is prized, and those in which paucity is prized. Where abundance is prized, it is because the heart is directed outward; where paucity is prized, it is because the heart is directed inward. What is here called being able to exhaust the meaning of sacrifice proceeds from the inner to the outer; what is there called prizing abundance is to perceive the root by means of outward form. If the student can truly take the inner as what is honored and the outer as what gives joy, then root and pattern are both upheld and neither inner nor outer is neglected—how could the name of "complete harmony in all things" (baishun, i.e., blessing) not certainly be received by oneself?

Discourse
"The Sage's Position and Heavenly Virtue"
Gong Yuan 龔沅
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Luo: Surpasses all the other compositions; it may stand as the champion among the discourses.
Comment by Examiner Director of Studies Yang: The candidates misconstrued the meaning of the topic, leaving the mind dissatisfied. Suddenly coming upon this paper—comprehensive in both diction and principle, upright and grand in its argumentation—was nothing less than listening to the Yellow Bell (huangzhong) and Great Cluster (taicu) pitch-pipes playing in concert.

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭聶批諸作皆不考張子立言之意令人厭
觀惟此篇旨趣高遠考據精詳筆勢
滔滔所謂波瀾老成者
論曰莫大乎天而元亨利貞運行於四時無一息之或爽莫大於聖
人而仁義禮智充周於一身無一時之或間夫天之德不可名以其
運而不已無朕兆之可覩也聖人之德不可名以其大而化之無形跡
之可窺也造聖人之位達天德之妙非大而化之其孰能與於斯
請因先儒張子正蒙之旨而申論之正南面而垂衣裳人皆知其
位之尊也此特聖人所得之位而非造天德之位也居九重而履
===
大寶人皆謂其位之貴也此特聖人所處之位而非聖人達天德之
位也欲知聖位天德之妙果何如哉必大而化之而後可造乎其極
也殊不知充満而積實可以謂之美矣豈得謂之化乎未至於化
則與天德有間矣積實而光輝可以謂之大矣豈得謂之化乎未
至於化則與天德不侔矣大可為也化其可為乎大可勉也化其可
勉乎彼其伊尹聖之任者也能負荷聖人所當為之事勉力以
求至乎聖人之地雖有跡之可見猶不害於未化爾顏子聖之
亞者也克己以請事聖人之教欲竭其才以求底乎聖人之域
但不假之以年而未至於化爾必也無我而後大大成性而後
punctuated:
考試官教諭聶批：「諸作皆不考張子立言之意，令人厭觀；惟此篇旨趣高遠，考據精詳，筆勢滔滔，所謂波瀾老成者。」

論曰：莫大乎天，而元、亨、利、貞運行於四時，無一息之或爽；莫大於聖人，而仁、義、禮、智充周於一身，無一時之或間。夫天之德不可名，以其運而不已，無朕兆之可覩也；聖人之德不可名，以其大而化之，無形跡之可窺也。造聖人之位，達天德之妙，非大而化之，其孰能與於斯？請因先儒張子《正蒙》之旨而申論之。正南面而垂衣裳，人皆知其位之尊也，此特聖人所得之位，而非造天德之位也；居九重而履大寶，人皆謂其位之貴也，此特聖人所處之位，而非聖人達天德之位也。欲知聖位天德之妙，果何如哉？必大而化之，而後可造乎其極也。殊不知充満而積實，可以謂之美矣，豈得謂之化乎？未至於化，則與天德有間矣。積實而光輝，可以謂之大矣，豈得謂之化乎？未至於化，則與天德不侔矣。大可為也，化其可為乎？大可勉也，化其可勉乎？彼其伊尹，聖之任者也，能負荷聖人所當為之事，勉力以求至乎聖人之地，雖有跡之可見，猶不害於未化爾。顏子，聖之亞者也，克己以請事聖人之教，欲竭其才以求底乎聖人之域，但不假之以年，而未至於化爾。必也無我而後大，大成性而後…
translation_en:
Examiner Nie, Instructor, commented: "All the other essays fail to examine Master Zhang's [Zhang Zai 張載] intention in establishing these words, making them tiresome to read. Only this piece is lofty and far-reaching in its purport, precise and detailed in its textual grounding, and surging in its brushwork—truly what is called mature and accomplished in its grand sweep."

The discourse reads: Nothing is greater than Heaven, whose origination, flourishing, advantage, and firmness revolve through the four seasons without a single breath's deviation; nothing is greater than the sage, in whose single person benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom circulate fully without a single moment's interruption. Now, the virtue of Heaven cannot be named, because it revolves ceaselessly without any incipient sign that can be witnessed; the virtue of the sage cannot be named, because it is great and transmuting, without any physical trace that can be glimpsed. To reach the position of the sage and attain the subtlety of heavenly virtue—if not one who is great and transmuting, who could partake in this? Allow me to elaborate on this on the basis of the purport of the former Confucian Master Zhang's Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng). When one faces due south and lets robes hang down, everyone knows the尊崇 (exaltedness) of his position; yet this is merely the position the sage has acquired, not the position that reaches heavenly virtue. When one dwells in the ninefold palace and occupies the Great Treasure [the throne], everyone speaks of the nobility of his position; yet this is merely the position in which the sage resides, not the position in which the sage attains heavenly virtue. If we wish to know what the subtlety of the sage's position and heavenly virtue is really like, how can it be understood? One must be great and transmuting, and only then can one reach its ultimate pinnacle. People fail to realize that being completely filled and accumulating substance may be called "beautiful," but how could it be called "transmuting"? Before reaching transmutation, there is still a gap between oneself and heavenly virtue. Accumulating substance and shining forth gloriously may be called "great," but how could it be called "transmuting"? Before reaching transmutation, one is still not equal to heavenly virtue. Greatness can be achieved through deliberate action, but can transmutation be achieved through deliberate action? Greatness can be striven for, but can transmutation be striven for? Consider Yi Yin 伊尹, who was the "responsible one" among sages: he was able to shoulder the affairs that a sage ought to undertake, striving with all his might to reach the ground of the sage; though traces of his effort could still be seen, it did no harm to the fact that he had not yet reached transmutation. Master Yan [Yan Hui 顏回] was second to the sage: he overcame himself and asked to put the sage's teachings into practice, wishing to exhaust his talents in seeking to arrive at the realm of the sage; it was only that Heaven did not grant him the years, and so he had not yet reached transmutation. Only when there is no self-centeredness does one become great, and only when greatness becomes one's very nature does one…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
化化則泯然無形之可驗蕩然無跡之可名德盛仁熟自然而然
非智力之所能及也至此而謂之聖位天德乃造其極而無以加
矣非天下之至聖其孰能與於斯由是觀之天之於穆不已即
聖人之至誠無息也天之物各付物即聖人之泛應曲應當也在
天為元聖人之仁即天之元時之春也在天為亨聖人之禮即天之
亨時之夏也以至聖人之義與天之利時之秋同一機聖人之智與
天之貞時之冬無二致論而至是吾不知聖人其天乎天其聖人
乎彼伊尹顏淵固未及此求其可以當此者其惟堯舜乎吁堯
舜遠矣造聖人之位具天德之大幸有今日
===
聖人在上
表
擬宋胡安國進春秋傳表
鄧珙
同考試官教諭黎批表得體
考試官學正楊批典雅
考試官教諭聶批嗣嚴義正隊仗森然可取
天子議禮考文表六經之正學
聖人神道設教開萬世之太平當關雎麟趾之化行正奎璧圖
punctuated:
化，化則泯然無形之可驗，蕩然無跡之可名，德盛仁熟，自然而然，非智力之所能及也。至此而謂之聖位天德，乃造其極而無以加矣。非天下之至聖，其孰能與於斯？由是觀之，天之於穆不已，即聖人之至誠無息也；天之物各付物，即聖人之泛應曲應當也。在天為元，聖人之仁即天之元、時之春也；在天為亨，聖人之禮即天之亨、時之夏也；以至聖人之義與天之利、時之秋同一機，聖人之智與天之貞、時之冬無二致。論而至是，吾不知聖人其天乎？天其聖人乎？彼伊尹、顏淵固未及此，求其可以當此者，其惟堯、舜乎！吁，堯、舜遠矣，造聖人之位、具天德之大，幸有今日聖人在上。

表

擬宋胡安國進《春秋傳》表
鄧珙
同考試官教諭黎批：表得體。
考試官學正楊批：典雅。
考試官教諭聶批：嗣嚴義正，隊仗森然，可取。

天子議禮考文，表六經之正學；聖人神道設教，開萬世之太平。當《關雎》、《麟趾》之化行，正奎、璧、圖、
translation_en:
… transformation. Once transformed, it is seamless without any form that can be verified, boundless without any trace that can be named; virtue is abundant and benevolence is mature, being so of itself, beyond what knowledge and effort can reach. Reaching this point and calling it the sage's position and heavenly virtue is to have attained the ultimate to which nothing more can be added. Save for the most sagely in the world, who could partake in this? Viewed from this perspective, Heaven's profound and ceaseless operation is none other than the sage's utmost sincerity without pause; Heaven's endowing each thing according to its nature is none other than the sage's responding broadly and intricately with exact appropriateness [?]. What in Heaven is origination (yuan) is in the sage benevolence, which is Heaven's origination and the season of spring; what in Heaven is flourishing (heng) is in the sage propriety, which is Heaven's flourishing and the season of summer; and so too the sage's righteousness shares the same mechanism as Heaven's advantage (li) and the season of autumn, while the sage's wisdom is no different from Heaven's firmness (zhen) and the season of winter. Carrying the discussion to this point, I do not know whether the sage is Heaven, or Heaven is the sage! Yi Yin and Yan Yuan certainly did not reach this; if we seek those who can match it, would it not be only Yao and Shun! Alas, Yao and Shun are distant now, yet to attain the position of the sage and possess the greatness of heavenly virtue, we are fortunate today to have a sage on the throne above.

Memorial (Biao)

A Memorial in the Persona of Hu Anguo of the Song Presenting His Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu zhuan)
Deng Gong
Associate Examiner and Confucian Instructor Li comments: The memorial is fitting in form.
Examiner and Director of Studies Yang comments: Classically elegant.
Examiner and Confucian Instructor Nie comments: The diction [? reading 嗣 as 詞] is rigorous and the meaning upright; its parallel array is stately and impressive—worthy of selection.

The Son of Heaven deliberates on rituals and examines the written script, displaying the orthodox learning of the Six Classics; the Sage establishes teachings by the divine way, opening up supreme peace for ten thousand generations. Just as the transforming influence of the "Guanju" and "Linzhi" odes is in effect, and the auspicious omens of the Kui and Bi constellations, River Chart, and…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
書之瑞應若稽往古斷自
宸衷謂春秋之作實肇於素王而
宵旰之勤尚勞於
睿覽褒貶每嚴於一字傳註多謬於專門大義乖而未彰曲說
混而莫辨欲明三傳之得失獨究遺經之始終爰命近臣
重加著釋臣深慚末學濫綴清班強探儒先直指之歸未領
史外傳心之要是用旁搜載博采群言徵顯闡幽窺見十二
公之事尊王賤伯講明數千載之前雖淵微之義或未貫
通而綱常之道庶其有補兹盖伏遇
===
〇〇〇〇
聰明天縱
聖敬日躋
乃武乃文光復
中興之大業
惟精惟一丕承
烈祖之鴻猷俯
萬幾之暇特
賜覽觀而一得之愚敢忘報稱休願
punctuated: 書之瑞應。若稽往古，斷自宸衷；謂《春秋》之作，實肇於素王；而宵旰之勤，尚勞於睿覽。褒貶每嚴於一字，傳註多謬於專門；大義乖而未彰，曲說混而莫辨。欲明三傳之得失，獨究遺經之始終，爰命近臣，重加著釋。臣深慚末學，濫綴清班；強探儒先直指之歸，未領史外傳心之要。是用旁搜載，博采群言，徵顯闡幽，窺見十二公之事；尊王賤伯，講明數千載之前。雖淵微之義或未貫通，而綱常之道庶其有補。兹盖伏遇〇〇〇〇聰明天縱，聖敬日躋；乃武乃文，光復中興之大業；惟精惟一，丕承烈祖之鴻猷。俯萬幾之暇，特賜覽觀；而一得之愚，敢忘報稱？休願
translation_en:
… auspicious signs of Charts and Writings. Examining remote antiquity, You decide from Your imperial heart. Considering that the composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) truly originated with the Uncrowned King [Confucius], amid Your diligence from before dawn until late at night You still trouble Your imperial gaze with it. Its praise and blame are ever strict down to a single word, yet commentaries and annotations often err through narrow specialization; its great principles have been distorted and remain unmanifested, while crooked theories are jumbled together and cannot be distinguished. Wishing to clarify the merits and defects of the Three Commentaries and exclusively investigate the beginning and end of the bequeathed Classic, You have therefore commanded a close minister to compile and explain it anew.

Your servant is deeply ashamed of his shallow learning and of unworthily occupying a place in the pure court ranks. Straining to probe the direct import of former Confucians, I have not yet grasped the essentials of the mind-to-mind transmission beyond the historical record. Therefore I have searched widely through records [?] and gathered extensively from diverse views; verifying the manifest and elucidating the hidden, I have glimpsed the affairs of the twelve dukes; honoring the King and disparaging the hegemons, I have expounded upon events of several thousand years ago. Although its profound and subtle meanings may not yet be thoroughly penetrated, to the Way of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues this may perhaps offer some small aid.

This is because I humbly encounter Your Majesty [〇〇〇〇], whose intelligence and acuity are endowed by Heaven, and whose sage reverence daily ascends; both martial and civil, You gloriously restore the great enterprise of dynastic revival; refined and single-minded, You grandly carry on the vast plans of our Illustrious Ancestors. Condescending in Your leisure from ten thousand affairs of state, You specially bestow Your perusal; how then could my humble wit, with its single insight, dare forget to repay Your grace? I humbly [?] wish that…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
緝熈
聖學川方至而日方升鞏固
皇圖天愈長而地愈久臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所撰春秋傳隨
表上
進以
聞
punctuated: 緝熈聖學，川方至而日方升；鞏固皇圖，天愈長而地愈久。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹以所撰《春秋傳》隨表上進以聞。
translation_en: …continually illuminate Your Sagely Learning, like a stream just arriving in flood and the sun just rising; and consolidate the Imperial Domain, as enduring as heaven and as everlasting as earth. Your servant is overcome with the utmost awe and earnest trepidation in gazing up at Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, and respectfully presents the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu zhuan) that he has composed, accompanying this memorial, for the Imperial attention.

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
策
第一問周瑛
同考試官教諭羅批翩翩五策文彩燁然而此尤傑出者也
故表而出之
考試官學正楊批五策條答無遺此篇事實尤備足
見學識
考試官教諭聶批一策皆隨問而答得士如此可以
謂之文矣
聖君出而繼天立極之功大聖經作而垂世立教之道明欽惟
===
太宗文皇帝萬機之暇采輯傳記得古人為善獲報者百六十五人既
各為論斷以發揚其潜德復為歌詩吟以詠其性情以嘉惠
臣民昭示四海誠為萬世之大寶也執事發策以是下詢承學愚
不敏敢不採摭以對彼其立定大計口不言功丙吉之深厚不
伐也為治循良舉善而教卓茂之視人如子也握兵柄而好生
非鄧禹之出師不殺乎假蒲鞭以示辱非劉寬之臨政温仁
乎又如王忔之彌全營殯非敦義乎嚴譔之平活無辜非
詳審乎李玨之販糴平量敏中之守護遺物范寧之擇嫁
彥賓之還女曹彬之仁惠王祐之公直若水之察誣寃堯佐
punctuated:
策

第一問

周瑛

同考試官教諭羅批：「翩翩五策，文彩燁然，而此尤傑出者也，故表而出之。」

考試官學正楊批：「五策條答無遺，此篇事實尤備，足見學識。」

考試官教諭聶批：「一策皆隨問而答，得士如此，可以謂之文矣。」

聖君出而繼天立極之功大，聖經作而垂世立教之道明。欽惟太宗文皇帝萬機之暇，采輯傳記，得古人為善獲報者百六十五人，既各為論斷以發揚其潜德，復為歌詩吟以詠其性情，以嘉惠臣民，昭示四海，誠為萬世之大寶也。執事發策以是下詢，承學愚不敏，敢不採摭以對？彼其立定大計，口不言功，丙吉之深厚不伐也；為治循良，舉善而教，卓茂之視人如子也；握兵柄而好生，非鄧禹之出師不殺乎？假蒲鞭以示辱，非劉寬之臨政温仁乎？又如王忔之彌全營殯，非敦義乎？嚴譔之平活無辜，非詳審乎？李玨之販糴平量，敏中之守護遺物，范寧之擇嫁，彥賓之還女，曹彬之仁惠，王祐之公直，若水之察誣寃，堯佐
translation_en:
Policy Essays

First Question

Zhou Ying 周瑛

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Luo 羅: "His five graceful policy essays shine with literary brilliance, and this one is especially outstanding; therefore it is singled out for presentation."

Comment by Examiner Director of Studies Yang 楊: "All five policy essays answer point by point without omission, and this piece is especially complete in its historical facts, amply demonstrating his learning and insight."

Comment by Examiner Instructor Nie 聶: "Throughout this policy essay, every point answers the question directly; to obtain a scholar like this may truly be called refined accomplishment."

When a sage ruler arises, great is his achievement in succeeding Heaven and establishing the supreme standard; when a sage classic is composed, clear is its Way in handing down teachings for the world. We reverently reflect upon how Emperor Taizong Wen 太宗文皇帝 (the Yongle Emperor), in his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, gathered and compiled biographies and records, obtaining one hundred and sixty-five men of antiquity who did good and received their reward. Having composed critical evaluations for each to bring forth their hidden virtues, he further wrote songs, poems, and chants to sing of their dispositions and feelings, thereby graciously benefitting his officials and people and making them manifest to the Four Seas—truly a great treasure for ten thousand generations! Since Your Excellency has posed this policy question to inquire of us below, though I, a junior student, am foolish andunclever, how could I dare not gather what I know in reply?

As for settling the great plan of succession while never speaking of his own merit, that was the deep generosity and lack of boasting of Bing Ji 丙吉; governing as a benevolent and upright official, promoting the good and instructing the people, that was Zhuo Mao's 卓茂 regarding the people as his own children. Holding military authority yet loving life—was this not Deng Yu's 鄧禹 leading out armies without indiscriminate killing? Using a rush whip merely to show shame—was this not Liu Kuan's 劉寬 gentle benevolence in administering government? Take also Wang Yin's 王忔 [WangZhi 王忔/王忭?] seeing a friend's illness through to the end and arranging his burial—was this not篤厚 righteousness? Yan Zhuan's 嚴譔 redressing injustices and saving the innocent—was this not careful judicial review? There were also Li Jue's 李玨 selling grain with fair measure, Xiang Minzhong's 向敏中 guarding left-behind property, Fan Ning's 范寧 [or Fan Zhi's?] choosing a proper marriage for an orphan girl, Yanbin's 彥賓 returning a purchased girl, Cao Bin's 曹彬 benevolence and kindness, Wang You's 王祐 fairness and uprightness, Qian Ruoshui's 錢若水 discerning false accusations and wrongs, and Chen Yaozuo's 陳堯佐…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
之興水利具經濟之才蠲屋地之輸非范仲淹李允則其人乎
夜燭治書死獄求生此歐陽觀之留心讞獄也三喪未舉麥
舟相濟此范純仁之推惠朋友也若夫出粟濟人對衆焚券
歲凶發廩米粥賑飢非李謙天福之長者乎造舟濟渡人免
病涉以食施貧人賴全活非宋仁祝染之惠利乎伯林為吏與民
休息嚴實從征活人數萬希憲出鎮荊南人漸德化田滋廉訪
浙西政稱廉能之數君子者所行雖不同而立心之仁則同所
為雖有異而立心之善則無異所謂積陰德於冥冥之中
而顯受陽報者愚生游學庠序敢不佩服
===
聖教倘異日居官臨政亦竊有志於斯執事有以進之幸甚
第二問
卓天錫
考試官學正楊批推原理數敷荅詳明非平昔探求
諸子之蘊者曷克臻此
考試官教諭聶批發策正欲觀士子本領之學理數
之荅詳備可敬
觀諸儒理數之言當求諸儒理數之㫖甚矣理數之學不可以不
講也觀諸儒之言雖有不同求其所論之㫖又豈不各有攸當哉
punctuated:
之興水利。具經濟之才，蠲屋地之輸，非范仲淹、李允則其人乎？夜燭治書，死獄求生，此歐陽觀之留心讞獄也；三喪未舉，麥舟相濟，此范純仁之推惠朋友也。若夫出粟濟人，對衆焚券，歲凶發廩，米粥賑飢，非李謙、天福之長者乎？造舟濟渡，人免病涉，以食施貧，人賴全活，非宋仁、祝染之惠利乎？伯林為吏，與民休息；嚴實從征，活人數萬；希憲出鎮荊南，人漸德化；田滋廉訪浙西，政稱廉能。之數君子者，所行雖不同，而立心之仁則同；所為雖有異，而立心之善則無異。所謂積陰德於冥冥之中，而顯受陽報者。愚生游學庠序，敢不佩服聖教！倘異日居官臨政，亦竊有志於斯，執事有以進之，幸甚。

第二問
卓天錫
考試官學正楊批：推原理數，敷荅詳明，非平昔探求諸子之蘊者，曷克臻此！
考試官教諭聶批：發策正欲觀士子本領之學，理數之荅，詳備可敬。

觀諸儒理數之言，當求諸儒理數之㫖。甚矣，理數之學不可以不講也！觀諸儒之言雖有不同，求其所論之㫖，又豈不各有攸當哉？
translation_en:
… promotion of waterworks. And as for possessing the talent for ordering the state and relieving the people, and remitting the taxes on houses and land—were those men not Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹 and Li Yunze 李允則? Examining documents by candlelight at night to seek a way for those in capital cases to live—this was Ouyang Guan's 歐陽觀 careful attention to adjudicating lawsuits. Parting with a boatload of wheat to help someone who had three unburied dead in his family—this was Fan Chunren's 范純仁 extending kindness to friends. And as for bringing out grain to relieve people and burning loan tallies before the crowd, or opening granaries in years of famine to relieve the starving with rice gruel—were these not the magnanimous deeds of Li Qian 李謙 and Tianfu 天福 [Dou Tianfu 竇天福]? Building boats to ferry people across so that they were spared the hardship of wading, and bestowing food upon the poor so that people relied on it to survive intact—were these not the beneficent acts of Song Ren 宋仁 and Zhu Ran 祝染 [? ZhuQs/Zhu Gong 祝公]? Bolin 伯林 [Zhang Bolin 張伯林] served as an official and gave the people rest and recuperation; Yan Shi 嚴實 followed on military campaigns and saved the lives of tens of thousands; Xixian 希憲 [Lian Xixian 廉希憲] went out to garrison Jingnan, and the people were gradually transformed by virtue; Tian Zi 田滋 served as Surveillance Commissioner in Zhexi, and his governance was praised for its integrity and capability. Although the actions of these several noble men were not the same, the benevolence of their intentions was identical; although their deeds differed, the goodness of their intentions was no different. They were what is meant by accumulating hidden virtue in the unseen realm and manifestly receiving visible rewards. As a foolish student studying in the state schools, how could I dare not take to heart the sacred teachings! Should I one day hold office and oversee governance, I too would privately aspire to this. I would be most fortunate if Your Excellency would advance and guide me in it.

Question 2
Zhuo Tianxi 卓天錫
Examiner and Director of Studies Yang 楊 comments: He traces the origins of principle and number, setting forth his answer with detailed clarity. Were he not one who in ordinary times explored the profundities of the various masters, how could he attain this!
Examiner and Instructor Nie 聶 comments: In posing the policy question, the intention was precisely to observe the candidates' fundamental learning. His answer on principle and number is detailed, thorough, and worthy of respect.

When examining the words of the various Confucian scholars on principle and number, one ought to seek the underlying meaning of those scholars regarding principle and number. Indeed, the study of principle and number cannot go unexamined! Although the words of the various scholars differ when we examine them, if we seek the underlying meaning of what they discuss, how could each not be fitting in its own right? …

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
請因明問而畧陳之周子太極一圖剖析精微易通一書又所以
法此圖者也盖圖有太極書則以誠發之太極本無極書則以
誠無為著之圖之陽動即書所謂誠之源也圖之陰靜即書
所謂誠之立也陽變陰合而生水火木金土即誠通誠復而為
元亨利貞者也善惡一陰陽也仁義禮智信一五行也圖書相
為表裏者如此易有太極而圖言無極盖易之言有以理言也
圖之言無以形言也曰無曰有同此理耳豈太極之外復有無
極者哉至於古書有所謂太一者盖以其無二則曰一以其至極
則曰極其與太極名雖殊而義則一也若所謂太易未見氣
===
太初氣之始太始形之始太素質之始是以氣形質言之而非
指乎此理矣豈可與太極同論哉程子學於周子其圖親得
手授之傳著書立言傳道解惑而未嘗有一言及於圖者盖
以圖之立象盡意周子不得已而作也觀其手授之意惟程子
為能當之至程子而不言則疑其未有能受之者爾至若西
銘正蒙張子所著西銘統而論之乾父坤母民胞物與理之
一也然曰人曰物其分殊矣分而論之則大君而宗子大臣而家
相以至於煢獨鰥寡皆吾之兄弟顛連而無告者亦理之一
也然以必各親其親各長其長而後有以及人之親長則其
punctuated: 請因明問而畧陳之。周子《太極》一圖，剖析精微；《易通》一書，又所以法此圖者也。盖圖有太極，書則以誠發之；太極本無極，書則以誠無為著之。圖之陽動，即書所謂誠之源也；圖之陰靜，即書所謂誠之立也；陽變陰合而生水、火、木、金、土，即誠通、誠復而為元、亨、利、貞者也。善惡，一陰陽也；仁、義、禮、智、信，一五行也。圖、書相為表裏者如此。《易》有太極，而圖言無極，盖《易》之言有，以理言也；圖之言無，以形言也。曰無曰有，同此理耳，豈太極之外復有無極者哉？至於古書有所謂太一者，盖以其無二則曰一，以其至極則曰極，其與太極名雖殊而義則一也。若所謂太易未見氣、太初氣之始、太始形之始、太素質之始，是以氣、形、質言之，而非指乎此理矣，豈可與太極同論哉？程子學於周子，其圖親得手授之傳，著書立言，傳道解惑，而未嘗有一言及於圖者，盖以圖之立象盡意，周子不得已而作也。觀其手授之意，惟程子為能當之；至程子而不言，則疑其未有能受之者爾。至若《西銘》、《正蒙》，張子所著。《西銘》統而論之：乾父坤母，民胞物與，理之一也；然曰人曰物，其分殊矣。分而論之：則大君而宗子，大臣而家相，以至於煢獨鰥寡，皆吾之兄弟顛連而無告者，亦理之一也；然以必各親其親、各長其長，而後有以及人之親長，則其
translation_en:
Allow me to briefly set this forth in response to Your insightful question. Master Zhou’s [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤] single Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu) analyzes the subtle and minute, while his book Penetrating the Book of Changes (Yitong [Tongshu]) is in turn modeled upon this diagram. For where the Diagram has the Supreme Ultimate, the Book elucidates it through "sincerity" (cheng); where the Supreme Ultimate is fundamentally the Ultimateless (wuji), the Book makes this manifest through "sincerity engaging in no-action" (cheng wuwei). The movement of yang in the Diagram is what the Book calls the "source of sincerity"; the stillness of yin in the Diagram is what the Book calls the "establishment of sincerity"; the transformation of yang and the union of yin generating Water, Fire, Wood, Metal, and Earth correspond to the "penetration of sincerity" and the "return of sincerity" becoming origination (yuan), flourishing (heng), advantage (li), and firmness (zhen). Good and evil are simply yin and yang; humaneness, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness are simply the Five Phases. Such is the way the Diagram and the Book serve as outer and inner aspects of each other.

The Book of Changes (Yi) states that there is a Supreme Ultimate, whereas the Diagram speaks of the Ultimateless. This is because when the Changes speaks of "having" [the Supreme Ultimate], it speaks in terms of principle (li); when the Diagram speaks of "non-being" [the Ultimateless], it speaks in terms of physical form (xing). Whether called non-being or being, it is this same principle; how could there be an Ultimateless existing apart from the Supreme Ultimate? As for what ancient books call the Supreme One (Taiyi), because it has no second it is called "One," and because it reaches the ultimate limit it is called "Ultimate"; although its name differs from the Supreme Ultimate, the meaning is one and the same. As for what are called the Great Change (Taiyi) before qi is visible, the Great Inception (Taichu) as the beginning of qi, the Great Beginning (Taishi) as the beginning of form, and the Great Simplicity (Taisu) as the beginning of substance—these are spoken of in terms of qi, form, and substance, and do not point to this principle. How could they be discussed on the same level as the Supreme Ultimate?

The Masters Cheng [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤] studied under Master Zhou and personally received the transmission of his Diagram from his own hand. Yet in writing books and establishing their teachings to transmit the Way and resolve doubts, they never once mentioned the Diagram. This was because the Diagram’s establishment of images to exhaust meaning was something Master Zhou created only out of necessity. Viewing his intention in personally handing it down, only the Masters Cheng were worthy of receiving it; when it came to the Masters Cheng and they did not speak of it, they seguramente suspected there was not yet anyone capable of receiving it.

As for the Western Inscription (Ximing) and Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng), they were written by Master Zhang [Zhang Zai 張載]. If we discuss the Western Inscription as a whole: Heaven (Qian) is the father and Earth (Kun) is the mother, the people are my womb-fellows and things are my companions—this is the oneness of principle (li zhi yi). Yet in speaking of "people" and "things," their allotments differ (fen shu). If we discuss it in terms of distinctions: that the great sovereign is the eldest son of the lineage, the great ministers are his household stewards, and down to the solitary, orphaned, widowed, and childless, all are my brothers who have fallen into distress and have no one to appeal to—this too is the oneness of principle. title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
分未嘗不殊矣分殊之中理之一者固未嘗不寓而理一之中不
害其為分之殊也程子之言可謂一言以蔽之矣又謂其書推
理以存義與孟子性善之論同功信夫楊中立謂其言體而
不及用未免流於兼愛者是烏足以知西銘者哉正蒙語造
化則極乎日月寒暑之變語鬼神則極乎二氣良能之妙
語陰陽則一神兩化之論備焉語性命則太虛氣化之論詳
焉合而論之西銘之理一即圖之所以發太極陰陽之蘊也是
則太極也易通也西銘也正蒙也同乎一理也故曰四者理學
之源也先天經世邵子所著先天有變象者則寒暑晝夜
===
比象者則風雨露雷感象則性情形體應象則飛走草木
此象之不一也有往數者已生之卦由左而旋來數者未生之
卦由右而轉陰數起於十二陽數起於三十此數之不一也經
世之數起乎四本之以元會運世主之以日月星辰配之以春
夏秋冬參之以皇帝王伯又所以發明此圖者也然先天
也經世也皆主數言而太極獨以理言數之與理若相戾
矣殊不知理者數之本源數者理之妙用合而言之則未始
相離也先儒謂論其義理則先天不如太極之精而約其
言信夫陳瑩中指先天之易為心法是已後来者反名其
punctuated: 分未嘗不殊矣。分殊之中，理之一者固未嘗不寓；而理一之中，不害其為分之殊也。程子之言，可謂一言以蔽之矣。又謂其書推理以存義，與孟子性善之論同功，信夫！楊中立謂其言體而不及用，未免流於兼愛者，是烏足以知《西銘》者哉？《正蒙》語造化，則極乎日月寒暑之變；語鬼神，則極乎二氣良能之妙；語陰陽，則一神兩化之論備焉；語性命，則太虛氣化之論詳焉。合而論之，《西銘》之理一，即《圖》之所以發太極陰陽之蘊也。是則《太極》也、《易通》也、《西銘》也、《正蒙》也，同乎一理也。故曰四者理學之源也。《先天》、《經世》，邵子所著。《先天》有變象者，則寒暑晝夜；比象者，則風雨露雷；感象，則性情形體；應象，則飛走草木：此象之不一也。有往數者，已生之卦由左而旋；來數者，未生之卦由右而轉；陰數起於十二，陽數起於三十：此數之不一也。《經世》之數起乎四，本之以元會運世，主之以日月星辰，配之以春夏秋冬，參之以皇帝王伯，又所以發明此圖者也。然《先天》也、《經世》也，皆主數言，而《太極》獨以理言，數之與理若相戾矣。殊不知理者數之本源，數者理之妙用，合而言之，則未始相離也。先儒謂論其義理，則《先天》不如《太極》之精而約，其言信夫！陳瑩中指《先天》之《易》為心法，是已；後来者反名其
translation_en: …allotments are never without differentiation. Within the differentiation of allotments, the unity of principle is certainly never absent; and within the unity of principle, there is no hindrance to the differentiation of allotments. Master Cheng’s words may be said to sum it up in a single phrase. He also said that this work deduces principle in order to preserve righteousness, achieving the same merit as Mencius’s discourse on the goodness of human nature—truly so! When Yang Zhongli (Yang Shi 楊時) claimed that it speaks of substance without reaching function and inevitably lapses into Mohist universal love, how could that be sufficient to understand the Western Inscription (Ximing)? As for Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng), when it speaks of creative transformation, it exhausts the changes of sun and moon, cold and heat; when it speaks of ghosts and spirits, it exhausts the subtlety of the innate efficacy of the two vital forces (qi); when it speaks of yin and yang, the discourse on the one spirit and two transformations is complete therein; when it speaks of human nature and destiny, the discourse on the Great Vacuity and the transformation of vital force is detailed therein. Considered together, the unity of principle in the Western Inscription is precisely that by which the Diagram (Taijitu) reveals the profound store of the Supreme Ultimate and of yin and yang. Thus the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taijitu), the Penetrating the Book of Changes (Yitong / Tongshu), the Western Inscription (Ximing), and Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng) all share a single principle. Therefore it is said that these four are the source of the Learning of Principle (lixue). The Former Heaven Diagram (Xiantian) and the Supreme Principles Governing the World (Huangji jingshi) were written by Master Shao (Shao Yong 邵雍). In the Former Heaven Diagram, there are images of change, which are cold and heat, day and night; images of correspondence, which are wind, rain, dew, and thunder; images of stimulus, which are nature, emotion, form, and body; and images of response, which are birds, beasts, grasses, and trees—this is the diversity of its images. There are numbers of the past, whereby the hexagrams already generated revolve from the left; numbers of the future, whereby the hexagrams not yet generated turn from the right; the yin numbers begin at twelve, and the yang numbers begin at thirty—this is the diversity of its numbers. The numbers of the Supreme Principles Governing the World begin with four: grounded in Epoch (yuan), Conjunction (hui), Revolution (yun), and Generation (shi); governed by the sun, moon, stars, and zodiacal spaces; matched with spring, summer, autumn, and winter; and integrated with August Sovereign (huang), Emperor (di), King (wang), and Hegemon (ba)—which in turn serves to elucidate this diagram. Yet the Former Heaven Diagram and the Supreme Principles Governing the World both speak primarily in terms of numbers, whereas the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate speaks solely in terms of principle, so that number and principle might seem to be at odds with one another. Little do people realize that principle is the fundamental source of number, and number is the wondrous function of principle; spoken of together, they have never been separate. Earlier Confucians said that in discussing moral principle, the Former Heaven Diagram is not as fine and concise as the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate—how true those words are! title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
書為考數又烏足以知先天者哉然雖衆論紛紜得失殊致
不有朱夫子無極之辨通書之解西銘正蒙之訓釋皇極經
世之考正又何以會諸書而同一理合三子而同一心哉噫數君
子之書固皆有功於世而朱子又有功於數君子之書也歟敢
以是為復
第五問
許評
同考試官教諭鮑批事有考究文有波瀾允為策手
考試官學正楊批策有事實可取
===
考試官教諭聶批此問鮮能詳答惟此篇明備足
見博識
嘗謂制治莫善於訓兵訓兵莫先於擇將盖兵者國之
衞而將者兵之帥者不訓兵則無以衞其國不擇將又何以帥
其兵哉執事發策以戎兵下詢承學愚雖不敏敢不撫其
所問以對乎且戎兵者國之大事周公之於成王必以詰爾
戎兵為訓召公之於康王必以張皇六師為戒故戎兵者
誠制治保邦之良法而士君子之所當講也夫周制三軍
非前軍中軍後軍乎周禮六軍非伍兩卒旅師軍乎軒
punctuated:
書為考數，又烏足以知《先天》者哉？然雖衆論紛紜，得失殊致，不有朱夫子無極之辨、《通書》之解、《西銘》《正蒙》之訓釋、《皇極經世》之考正，又何以會諸書而同一理，合三子而同一心哉？噫！數君子之書，固皆有功於世，而朱子又有功於數君子之書也歟！敢以是為復。
第五問
許評
同考試官教諭鮑批：事有考究，文有波瀾，允為策手。
考試官學正楊批：策有事實，可取。
考試官教諭聶批：此問鮮能詳答，惟此篇明備，足見博識。
嘗謂制治莫善於訓兵，訓兵莫先於擇將。盖兵者，國之衞，而將者，兵之帥。者不訓兵，則無以衞其國；不擇將，又何以帥其兵哉？執事發策，以戎兵下詢承學，愚雖不敏，敢不撫其所問以對乎？且戎兵者，國之大事。周公之於成王，必以「詰爾戎兵」為訓；召公之於康王，必以「張皇六師」為戒。故戎兵者，誠制治保邦之良法，而士君子之所當講也。夫周制三軍，非前軍、中軍、後軍乎？《周禮》六軍，非伍、兩、卒、旅、師、軍乎？軒…
translation_en:
… book as an "investigation of numbers" (kaoshu), how could they possibly suffice to understand the Prior to Heaven (Xiantian)? Yet even though the multitude of discussions are tangled and confused, with their hits and misses leading to different conclusions, were it not for Master Zhu's [Zhu Xi's] differentiation of the Supreme Polarity and Non-Polarity (Wuji), his commentary on the Penetrating the Book of Changes (Tongshu), his explications of the Western Inscription (Ximing) and Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng), and his critical emendations of the Supreme Principles Governing the World (Huangji jingshi), how could one bring together all these books and unite them in a single principle, or join the three masters and unite them in a single mind? Alas! The writings of these several gentlemen have indeed all rendered meritorious service to the world, and has not Master Zhu in turn rendered meritorious service to the writings of these several gentlemen? I venture to offer this in reply.

Fifth Question
Xu Ping 許評
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Bao comments: The facts are well researched and the prose has surging momentum; truly a master of the policy essay.
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng) Yang comments: The policy essay is grounded in factual substance and is worthy of selection.
Examiner, Instructor Nie comments: Few were able to answer this question in detail; this essay alone is clear and comprehensive, amply demonstrating broad learning.

I have always held that in establishing good governance, nothing is better than training troops, and in training troops, nothing takes precedence over selecting generals. For troops are the guard of the state, while generals are the commanders of the troops. If [? reading 者 as 若] one does not train troops, there is no way to guard the state; if one does not select generals, how then can one command the troops? Since Your Excellency has posed this policy question, inquiring of us students about military affairs and weaponry, though I am dull-witted, how dare I not gather up what has been asked in order to reply? Moreover, military affairs and weaponry are a great matter of the state. When the Duke of Zhou addressed King Cheng, he unfailingly instructed him to "look well to your weapons of war"; when the Duke of Shao addressed King Kang, he unfailingly admonished him to "make grand Your Majesty's Six Armies." Therefore, military affairs and weaponry are truly a fine method for establishing governance and preserving the state, and something that scholar-gentlemen ought to study and discuss. Now, as for the Three Armies of the Zhou system, were they not the Vanguard Army, the Center Army, and the Rear Army? And as for the Six Armies of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), were they not formed from the squad of five (wu), the platoon of twenty-five (liang), the company of one hundred (zu), the battalion of five hundred (lü), the division of twenty-five hundred (shi), and the army of twelve thousand five hundred (jun)? title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
轅之五行曰直陣銳陣圓陣方陣曲陣是也風后之八陣曰
天地風雲虎翼蛇蟠飛龍鳥翔是也方圓牝牡衝方罘罝
車輪鴈行則孫子之八陣為可知洞當中黃龍騰鳥翔連
衡握機虎翼折衝則孔明之八陣又可見至若李靖之中軍
左虞候右虞候左一廂右一廂左二廂右二廂不謂之六花
陣歟大黑大赤青蛇白雲左突右擊前衝後衝摧兇决勝
破敵先鋒不謂之十二陣歟然歷代兵法既陳矣若夫勇
智福者將之三等勇智仁信忠者將之五材五慎五危
者理備果戒約必死必生忿疾廉潔愛民也三道三急者
===
正兵竒兵伏兵得地形卒服習器用利也有所謂鼓金旗之
三官鼙鼓金鐸旌旗麾幟禁令刑罰之三威者焉有所謂
氣地事力之四機整兵習陣趨食嚴令就行之五鼓者焉形
色之旗號令之數進退之度長短之利賞罰之信則五教
之訓練為何如目習耳習心習手習足習則五習之教令又
何似五事者道天地將法之謂五法者度量數称勝之謂
因内反死生非五間乎人積輜庫隊非火五攻乎他如人正辭
巧火水兵之七政權謀形勢陰陽技巧之四種形勢情之
决勝三術争交衝重之類九地其將兵又歷歷可得而言
punctuated: 轅之五行，曰直陣、銳陣、圓陣、方陣、曲陣是也；風后之八陣，曰天、地、風、雲、虎翼、蛇蟠、飛龍、鳥翔是也。方、圓、牝、牡、衝方、罘罝、車輪、鴈行，則孫子之八陣為可知；洞當、中黃、龍騰、鳥翔、連衡、握機、虎翼、折衝，則孔明之八陣又可見。至若李靖之中軍、左虞候、右虞候、左一廂、右一廂、左二廂、右二廂，不謂之六花陣歟？大黑、大赤、青蛇、白雲、左突、右擊、前衝、後衝、摧兇、决勝、破敵、先鋒，不謂之十二陣歟？然歷代兵法既陳矣，若夫勇、智、福者，將之三等；勇、智、仁、信、忠者，將之五材。五慎、五危者，理、備、果、戒、約，必死、必生、忿疾、廉潔、愛民也。三道、三急者，正兵、竒兵、伏兵，得地形、卒服習、器用利也。有所謂鼓、金、旗之三官，鼙鼓金鐸、旌旗麾幟、禁令刑罰之三威者焉；有所謂氣、地、事、力之四機，整兵、習陣、趨食、嚴令、就行之五鼓者焉。形色之旗、號令之數、進退之度、長短之利、賞罰之信，則五教之訓練為何如；目習、耳習、心習、手習、足習，則五習之教令又何似。五事者，道、天、地、將、法之謂；五法者，度、量、數、称、勝之謂。因、内、反、死、生，非五間乎？人、積、輜、庫、隊，非火五攻乎？他如人、正、辭、巧、火、水、兵之七政，權謀、形勢、陰陽、技巧之四種，形、勢、情之决勝三術，争、交、衝、重之類九地，其將兵又歷歷可得而言…
translation_en:
… [Xuanyuan]’s Five Elements: namely, the Straight Formation, Pointed Formation, Circular Formation, Square Formation, and Curved Formation; and Fenghou’s风后 Eight Formations: namely, Heaven, Earth, Wind, Cloud, Tiger Wing, Coiled Serpent, Flying Dragon, and Soaring Bird. From Square, Circular, Female, Male, Assaulting Square, Netting, Chariot Wheel, and Wild Geese in Flight, Sunzi’s孫子 Eight Formations may be known; from Piercing Center (Dongdang), Central Yellow, Leaping Dragon, Soaring Bird, Horizontal Alliance (Lianheng), Grasping the Mechanism (Woji), Tiger Wing, and Repelling Assault (Zhechong), Kongming’s孔明 [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮] Eight Formations may likewise be seen. As for Li Jing’s李靖 Central Army, Left Patrol (Zuoyuhou), Right Patrol (Youyuhou), Left First Wing, Right First Wing, Left Second Wing, and Right Second Wing—is this not called the Six-Petal Formation? And Great Black, Great Red, Green Serpent, White Cloud, Left Thrust, Right Strike, Front Assault, Rear Assault, Crushing the Fierce, Deciding Victory, Breaking the Enemy, and Vanguard—are these not called the Twelve Formations?

Now that the military methods of successive dynasties have been set forth: Courage, Wisdom, and Good Fortune are the Three Grades of a general; Courage, Wisdom, Benevolence, Trustworthiness, and Loyalty are the Five Qualities of a general. The Five Cautions and Five Dangers are Principle, Preparedness, Resoluteness, Vigilance, and Simplicity; and Recklessness Unto Death, Clinging to Life, Quickness to Anger, Obsession with Purity, and Excessive Compassion for the People. The Three Ways and Three Urgencies are Regular Troops, Surprise Troops, and Ambush Troops; and Gaining the Terrain, Troops Accustomed to Discipline, and Sharpness of Weapons and Equipment. There are what are called the Three Officers of Drums, Bells, and Flags, and the Three Awesomenesses of War-Drums and Metal Bells, Banners and Pennants, and Prohibitions and Punishments; there are what are called the Four Pivots of Morale, Terrain, Affairs, and Strength, and the Five Drum-Signals for Mustering Troops, Practicing Formations, Taking Meals, Enforcing Orders, and Marching in Ranks. How goes the training of the Five Instructions—banners of distinct shapes and colors, the tallies of commands, the measures of advance and retreat, the advantages of long and short weapons, and trustworthiness in rewards and punishments? And what are the drill orders of the Five Habituations—training the eyes, training the ears, training the mind, training the hands, and training the feet? The Five Factors refer to the Way, Heaven, Earth, the General, and Method; the Five Measurements refer to Measurement, Estimation, Calculation, Balancing, and Victory. Are not Local, Inside, Doubled, Doomed, and Surviving the Five Spies? Are not Personnel, Stores, Supply Wagons, Arsenals, and Formations the Five Fire Attacks? As for other matters—such as the Seven Administrations of Men, Rectitude, Words, Ingenuity, Fire, Water, and Weapons; the Four Categories of Military Treatises: StrategicCalculation, Disposition and Momentum, Yin-Yang, and Technical Skills; the Three Arts of Deciding Victory through Form, Momentum, and Sentiment; and the Nine Terrains such as Contentious, Intersecting, Focal, and Serious—all these principles of commanding troops can be enumerated one by one…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
矣我
朝擇將用兵超軼前代內而衛國都外而捍疆場士氣銳鎧仗
精使將得人兵練有法則雖荒遠之地岩險之邦如前之陣
勢講而行之無施不可若夫料敵制勝隨時應機責在主
帥愚生管見軍旅未閑惟執事進而教之幸甚
punctuated: 矣。我朝擇將用兵，超軼前代，內而衛國都，外而捍疆場，士氣銳，鎧仗精。使將得人，兵練有法，則雖荒遠之地、岩險之邦，如前之陣勢，講而行之，無施不可。若夫料敵制勝，隨時應機，責在主帥。愚生管見，軍旅未閑，惟執事進而教之，幸甚。
translation_en: … Our dynasty's selection of commanders and employment of troops surpass those of former eras: internally guarding the imperial capital and externally defending the frontiers, with keen troop morale and refined armor and weaponry. If the right men are obtained as commanders and the troops are trained with proper method, then even in remote, desolate lands and precipitous regions, should battle formations such as those mentioned above be studied and put into practice, there is nowhere they cannot be effectively applied. As for assessing the enemy to secure victory and responding to opportunities according to the moment, the responsibility lies with the commander-in-chief. As a foolish student of narrow vision, I am unversed in military affairs; I only hope that Your Excellency will bring me forward and instruct me, which would be most fortunate.

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試小錄後序
景星慶雲麒麟鳳凰人知其為文明之祥太平之瑞也而
不知賢才輩出弼亮化工鼓舞至治有關乎氣運之
盛實
天下國家之祥瑞焉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝受
天明命統有萬方大興學校設置賢科當時賢俊奮登
際雲龍風虎之亨嘉固泰山磐石之基業
列聖相承益隆化理敷求賢哲茂篤成功迄今迨將百
===
年我
皇上纘承丕緒誕敷文教華夷率俾海岳效靈是固
聖化之自然亦賢才翊贊之所致也然猶慮用賢未廣於
是三年大比開取士之額以網羅天下豪傑益欲恢
宏至治垂萬億年太平之統廼景泰四年適藩鄉舉
得士之文且賢者凡若干人小錄成僉謂宜序惟治
道固本乎賢才而賢才實關乎氣運方今
氣運全盛之日正賢才效用之時生斯世也與斯選也
何其榮且幸歟雖然繼今以往尚當益勵廼學懋廼
punctuated:
福建鄉試小錄後序

景星慶雲、麒麟鳳凰，人知其為文明之祥、太平之瑞也，而不知賢才輩出，弼亮化工，鼓舞至治，有關乎氣運之盛，實天下國家之祥瑞焉。洪惟我太祖高皇帝受天明命，統有萬方，大興學校，設置賢科。當時賢俊奮登，際雲龍風虎之亨嘉，固泰山磐石之基業。列聖相承，益隆化理，敷求賢哲，茂篤成功，迄今迨將百年。我皇上纘承丕緒，誕敷文教，華夷率俾，海岳效靈，是固聖化之自然，亦賢才翊贊之所致也。然猶慮用賢未廣，於是三年大比，開取士之額，以網羅天下豪傑，益欲恢宏至治，垂萬億年太平之統。廼景泰四年，適藩鄉舉得士之文且賢者凡若干人。小錄成，僉謂宜序。惟治道固本乎賢才，而賢才實關乎氣運。方今氣運全盛之日，正賢才效用之時。生斯世也，與斯選也，何其榮且幸歟！雖然，繼今以往，尚當益勵廼學，懋廼
translation_en:
Postface to the Brief Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

Auspicious stars and felicitous clouds, unicorns (qilin) and phoenixes (fenghuang)—people know that these are omens of civilizing brilliance and portents of Great Peace. Yet they do not know that when worthy talents emerge in succession to assist and illuminate the transformative work of creation and to inspire supreme governance, this is bound up with the flourishing of the cosmic destiny and is truly the auspicious portent of the empire and the state.

Reflecting upon our Grand Progenitor the High Emperor (Taizu), he received the bright mandate of Heaven and united the myriad regions under his rule, greatly expanding schools and establishing the examination categories for the worthy. At that time, worthies and men of outstanding talent rose up eagerly, meeting the propitious confluence of clouds following the dragon and winds following the tiger, and consolidating a dynastic foundation as firm as Mount Tai and great bedrock. Successive Sacred Emperors inherited the line, further exalting transformative governance, broadly seeking out the worthy and wise, and richly consolidating their achievements, until now nearly a hundred years have passed.

Our August Emperor has succeeded to the great patrimony and widely spread civil teachings. Chinese and non-Chinese alike submit and follow, and the seas and sacred peaks manifest their numinous efficacy. While this is assuredly the natural outcome of sacred transformation, it is also brought about by the supportive assistance of worthy talents. Even so, still concerned that the employment of worthies is not yet sufficiently broad, in the triennial great competition he has expanded the quota for selecting scholars in order to gather in the outstanding heroes of the empire, wishing all the more to enlarge supreme governance and hand down a lineage of Great Peace for myriad tens of thousands of years.

Now, in the fourth year of the Jingtai reign (1453), at the Provincial Examination in this province, a certain number of scholars who are both literary and worthy have been obtained. The brief record having been completed, all said that there ought to be a postface.

Indeed, the way of governance is assuredly rooted in worthy talents, and worthy talents are truly bound up with the cosmic destiny. Right now, a day when the cosmic destiny is in full flourishing is precisely the time for worthy talents to render their service. To be born in this age and to be included in this selection—how glorious and fortunate it is! Even so, from this time onward, they should all the more diligently encourage their learning and cultivate their…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
德捷
春官對
大廷以黼藻
鴻猷笙簧治道為我
國家賢良之輔俾世之人目為文明之祥太平之瑞如
景星慶雲之昭于雲漢麒麟鳳凰之出於郊藪其榮
其幸不既又大乎哉序以伺之
景泰癸酉秋八月既望
山東兗州府東平州儒學學正楊𤣾序
punctuated:
德，捷春官，對大廷，以黼藻鴻猷，笙簧治道，為我國家賢良之輔，俾世之人目為文明之祥、太平之瑞，如景星慶雲之昭于雲漢，麒麟鳳凰之出於郊藪，其榮其幸，不既又大乎哉！序以伺之。
景泰癸酉秋八月既望
山東兗州府東平州儒學學正楊𤣾序
translation_en:
…virtue, triumph in the Metropolitan Examination under the Ministry of Rites, and present their responses in the Palace Examination at the Great Court, so as to adorn the grand imperial enterprise like embroidered robes and give harmonious voice to the way of governance like reed-pipe music. Thus they will serve as worthy and capable coadjutors to our State, causing the people of the world to regard them as auspicious tokens of cultural flourishing and felicitous omens of Great Peace—just like auspicious stars and propitious clouds shining in the Milky Way, or the qilin and the phoenix appearing in the suburban marshes. Will not their glory and their good fortune then be even greater! I write this preface and await it.

On the sixteenth day of the eighth month in the autumn of the guiyou year of the Jingtai reign (September 18, 1453).

Preface by Yang Yu 楊𤣾, Subprefectural Director of Studies of the Confucian School of Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong.
