Therefore, benevolence is centered on love, and no love is greater than loving one's parents. When a person can fully realize his heart of loving his parents, the application of benevolence will not lose its proper order. Yet if benevolence is not first applied to filial piety, how could it be called the virtue of benevolence? Ritual propriety is centered on reverence, and no reverence comes before revering one's parents. When a person can carry out the rites of revering his parents, the function of ritual propriety will surely fulfill its substance. Yet if ritual propriety cannot be practiced in filial piety, how could it be called the virtue of ritual propriety? As for righteousness, which means conforming to what is appropriate: if one does not follow what principle naturally requires and instead leads one's parents into unrighteousness, then the virtue of righteousness will surely be impaired; thus righteousness is nothing other than acting appropriately in filial piety. And as for trustworthiness, which means being genuine: if one cannot make genuine [?] what issues from one's mind and instead serves one's parents with insincerity, then the virtue of trustworthiness will surely become false; thus trustworthiness is nothing other than being genuine in filial piety. Yet what are called benevolence…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
曰禮固行於孝矣尤必始終一心而無始勤終怠之失則可謂之強以強此孝
焉曰義曰信亦施於孝矣尤必先後一致而有自強不息之意斯可謂之
強此孝焉吁資衆德以成一孝頼一勇以全衆德則人子事親之道不其至
歟大抵孝者衆德之本人心同然之理也置之而塞乎天地溥之而横乎
四海者此孝也施諸後世而無朝夕者亦此孝也昔吾夫子謂其為德
之本而教之所由生夫豈不信
唯賢者能盡祭之義賢者之祭也必受其福
張德瑄
同考試官教諭黎批祭統題講雖可為而破難下手此作
===
講旣詳贍而破尤簡健本經之冠匪此其誰
考試官學正揚批此題義與福字作者多不能識惟此
篇體認得實宜冠本經
考試官教諭聶批說者於祭必受福處多指五福惟此
篇甚合本旨其亦熟於經者乎
觀君子之於祭以其義獨能盡而福必能受也盖無所不順者福之名
以物將心者祭之義君子之於祭旣能獨盡其義則其於祭之前豈
不能必受其福哉今夫祭禮之行貴乎有心而後有物也但世之忘
其心者固多徇於物者不少惟君子之祭感春雨之旣濡其怵惕之
punctuated:
曰禮，固行於孝矣，尤必始終一心，而無始勤終怠之失，則可謂之強以強此孝焉；曰義、曰信，亦施於孝矣，尤必先後一致，而有自強不息之意，斯可謂之強此孝焉。吁！資衆德以成一孝，頼一勇以全衆德，則人子事親之道不其至歟？大抵孝者，衆德之本，人心同然之理也。置之而塞乎天地，溥之而横乎四海者，此孝也；施諸後世而無朝夕者，亦此孝也。昔吾夫子謂其為德之本，而教之所由生，夫豈不信！
「唯賢者能盡祭之義，賢者之祭也，必受其福。」
張德瑄
同考試官教諭黎批：祭統題講雖可為，而破難下手。此作講旣詳贍，而破尤簡健，本經之冠，匪此其誰？
考試官學正揚批：此題義與福字，作者多不能識，惟此篇體認得實，宜冠本經。
考試官教諭聶批：說者於「祭必受福」處，多指五福，惟此篇甚合本旨，其亦熟於經者乎！
觀君子之於祭，以其義獨能盡，而福必能受也。盖無所不順者，福之名；以物將心者，祭之義。君子之於祭，旣能獨盡其義，則其於祭之前，豈不能必受其福哉？今夫祭禮之行，貴乎有心而後有物也。但世之忘其心者固多，徇於物者不少。惟君子之祭，感春雨之旣濡，其怵惕之
translation_en:
… and ritual propriety are indeed practiced in filial piety, yet one must especially remain of one mind from beginning to end without the fault of being diligent at first and lax at the end—then this may be called strength, strengthening this filial piety. Righteousness and trustworthiness are likewise applied in filial piety, yet one must especially remain consistent from start to finish with the intent of unceasing self-strengthening—then this may be called strengthening this filial piety. Ah! Drawing upon the multitude of virtues to accomplish the single virtue of filial piety, and relying upon the single virtue of courage to perfect the multitude of virtues—is not the way a filial son serves his parents thus at its ultimate height? On the whole, filial piety is the root of all virtues and the principle shared alike by all human hearts. Set it up and it fills heaven and earth; spread it wide and it extends across the four seas—such is this filial piety. Hand it down to future generations and it knows no cease morning or evening—such too is this filial piety. Long ago our Master said that it is the root of virtue and that from which teaching grows; how could that not be true!

"Only the worthy can fulfill the meaning of sacrifice; in his sacrifices, the worthy is certain to receive blessing."
Zhang Dexuan 張德瑄
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Li 黎: On a topic from the Summary of Sacrifices (Jitong 祭統), although the exposition can be managed, the opening statement of the theme (po 破) is hard to approach. In this essay, the exposition is detailed and rich, while the opening statement is especially concise and vigorous. To head the list for this Classic—if not this essay, then whose?
Comment by Examiner, Director of Studies Yang 揚 [楊]: Most candidates failed to grasp the words "meaning" (yi 義) and "blessing" (fu 福) in this topic. Only this essay comprehends them with true substance; it deserves to top the list for this Classic.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Nie 聶: In explaining the passage "in sacrifice one is certain to receive blessing," most commentators refer to the Five Blessings (wufu 五福). Only this essay accords very closely with the original purport of the text; is its author not deeply versed in the Classic?

When we observe the gentleman in relation to sacrifice, we see that because he alone is able to fulfill its meaning, he is certain to receive its blessing. For "blessing" is the name for a state in which nothing is out of harmony, and the "meaning of sacrifice" is to convey one's heart by means of offerings. Since in sacrifice the gentleman alone is able to fulfill its meaning, how could he fail, even before the sacrifice takes place, to be certain of receiving its blessing? Now in the performance of sacrificial rites, what is valued is that there first be the heartfelt intent and only afterward the material offerings. Yet in the world there are certainly many who forget the heart, and no few who merely pursue the material offerings. Only when the gentleman sacrifices, moved by the falling of the spring rains, does his feeling of awe and solicitude…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
心油然以生感霜露之旣降其悽愴之心盡然以動於是奉之以三
牲之俎以表此心之誠陳之以八簋之實以將此心之敬發於心而奉其物此
豈衆人之所能奉其物以將其心實乃君子之所獨夫君子之能祭如此
必其於祭之前雖鬼神極其幽也則致其誠信而上有以順乎鬼神矣雖
君長極其尊也則與其忠敬而外有以順於君長矣內焉順於親而
親無不安外焉順於道而道無不達幽明人鬼無一事之不順外道內
親無一順之不備君子於祭之必受其福也如此夫豈世之所謂永受
胡福介爾景福之可比哉抑觀祭祀之禮至不一也有以多為貴者有
以少為貴者以多為貴者以其外心也以少為貴者以其內心也此之
===
所謂能盡祭之義者是由內而之外彼之所謂以多為貴者是因文
以見本學者誠能以內為尊以外為樂則本文兼舉而內外不遺百
順之名豈不必受於已哉
論
聖位天德
龔沅
同考試官教諭羅批超出衆作可為論中之魁者也
考試官學正楊批作者妄認題意不愜人心忽得此卷
辭理兼該議論正大不啻若聆黃鍾
太簇之交奏也
punctuated:
心油然以生；感霜露之旣降，其悽愴之心盡然以動。於是奉之以三牲之俎，以表此心之誠；陳之以八簋之實，以將此心之敬。發於心而奉其物，此豈衆人之所能？奉其物以將其心，實乃君子之所獨。夫君子之能祭如此，必其於祭之前，雖鬼神極其幽也，則致其誠信，而上有以順乎鬼神矣；雖君長極其尊也，則與其忠敬，而外有以順於君長矣。內焉順於親，而親無不安；外焉順於道，而道無不達。幽明人鬼，無一事之不順；外道內親，無一順之不備。君子於祭之必受其福也如此，夫豈世之所謂「永受胡福」、「介爾景福」之可比哉！抑觀祭祀之禮至不一也：有以多為貴者，有以少為貴者。以多為貴者，以其外心也；以少為貴者，以其內心也。此之所謂「能盡祭之義」者，是由內而之外；彼之所謂「以多為貴」者，是因文以見本。學者誠能以內為尊，以外為樂，則本、文兼舉而內、外不遺，「百順之名」豈不必受於已哉？

論
聖位天德
龔沅
同考試官教諭羅批：超出衆作，可為論中之魁者也。
考試官學正楊批：作者妄認題意，不愜人心；忽得此卷，辭理兼該，議論正大，不啻若聆黃鍾、太簇之交奏也。
translation_en:
… heart arises spontaneously; moved when frost and dew have descended, his sorrowful heart is stirred to the utmost [? 盡 for 憯]. Thereupon he presents the sacrificial stands of the three victims to manifest the sincerity of this heart, and sets forth the contents of the eight grain-vessels to convey the reverence of this heart. To issue from the heart and then present the offerings—how could this be something the multitude is capable of? To present the offerings in order to convey the heart is truly unique to the gentleman. Now, since the gentleman is able to sacrifice in this manner, it must be that prior to the sacrifice, even though ghosts and spirits are supremely unfathomable, he extends his sincerity and trustworthiness, and thus above has the means to be in harmony with ghosts and spirits; even though ruler and superiors are supremely exalted, he gives his loyalty and reverence, and thus outwardly has the means to be in harmony with ruler and superiors. Inwardly he is in harmony with his parents, and his parents are never unpeaced; outwardly he is in harmony with the Way, and the Way is never obstructed. Across the unseen and the manifest, among men and spirits, there is not a single matter that is not in harmony; between the Way without and parents within, there is not a single harmony that is not complete. That the gentleman in sacrificing is certain to receive its blessing is like this—how could it be compared to what the world calls "forever receiving longevity's blessing" or "increasing your great blessing"? Moreover, if we observe the rites of sacrifice, they are most varied: there are those in which abundance is prized, and those in which paucity is prized. Where abundance is prized, it is because the heart is directed outward; where paucity is prized, it is because the heart is directed inward. What is here called "being able to exhaust the meaning of sacrifice" proceeds from the inner to the outer; what is there called "prizing abundance" uses the outward form to manifest the root. If the student can truly revere the inner and take joy in the outer, then both root and form will be upheld together and neither inner nor outer will be neglected—how then could "the name of total harmony" not be received by oneself?

Discourse
"The Position of the Sage and the Virtue of Heaven"
Gong Yuan 龔沅
Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor (jiaoyu): Surpasses the crowd of compositions; it may stand as the champion among the discourses.
Comment by Examiner Yang, Director of Studies (xuezheng): Other writers misconstrued the meaning of the topic, failing to satisfy the mind; suddenly obtaining this paper—comprehensive in both diction and principle, upright and grand in argument—was nothing less than listening to the alternating performance of the Yellow Bell (Huangzhong) and Great Cluster (Taicu) pitch-pipes.

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭聶批諸作皆不考張子立言之意令人厭
觀惟此篇旨趣高遠考據精詳筆勢
滔滔所謂波瀾老成者
論曰莫大乎天而元亨利貞運行於四時無一息之或爽莫大於聖
人而仁義禮智充周於一身無一時之或間夫天之德不可名以其
運而不已無朕兆之可覩也聖人之德不可名以其大而化之無形跡
之可窺也造聖人之位達天德之妙非大而化之其孰能與於斯
請因先儒張子正蒙之旨而申論之正南面而垂衣裳人皆知其
位之尊也此特聖人所得之位而非造天德之位也居九重而履
===
大寶人皆謂其位之貴也此特聖人所處之位而非聖人達天德之
位也欲知聖位天德之妙果何如哉必大而化之而後可造乎其極
也殊不知充滿而積實可以謂之美矣豈得謂之化乎未至於化
則與天德有間矣積實而光輝可以謂之大矣豈得謂之化乎未
至於化則與天德不侔矣大可為也化其可為乎大可勉也化其可
勉乎彼其伊尹聖之任者也能負荷聖人所當為之事勉力以
求至乎聖人之地雖有跡之可見猶不害於未化爾顏子聖之
亞者也克己以請事聖人之教欲竭其才以求底乎聖人之域
但不假之以年而未至於化爾必也無我而後大大成性而後
punctuated:
考試官教諭聶批：諸作皆不考張子立言之意，令人厭觀；惟此篇旨趣高遠，考據精詳，筆勢滔滔，所謂波瀾老成者。
論曰：莫大乎天，而元亨利貞運行於四時，無一息之或爽；莫大於聖人，而仁義禮智充周於一身，無一時之或間。夫天之德不可名，以其運而不已，無朕兆之可覩也；聖人之德不可名，以其大而化之，無形跡之可窺也。造聖人之位，達天德之妙，非大而化之，其孰能與於斯？請因先儒張子《正蒙》之旨而申論之。正南面而垂衣裳，人皆知其位之尊也，此特聖人所得之位，而非造天德之位也；居九重而履大寶，人皆謂其位之貴也，此特聖人所處之位，而非聖人達天德之位也。欲知聖位天德之妙，果何如哉？必大而化之，而後可造乎其極也。殊不知充滿而積實，可以謂之美矣，豈得謂之化乎？未至於化，則與天德有間矣。積實而光輝，可以謂之大矣，豈得謂之化乎？未至於化，則與天德不侔矣。大可為也，化其可為乎？大可勉也，化其可勉乎？彼其伊尹，聖之任者也，能負荷聖人所當為之事，勉力以求至乎聖人之地，雖有跡之可見，猶不害於未化爾。顏子，聖之亞者也，克己以請事聖人之教，欲竭其才以求底乎聖人之域，但不假之以年，而未至於化爾。必也無我而後大，大成性而後…
translation_en:
Examiner and County Instructor Nie comments: All the other essays fail to examine the intent of Master Zhang’s [Zhang Zai 張載] words, making them tiresome to read; only this piece is lofty and far-reaching in its purport, precise and thorough in its textual grounding, and surging in the momentum of its brush—what one calls mature and masterful in its surging waves.

The discourse reads: Nothing is greater than Heaven, whose originating growth, flourishing, advantage, and firmness (yuan, heng, li, zhen) operate through the four seasons without a single moment's lapse; nothing is greater than the sage, in whose person benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom fill every part without a single instant's interruption. Now, the virtue of Heaven cannot be named, because it revolves ceaselessly without any incipient sign that can be seen; the virtue of the sage cannot be named, because it is great and transforming without any physical trace that can be glimpsed. To reach the position of the sage and attain the subtlety of Heavenly virtue—if one is not great and transforming, who could partake in this? Allow me to elaborate on this based on the purport of the former Confucian Master Zhang’s Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng). Sitting facing directly south and letting robes hang down, everyone knows the exaltedness of such a position; yet this is merely the position the sage obtains, not the position of reaching Heavenly virtue. Dwelling within the ninefold palace gates and ascending the Great Treasure [the throne], everyone speaks of the nobility of such a position; yet this is merely the position the sage occupies, not the position in which the sage attains Heavenly virtue. If one wishes to know the subtlety of the sage's position and Heavenly virtue, what is it really like? Only when one is great and transforms it can one reach its ultimate pinnacle. Yet people do not realize that being filled to capacity and accumulating substance may be called admirable, but how could it be called transforming? When one has not yet reached transformation, there is still a gap between oneself and Heavenly virtue. Accumulating substance until it shines forth brightly may be called great, but how could it be called transforming? When one has not yet reached transformation, one is still not equal to Heavenly virtue. Greatness can be achieved through deliberate action, but can transformation be achieved through deliberate action? Greatness can be striven for, but can transformation be striven for? Take Yi Yin 伊尹: he was the sage who took responsibility upon himself. He was able to shoulder the tasks that a sage ought to do, striving with all his might to reach the ground of the sage; although there were visible traces in his conduct, that still did not detract from his simply not yet having reached transformation. As for Master Yan [Yan Hui 顏回], he was second to the sage. He overcame the self and asked to put into practice the teachings of the sage, wishing to exhaust his talents in seeking to arrive at the realm of the sage; it was only that Heaven did not grant him sufficient years, and so he did not yet reach transformation. Only when there is no self-centeredness does one become great; only when greatness becomes one's very nature does one…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
化化則泯然無形之可驗蕩然無跡之可名德盛仁熟自然而然
非智力之所能及也至此而謂之聖位天德乃造其極而無以加
矣非天下之至聖其孰能與於斯由是觀之天之於穆不已即
聖人之至誠無息也天之物各付物即聖人之泛應曲應當也在
天為元聖人之仁即天之元時之春也在天為亨聖人之禮即天之
亨時之夏也以至聖人之義與天之利時之秋同一機聖人之智與
天之貞時之冬無二致論而至是吾不知聖人其天乎天其聖人
乎彼伊尹顏淵固未及此求其可以當此者其惟堯舜乎吁堯
舜遠矣造聖人之位具天德之大幸有今日
===
聖人在上
表
擬宋胡安國進春秋傳表
鄧珙
同考試官教諭黎批表得體
考試官學正楊批典雅
考試官教諭聶批詞嚴義正隊仗森然可取
天子議禮考文表六經之正學
聖人神道設教開萬世之太平當關雎麟趾之化行正奎璧圖
punctuated:
化。化則泯然無形之可驗，蕩然無跡之可名；德盛仁熟，自然而然，非智力之所能及也。至此而謂之聖位天德，乃造其極而無以加矣。非天下之至聖，其孰能與於斯？由是觀之，天之於穆不已，即聖人之至誠無息也；天之物各付物，即聖人之泛應曲應當也。在天為元，聖人之仁即天之元、時之春也；在天為亨，聖人之禮即天之亨、時之夏也；以至聖人之義與天之利、時之秋同一機，聖人之智與天之貞、時之冬無二致。論而至是，吾不知聖人其天乎？天其聖人乎？彼伊尹、顏淵固未及此，求其可以當此者，其惟堯、舜乎！吁，堯、舜遠矣，造聖人之位，具天德之大，幸有今日聖人在上。

表
擬宋胡安國進《春秋傳》表
鄧珙
同考試官教諭黎批：表得體。
考試官學正楊批：典雅。
考試官教諭聶批：詞嚴義正，隊仗森然，可取。

天子議禮考文，表六經之正學；聖人神道設教，開萬世之太平。當《關雎》、《麟趾》之化行，正奎、璧、圖、
translation_en:
…transformation. Once transformed, it is seamless without any form that can be verified, boundless without any trace that can be named. When virtue is abundant and benevolence is ripe, it is naturally so of itself, beyond the reach of knowledge or effort. Arriving at this point, it is called the sage's position and Heavenly virtue, having reached the ultimate pinnacle to which nothing more can be added. Save for the most sagely in the world, who could partake in this? Viewed from this perspective, Heaven's profound and ceaseless operation is none other than the sage's utmost sincerity without rest; Heaven's bestowing upon each thing according to its nature is none other than the sage's universal and fitting response to all affairs [?]. What in Heaven is origination (yuan) is in the sage benevolence—which is Heaven's origination and the season of spring. What in Heaven is flourishing (heng) is in the sage propriety—which is Heaven's flourishing and the season of summer. Furthermore, the sage's righteousness shares the very same mechanism as Heaven's advantage (li) and the season of autumn, and the sage's wisdom is no different from Heaven's firmness (zhen) and the season of winter. Carrying the discussion to this point, I do not know whether the sage is Heaven, or Heaven is the sage! Figures such as Yi Yin 伊尹 and Yan Yuan 顏淵 certainly did not reach this level; if we seek those who are worthy of this, could it not be only Yao 堯 and Shun 舜! Alas, Yao and Shun are distant now, yet to attain the position of the sage and embody the greatness of Heavenly virtue, we are fortunate today to have a Sage on high.

Memorial
Imitating a Memorial by Hu Anguo 胡安國 of the Song Presenting His Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu zhuan 春秋傳)
Deng Gong 鄧珙
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Li 黎: The memorial is appropriate in form.
Comment by Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Yang 楊: Classical and elegant.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Nie 聶: The diction is rigorous and the meaning upright; its parallel structure is stately and well-ordered—worthy of selection.

The Son of Heaven deliberates on rituals and examines the written script, exalting the orthodox learning of the Six Classics; the Sage establishes teachings by the divine way, opening up great peace for ten thousand generations. Just as the civilizing influence of the "Ospreys" (Guanju 關雎) and the "Foot of the Lin" (Linzhi 麟趾) prevails, it is precisely the time when the auspicious signs of the Kui 奎 and Bi 璧 constellations, the River Chart…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
書之瑞應若稽往古斷自
宸衷謂春秋之作實肇於素王而
宵旰之勤尚勞於
睿覽褒貶每嚴於一字傳註多謬於專門大義乖而未彰曲說
混而莫辨欲明三傳之得失獨究遺經之始終爰命近臣
重加著釋臣深慚末學濫綴清班強探儒先直指之歸未領
史外傳心之要是用旁搜載博采群言微顯闡幽窺見一二
公之事尊王賤伯講明數千載之前雖淵微之義或未貫
通而綱常之道庶其有補兹蓋伏遇
===
〇〇〇〇
聰明天縱
聖敬日躋
乃武乃文光復
中興之大業
惟精惟一丕承
烈祖之鴻猷倘
萬幾之暇特
賜覽觀而一得之愚敢忘報稱臣無任瞻天仰聖激切屏營之至謹奉表稱謝以聞
punctuated: 書之瑞應。若稽往古，斷自宸衷。謂《春秋》之作，實肇於素王；而宵旰之勤，尚勞於睿覽。褒貶每嚴於一字，傳註多謬於專門。大義乖而未彰，曲說混而莫辨。欲明三傳之得失，獨究遺經之始終，爰命近臣，重加著釋。臣深慚末學，濫綴清班。強探儒先直指之歸，未領史外傳心之要。是用旁搜載，博采群言。微顯闡幽，窺見一二公之事；尊王賤伯，講明數千載之前。雖淵微之義或未貫通，而綱常之道庶其有補。兹蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，聰明天縱，聖敬日躋。乃武乃文，光復中興之大業；惟精惟一，丕承烈祖之鴻猷。倘萬幾之暇，特賜覽觀，而一得之愚，敢忘報稱？臣無任瞻天仰聖激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
translation_en:
…the auspicious response of river charts and books. Investigating remote antiquity, the decision came from Your Imperial Heart. Considering that the composition of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) actually originated with the Uncrowned King [Confucius], yet amid the diligence of Your pre-dawn dressing and late-evening meals, You still trouble Your Imperial Perusal with it. Its praise and blame are always strict down to a single word, while its commentaries and annotations have mostly gone astray among specialized schools. The great principles were perverted and left unclarified; crooked theories were mixed in and could not be distinguished. Wishing to clarify the successes and failures of the Three Commentaries, and to investigate solely the beginning and end of the bequeathed Classic, You thereupon commanded a close minister to compose an explanation anew.

Your servant is deeply ashamed of his shallow learning, unworthily occupying a place in the pure court ranks. Though I strained to explore the direct aims of earlier Confucians, I had not yet grasped the essentials of the transmission of the mind beyond history. Therefore I searched broadly through records [? missing 籍 after 載] and gathered widely from the words of many scholars. Making manifest the subtle and elucidating the obscure, I caught a glimpse of the affairs of the twelve dukes; honoring the King and disparaging the hegemons, I expounded and clarified events from several thousand years ago. Although its profound and subtle meanings may not yet be thoroughly penetrated, to the Way of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues it may perhaps offer some small aid.

This is because I humbly encounter [Your Majesty, four-character imperial title placeholder 〇〇〇〇], whose intelligence is Heaven-bestowed, and whose sage reverence daily ascends; both martial and civil, gloriously restoring the great enterprise of dynastic revival; refined and single-minded, grandly carrying on the vast plans of the Illustrious Ancestors. If in the leisure from Your myriad affairs You specially grant it Your perusal, how would my humble wit, with its single insight, dare forget to repay Your grace [? the final clause from 而一得之愚 through 以聞 appears to be a scribal intrusion here, as the sentence continues onto the next page with 緝熙聖學…]…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
緝熙
聖學川方至而日方升鞏固
皇圖天愈長而地愈久臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所撰春秋傳隨
表上
進以
聞
punctuated: 緝熙聖學，川方至而日方升；鞏固皇圖，天愈長而地愈久。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹以所撰《春秋傳》隨表上進以聞。
translation_en: …May you continually illuminate your imperial learning, like rivers just arriving at the flood and the sun just rising; may you consolidate the imperial enterprise, enduring as long as heaven and earth. Your servant is overwhelmed with boundless reverence and awe as he gazes up toward Heaven and the Sacred Person, and respectfully submits the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu zhuan) that he has compiled, accompanying this memorial, for the Emperor's hearing.

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
策
第一問周瑛
同考試官教諭羅批翩翩五策文彩燁然而此尤傑出者也
故表而出之
考試官學正楊批五策條荅無遺此篇事實尤備足
見學識
考試官教諭聶批一策皆隨問而荅得士如此可以
謂之文矣
聖君出而繼天立極之功大聖經作而垂世立教之道明欽惟
===
太宗文皇帝萬機之暇采輯傳記得古人為善獲報者百六十五人旣
各為論斷以發揚其潜德復為歌詩吟以詠其性情以嘉惠
臣民昭示四海誠為萬世之大寶也執事發策以是下詢承學愚
不敏敢不採摭以對彼其立定大計口不言功丙吉之深厚不
伐也為治循良舉善而教卓茂之視人如子也握兵柄而好生
非鄧禹之出師不殺乎假蒲鞭以示辱非劉寬之臨政温仁
乎又如王忱之稱髙全營殯非敦義乎嚴謖之平治無辜非
詳審乎李珏之販糴平量敏中之守護遺物范宰之擇嫁
彥廣之還女曹彬之仁惠王祐之公直若水之察誣寃堯佐
punctuated:
策
第一問：周瑛。
同考試官教諭羅批：翩翩五策，文彩燁然，而此尤傑出者也，故表而出之。
考試官學正楊批：五策條荅無遺，此篇事實尤備，足見學識。
考試官教諭聶批：一策皆隨問而荅，得士如此，可以謂之文矣。

聖君出而繼天立極之功大，聖經作而垂世立教之道明。欽惟太宗文皇帝萬機之暇，采輯傳記，得古人為善獲報者百六十五人，旣各為論斷以發揚其潜德，復為歌、詩、吟以詠其性情，以嘉惠臣民，昭示四海，誠為萬世之大寶也。執事發策以是下詢，承學愚不敏，敢不採摭以對？彼其立定大計，口不言功，丙吉之深厚不伐也；為治循良，舉善而教，卓茂之視人如子也；握兵柄而好生，非鄧禹之出師不殺乎？假蒲鞭以示辱，非劉寬之臨政温仁乎？又如王忱之稱髙、全營殯，非敦義乎？嚴謖之平治無辜，非詳審乎？李珏之販糴平量，敏中之守護遺物，范宰之擇嫁，彥廣之還女，曹彬之仁惠，王祐之公直，若水之察誣寃，堯佐…
translation_en:
Policy Essays
First Question: Zhou Ying 周瑛

Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Luo 羅: "All five policy essays are gracefully written and brilliant in literary style, and this one is especially outstanding; therefore, we have singled it out for presentation."
Comment by Examiner, Director of Studies (xuezheng) Yang 楊: "The five policy essays answer each point without omission, and the historical facts in this essay are particularly thorough, which is enough to show his learning and insight."
Comment by Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Nie 聶: "Every part of this policy essay answers in direct response to the question. To obtain a scholar such as this—one may truly call this refined writing!"

When a sage ruler arises, his achievement in succeeding Heaven and establishing the supreme standard is great; when a sacred classic is composed, its Way in handing down teachings to the world becomes manifest. We reverently reflect upon how Emperor Taizong Wen 太宗文皇帝 (the Yongle Emperor), in his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, gathered and compiled biographies and records, finding one hundred and sixty-five ancients who did good and received recompense. Having written a critical appraisal for each to bring to light their hidden virtues, he further composed songs, poems, and chants to sing of their dispositions and feelings, thereby graciously benefitting his officials and people and clearly displaying them to all within the Four Seas; truly, this is a great treasure for ten thousand generations! Now that Your Excellency has set forth this policy question to inquire of us below, though I, a junior student, am foolish and dull, how dare I not gather what I know to reply?

As for helping to settle the great plan of succession while never speaking of his own merit, that was the deep generosity and lack of boastfulness of Bing Ji 丙吉; governing as a dutiful and良 (benevolent) official, promoting the good and instructing the people, that was Zhuo Mao's 卓茂 regarding the people as his own children. Holding military authority yet loving life—was this not Deng Yu's 鄧禹 leading armies into the field without indiscriminate killing? Using a cattail whip merely to show disgrace—was this not Liu Kuan's 劉寬 gentle benevolence in administering government? Take also Wang Chen's 王忱 praising [Fan] Gao 范高 and [Liu] Quan's 劉全 arranging the burial of the dead—was this not honoring righteousness? Yan Su's 嚴謖 fairly adjudicating the innocent—was this not careful examination? Li Jue's 李珏 trading in grain with fair measures, [Xiang] Minzhong's 向敏中 guarding lost property, Magistrate Fan's 范宰 choosing a husband to marry off a girl, [Luo] Yanguang's 羅彥廣 returning a daughter, Cao Bin's 曹彬 benevolence and kindness, Wang You's 王祐 impartiality and uprightness, [Qian] Ruoshui's 錢若水 discerning false accusations and injustices, [Chen] Yaozuo's 陳堯佐…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
之興水利具經濟之才蠲屋地之輸非范仲淹李允則其人乎
夜燭治書死獄求生此歐陽觀之留心讞獄也三喪未舉麥
舟相濟此范純仁之推惠朋友也若夫出粟濟人對衆焚券
歲凶發廩米粥賑飢非李謙天福之長者乎造舟濟渡人免
病涉以食施貧人賴全活非宋仁祝染之惠利乎伯林為吏與民
休息嚴實從征活人數萬希憲出鎮荊南人漸德化田滋廉訪
浙西政稱廉能之數君子者所行雖不同而立心之仁則同所
為雖有異而立心之善則無異所謂積陰德於冥冥之中
而顯受陽報者愚生游學庠序敢不佩服
===
聖教倘異日居官臨政亦竊有志於斯執事有以進之幸甚
第二問
卓天錫
考試官學正楊批推原理數敷荅詳明非平昔探求
諸子之蘊者曷克臻此
考試官教諭聶批發策正欲觀士子本領之學理數
之荅詳備可敬
觀諸儒理數之言當求諸儒理數之㫖甚矣理數之學不可以不
講也觀諸儒之言雖有不同求其所論之㫖又豈不各有攸當哉
punctuated:
之興水利，具經濟之才、蠲屋地之輸，非范仲淹、李允則其人乎？夜燭治書，死獄求生，此歐陽觀之留心讞獄也；三喪未舉，麥舟相濟，此范純仁之推惠朋友也。若夫出粟濟人，對衆焚券，歲凶發廩，米粥賑飢，非李謙、天福之長者乎？造舟濟渡，人免病涉，以食施貧，人賴全活，非宋仁、祝染之惠利乎？伯林為吏，與民休息；嚴實從征，活人數萬；希憲出鎮荊南，人漸德化；田滋廉訪浙西，政稱廉能。之數君子者，所行雖不同，而立心之仁則同；所為雖有異，而立心之善則無異，所謂積陰德於冥冥之中，而顯受陽報者。愚生游學庠序，敢不佩服聖教？倘異日居官臨政，亦竊有志於斯。執事有以進之，幸甚。

第二問
卓天錫
考試官學正楊批：推原理數，敷荅詳明，非平昔探求諸子之蘊者，曷克臻此？
考試官教諭聶批：發策正欲觀士子本領之學，理數之荅，詳備可敬。

觀諸儒理數之言，當求諸儒理數之㫖。甚矣，理數之學不可以不講也！觀諸儒之言雖有不同，求其所論之㫖，又豈不各有攸當哉？
translation_en:
…developing waterworks; and as for possessing talents for statecraft and remitting taxes on houses and land, were those men not Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹 and Li Yunze 李允則? Examining documents by candlelight at night to seek a way of survival in capital cases—this was Ouyang Guan 歐陽觀 taking great care in adjudicating lawsuits; when three burials had not yet been carried out, coming to aid with a boatload of wheat—this was Fan Chunren 范純仁 extending kindness to a friend. As for bringing out grain to relieve people and burning debt tallies before the crowd, or opening granaries in years of dearth and providing rice gruel to relieve the starving, were these not the virtuous elders Li Qian 李謙 and [Dou] Tianfu [竇]天福? Building boats to ferry people across so that they were spared the hardship of wading, and bestowing food upon the poor so that people relied on it to survive intact, were these not the beneficent acts of Song Ren 宋仁 and Zhu Ran 祝染 [?]? As an official, [張] Bolin [張]伯林 gave the people rest and recuperation; following military campaigns, Yan Shi 嚴實 saved tens of thousands of lives; going out to garrison Jingnan, [Lian] Xixian [廉]希憲 gradually transformed the people through virtue; and serving as Surveillance Commissioner in Zhexi, Tian Zi 田滋 had an administration praised for its integrity and capability. As for these several gentlemen, although their actions were not the same, the benevolence of their intentions was the same; although what they did differed, the goodness of their intentions did not differ—they were what is called accumulating hidden virtue in the unseen realm and manifestly receiving visible rewards. As an ignorant student studying in the local schools, how could I dare not take to heart the sagely teachings? If on a future day I hold office and oversee administration, I too privately aspire to this. Should Your Excellency find something herein to advance me, it would be most fortunate.

Second Question
Zhuo Tianxi 卓天錫
Comment by Examiner Yang, Subprefectural Director of Studies: Tracing the origins of principle and number, the exposition and answers are detailed and clear. Were he not one who had ordinarily investigated the profound meanings of the various masters, how could he have achieved this?
Comment by Examiner Nie, County Director of Studies: In posing this policy question, the intention was precisely to observe the candidates' fundamental learning. His answer on principle and number is detailed, complete, and worthy of respect.

When examining the words of the various Confucians regarding principle and number, one ought to seek the underlying purport of the various Confucians regarding principle and number. Indeed, the learning of principle and number cannot go unstudied! Although the words of the various Confucians differ when examined, if one seeks the purport of what they discuss, how could each not have its own proper validity?…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
請因明問而畧陳之周子太極一圖剖析精微易通一書又所以
法此圖者也盖圖有太極書則以誠發之太極本無極書則以
誠無為著之圖之陽動即書所謂誠之源也圖之陰靜即書
所謂誠之立也陽變陰合而生水火木金土即誠通誠復而為
元亨利貞者也善惡一陰陽也仁義禮智信一五行也圖書相
為表裏者如此易有太極而圖言無極盖易之言有以理言也
圖之言無以形言也曰無曰有同此理耳豈太極之外復有無
極者哉至於古書有所謂太一者盖以其無二則曰一以其至極
則曰極其與太極名雖殊而義則一也若所謂太易未見氣
===
太初氣之始太始形之始太素質之始是以氣形質言之而非
指乎此理矣豈可與太極同論哉程子學於周子其圖親得
手授之傳著書立言傳道解惑而未嘗有一言及於圖者盖
以圖之立象盡意周子不得已而作也觀其手授之意惟程子
為能當之至程子而不言則疑其未有能受之者爾至若西
銘正蒙張子所著西銘統而論之乾父坤母民胞物與理之
一也然曰人曰物其分殊矣分而論之則大君而宗子大臣而家
相以至於惸獨鰥寡皆吾之兄弟顛連而無告者亦理之一
也然以必各親其親各長其長而後有以及人之親長則其
punctuated: 請因明問而畧陳之。周子《太極》一圖，剖析精微；《易通》一書，又所以法此圖者也。盖圖有太極，書則以誠發之；太極本無極，書則以誠無為著之；圖之陽動，即書所謂誠之源也；圖之陰靜，即書所謂誠之立也；陽變陰合而生水、火、木、金、土，即誠通誠復而為元、亨、利、貞者也；善惡，一陰陽也；仁、義、禮、智、信，一五行也。圖、書相為表裏者如此。《易》有太極，而圖言無極，盖《易》之言「有」，以理言也；圖之言「無」，以形言也。曰無、曰有，同此理耳，豈太極之外復有無極者哉！至於古書有所謂「太一」者，盖以其無二則曰「一」，以其至極則曰「極」，其與太極名雖殊而義則一也。若所謂「太易，未見氣；太初，氣之始；太始，形之始；太素，質之始」，是以氣、形、質言之，而非指乎此理矣，豈可與太極同論哉！程子學於周子，其圖親得手授之傳，著書立言，傳道解惑，而未嘗有一言及於圖者，盖以圖之立象盡意，周子不得已而作也。觀其手授之意，惟程子為能當之；至程子而不言，則疑其未有能受之者爾。至若《西銘》、《正蒙》，張子所著。《西銘》統而論之：乾父坤母，民胞物與，理之一也；然曰人、曰物，其分殊矣。分而論之，則大君而宗子，大臣而家相，以至於惸獨鰥寡，皆吾之兄弟顛連而無告者，亦理之一也；然以必各親其親、各長其長，而後有以及人之親長，則其
translation_en: Allow me to follow your perceptive question and briefly set this forth. Master Zhou’s [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤] Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu) analyzes the subtlest profundities, and his book Penetrating the Book of Changes (Yitong [Tongshu 通書]) is in turn modeled on this diagram. For where the Diagram has the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji), the book expounds it through sincerity (cheng); where the Supreme Ultimate is fundamentally the Non-Ultimate (Wuji), the book manifests it through sincerity being non-active (wuwei). The active yang of the Diagram is what the book calls the source of sincerity; the quiescent yin of the Diagram is what the book calls the establishment of sincerity. That yang transforms and yin unites to generate water, fire, wood, metal, and earth corresponds to sincerity penetrating and sincerity returning to become origination (yuan), flourish (heng), advantage (li), and firmness (zhen). Good and evil are simply yin and yang; benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness are simply the Five Phases. Such is the way the Diagram and the book serve as outer and inner aspects of one another. The Book of Changes (Yi) states that there is a Supreme Ultimate, whereas the Diagram speaks of the Non-Ultimate. This is because when the Changes speaks of "having" [a Supreme Ultimate], it speaks in terms of principle (li); when the Diagram speaks of "non-" [Ultimate], it speaks in terms of physical form (xing). Whether called "non-being" or "being," it is this same principle; how could there be another Non-Ultimate outside of the Supreme Ultimate! As for what ancient books call the "Supreme One" (Taiyi), because it has no second it is called "One," and because it is the utmost limit it is called "Ultimate"; although its name differs from the Supreme Ultimate, the meaning is one and the same. As for the sayings that "the Supreme Change (Taiyi) is before vital energy (qi) is seen; the Supreme Inception (Taichu) is the beginning of vital energy; the Supreme Beginning (Taishi) is the beginning of physical form; the Supreme Simplicity (Taisu) is the beginning of substantial matter," these speak in terms of vital energy, physical form, and substantial matter, and do not point to this principle. How could they be discussed on the same level as the Supreme Ultimate! The Masters Cheng [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤] studied under Master Zhou and personally received the transmission of his Diagram from his own hand. Yet in writing books and establishing their teachings to transmit the Way and resolve doubts, they never once mentioned the Diagram. This was because the Diagram sets up images to exhaust meaning, and Master Zhou created it only when he had no alternative. Looking at the intention behind his personal transmission, only the Masters Cheng were worthy of receiving it; when it came to the Masters Cheng and they did not speak of it, they likely suspected that there was not yet anyone capable of receiving it. As for the Western Inscription (Ximing) and Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng), they were written by Master Zhang [Zhang Zai 張載]. Speaking of the Western Inscription as a whole: Heaven (Qian) is the father and Earth (Kun) is the mother, the people are my womb-fellows and creatures are my companions—this is the oneness of principle. Yet in speaking of "human beings" and "creatures," their allotments (fen) are distinct. Speaking of it in terms of distinctions: the great ruler is the eldest宗-son (zongzi) and the great ministers are the household stewards, down to the solitary, the orphaned, the widower, and the widow, who are all my brothers in distress with no one to appeal to—this too is the oneness of principle. title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
分未嘗不殊矣分殊之中理之一者固未嘗不寓而理一之中不
害其為分之殊也程子之言可謂一言以蔽之矣又謂其書推
理以存義與孟子性善之論同功信夫楊中立謂其言體而
不及用未免流於兼愛者是烏足以知西銘者哉正蒙語造
化則極乎日月寒暑之變語鬼神則極乎二氣良能之妙
語陰陽則一神两化之論備焉語性命則太虛氣化之論詳
焉合而論之西銘之理一即圖之所以發太極陰陽之蘊也是
則太極也易通也西銘也正蒙也同乎一理也故曰四者理學
之源也先天經世邵子所著先天有變象者則寒暑晝夜
===
化象者則風雨露雷感象則性情形體應象則飛走草木
此象之不一也有往數者已生之卦由左而旋來數者未生之
卦由右而轉陰數起於十二陽數起於三十此數之不一也經
世之數起乎四本之以元會運世主之以日月星辰配之以春
夏秋冬參之以皇帝王伯又所以發明此圖者也然先天
也經世也皆主數言而太極獨以理言數之與理若相戾
矣殊不知理者數之本源數者理之妙用合而言之則未始
相離也先儒謂論其義理則先天不如太極之精而約其
言信夫陳瑩中指先天之易為心法是已後来者反名其
punctuated: 分未嘗不殊矣。分殊之中，理之一者固未嘗不寓；而理一之中，不害其為分之殊也。程子之言，可謂一言以蔽之矣。又謂其書推理以存義，與孟子性善之論同功，信夫！楊中立謂其言體而不及用，未免流於兼愛者，是烏足以知《西銘》者哉？《正蒙》語造化則極乎日月寒暑之變，語鬼神則極乎二氣良能之妙，語陰陽則一神两化之論備焉，語性命則太虛氣化之論詳焉。合而論之，《西銘》之理一，即圖之所以發太極陰陽之蘊也。是則《太極》也、《易通》也、《西銘》也、《正蒙》也，同乎一理也。故曰：四者，理學之源也。《先天》、《經世》，邵子所著。《先天》有變象者則寒暑晝夜，化象者則風雨露雷，感象則性情形體，應象則飛走草木，此象之不一也；有往數者，已生之卦由左而旋，來數者，未生之卦由右而轉，陰數起於十二，陽數起於三十，此數之不一也。《經世》之數起乎四，本之以元會運世，主之以日月星辰，配之以春夏秋冬，參之以皇帝王伯，又所以發明此圖者也。然《先天》也、《經世》也，皆主數言，而《太極》獨以理言，數之與理若相戾矣。殊不知理者數之本源，數者理之妙用，合而言之，則未始相離也。先儒謂論其義理，則《先天》不如《太極》之精而約，其言信夫！陳瑩中指先天之《易》為心法，是已；後来者反名其
translation_en: … roles have never failed to be distinct. Within the distinction of roles, the unity of principle never fails to reside; and within the unity of principle, there is no hindrance to there being a distinction of roles. Master Cheng’s words may be said to sum it up in a single phrase. He also said that this work deduces principle so as to preserve righteousness, achieving the same merit as Mencius’s discourse on the goodness of human nature—truly so! When Yang Zhongli 楊中立 (Yang Shi 楊時) claimed that it speaks of substance without reaching function and inevitably lapses into Mozi’s universal love, how could that suffice to show an understanding of the Western Inscription (Ximing)? As for Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng), when it speaks of creation and transformation, it exhausts the changes of sun and moon, cold and heat; when it speaks of ghosts and spirits, it exhausts the subtleties of the innate efficacy of the two vital forces (qi); when it speaks of yin and yang, the discourse on the one spirit and two transformations is complete therein; when it speaks of human nature and destiny, the discourse on the Great Vacuity and the transformation of qi is detailed therein. Considered together, the unity of principle in the Western Inscription is precisely that by which the Diagram brings forth the profound stores of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji) and yin and yang. Thus the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu), Penetrating the Book of Changes (Yitong), the Western Inscription (Ximing), and Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng) all share a single principle. Therefore it is said that these four are the source of the Learning of Principle (lixue). The Prior to Heaven Diagram (Xiantian tu) and the Supreme Principles Governing the World (Huangji jingshi) were composed by Master Shao (Shao Yong 邵雍). In the Prior to Heaven Diagram, there are the images of alternation, which are cold, heat, day, and night; the images of transformation, which are wind, rain, dew, and thunder; the images of stimulus, which are nature, emotion, form, and body; and the images of response, which are birds, beasts, grasses, and trees—such is the diversity of its images. There are the numbers of the past, whereby the hexagrams already generated revolve from the left, and the numbers of the future, whereby the hexagrams not yet generated turn from the right; the yin numbers begin at twelve, and the yang numbers begin at thirty—such is the diversity of its numbers. The numbers of Governing the World (Jingshi) begin with four: they are grounded in epochs (yuan), cycles (hui), revolutions (yun), and generations (shi); governed by the sun, moon, stars, and zodiacal spaces; matched with spring, summer, autumn, and winter; and correlated with August Ones (huang), Emperors (di), Kings (wang), and Hegemons (ba)—all of which further serve to elucidate this Diagram. Yet both the Prior to Heaven Diagram and Governing the World speak primarily in terms of numbers, whereas the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate speaks solely in terms of principle, so that number and principle might seem to be at odds with one another. Little do people realize that principle is the fundamental source of number, and number is the wondrous function of principle; considered together, they have never been separate from one another. Former Confucian scholars said that in discussing moral principle, the Prior to Heaven Diagram is not as refined and concise as the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate—truly their words are trustworthy! title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
書為考數又烏足以知先天者哉然雖眾論紛紜得失殊致
不有朱夫子無極之辨通書之解西銘正蒙之訓釋皇極經
世之考正又何以會諸書而同一理合三子而同一心哉噫數君
子之書固皆有功於世而朱子又有功於數君子之書也歟敢
以是為復
第五問
許評
同考試官教諭鮑批事有考究文有波瀾允為策手
考試官學正楊批策有事實可取
===
考試官教諭聶批此問鮮能詳答惟此篇明備足
見博識
嘗謂制治莫善於訓兵訓兵莫先於擇將盖兵者國之
衛而將者兵之帥者不訓兵則無以衛其國不擇將又何以帥
其兵哉執事發策以戎兵下詢承學愚雖不敏敢不撫其
所問以對乎且戎兵者國之大事周公之於成王必以詰爾
戎兵為訓召公之於康王必以張皇六師為戒故戎兵者
誠制治保邦之良法而士君子之所當講也夫周制三軍
非前軍中軍後軍乎周禮六軍非伍两卒旅師軍乎軒
punctuated:
書為考數，又烏足以知先天者哉！然雖眾論紛紜，得失殊致，不有朱夫子《無極》之辨、《通書》之解、《西銘》《正蒙》之訓釋、《皇極經世》之考正，又何以會諸書而同一理，合三子而同一心哉！噫！數君子之書，固皆有功於世，而朱子又有功於數君子之書也歟！敢以是為復。
第五問
許評
同考試官教諭鮑批：事有考究，文有波瀾，允為策手。
考試官學正楊批：策有事實，可取。
考試官教諭聶批：此問鮮能詳答，惟此篇明備，足見博識。
嘗謂制治莫善於訓兵，訓兵莫先於擇將。盖兵者，國之衛，而將者，兵之帥者。不訓兵，則無以衛其國；不擇將，又何以帥其兵哉？執事發策，以戎兵下詢承學，愚雖不敏，敢不撫其所問以對乎！且戎兵者，國之大事。周公之於成王，必以「詰爾戎兵」為訓；召公之於康王，必以「張皇六師」為戒。故戎兵者，誠制治保邦之良法，而士君子之所當講也。夫周制三軍，非前軍、中軍、後軍乎？《周禮》六軍，非伍、两、卒、旅、師、軍乎？軒
translation_en:
…writings "investigations of numerology"—how could they possibly understand the Prior to Heaven system! Yet, amid the welter of conflicting opinions and their varying merits and flaws, had it not been for Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] and his disputation on the Ultimate of Non-being (Wuji), his commentary on the Penetrating the Book of Changes (Tongshu), his explications of the Western Inscription (Ximing) and Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng), and his critical emendations of the Supreme Principles Governing the World (Huangji jingshi), how could one bring all these works together into a single principle and unite the three masters into a single mind? Alas! The writings of these several gentlemen have indeed rendered great service to the world, and has not Master Zhu in turn rendered great service to the writings of these several gentlemen? I venture to offer this as my reply.

Question Five
Xu Ping 許評
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Bao: The facts are well researched and the prose has surging momentum; truly a skilled writer of policy essays.
Comment by Examiner Director of Studies Yang: The policy essay is grounded in historical fact and is worthy of selection.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Nie: Few were able to answer this question in detail; only this essay is clear and thorough, amply demonstrating broad learning.

I have always held that in securing good governance nothing is better than training troops, and in training troops nothing is more urgent than selecting generals. For troops are the defense of the state, and generals are the commanders of the troops. If troops are not trained, there is no means to defend the state; if generals are not selected, how then can the troops be commanded? Now that Your Excellency has posed this policy question, inquiring of us junior scholars about military affairs, although I am dull-witted, how could I dare not take up what has been asked and offer a reply! Moreover, military affairs are a great matter of state. In addressing King Cheng, the Duke of Zhou made a point of instructing him to "look well to your weapons of war"; in addressing King Kang, the Duke of Shao made a point of admonishing him to "magnify the Six Armies." Thus, military preparedness is truly a sound method for securing governance and preserving the state, and a subject that scholar-gentlemen ought to study. As for the Three Armies of the Zhou system, were they not the Vanguard Army, the Center Army, and the Rear Army? As for the Six Armies of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), were they not organized through the hierarchy of squads of five (wu), files of twenty-five (liang), companies of a hundred (zu), battalions of five hundred (lü), divisions of twenty-five hundred (shi), and armies of twelve thousand five hundred (jun)? title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
轅之五行曰直陣銳陣圓陣方陣曲陣是也風后之八陣曰
天地風雲虎翼蛇蟠飛龍鳥翔是也方圓牝牡衝方罘罝
車輪鴈行則孫子之八陣為可知洞當中黃龍騰鳥翔連
衡握機虎翼折衝則孔明之八陣又可見至若李靖之中軍
左虞候右虞候左一廂右一廂左二廂右二廂不謂之六花
陣歟大黑大赤青蛇白雲左突右擊前衝後衝摧兇決勝
破敵先鋒不謂之十二陣歟然歷代兵法既陳矣若夫勇
智福者將之三等勇智仁信忠者將之五材五慎五危
者理備果戒約必死必生忿疾廉潔愛民也三道三急者
===
正兵竒兵伏兵得地形卒服習器用利也有所謂鼓金旗之
三官鼙鼓金鐸旌旗麾幟禁令刑罰之三威者焉有所謂
氣地事力之四機整兵習陣趨食嚴令就行之五鼓者焉形
色之旗號令之數進退之度長短之利賞罰之信則五教
之訓練為何如目習耳習心習手習足習則五習之教令又
何似五事者道天地將法之謂五法者度量數稱勝之謂
因內反死生非五間乎人積輜庫隊非火五攻乎他如人正辭
巧火水兵之七政權謀形勢陰陽技巧之四種形勢情之
決勝三術爭交輜重之類九地其將兵又歷歷可得而言
punctuated: 轅之五行，曰直陣、銳陣、圓陣、方陣、曲陣是也。風后之八陣，曰天、地、風、雲、虎翼、蛇蟠、飛龍、鳥翔是也。方、圓、牝、牡、衝方、罘罝、車輪、鴈行，則孫子之八陣為可知；洞當、中黃、龍騰、鳥翔、連衡、握機、虎翼、折衝，則孔明之八陣又可見。至若李靖之中軍、左虞候、右虞候、左一廂、右一廂、左二廂、右二廂，不謂之六花陣歟？大黑、大赤、青蛇、白雲、左突、右擊、前衝、後衝、摧兇、決勝、破敵、先鋒，不謂之十二陣歟？然歷代兵法既陳矣，若夫勇、智、福者，將之三等；勇、智、仁、信、忠者，將之五材。五慎、五危者，理、備、果、戒、約，必死、必生、忿疾、廉潔、愛民也。三道、三急者，正兵、竒兵、伏兵，得地形、卒服習、器用利也。有所謂鼓、金、旗之三官，鼙鼓金鐸、旌旗麾幟、禁令刑罰之三威者焉；有所謂氣、地、事、力之四機，整兵、習陣、趨食、嚴令、就行之五鼓者焉。形色之旗、號令之數、進退之度、長短之利、賞罰之信，則五教之訓練為何如？目習、耳習、心習、手習、足習，則五習之教令又何似？五事者，道、天、地、將、法之謂；五法者，度、量、數、稱、勝之謂。因、內、反、死、生，非五間乎？人、積、輜、庫、隊，非火五攻乎？他如人、正、辭、巧、火、水、兵之七政，權謀、形勢、陰陽、技巧之四種，形、勢、情之決勝三術，爭、交、輜重之類九地，其將兵又歷歷可得而言…
translation_en:
…The Five Phases of Xuanyuan [the Yellow Emperor] are the Straight Formation, Pointed Formation, Circular Formation, Square Formation, and Curved Formation. The Eight Formations of Fenghou are Heaven, Earth, Wind, Cloud, Tiger Wing, Coiling Snake, Flying Dragon, and Soaring Bird. From the Square, Circular, Female, Male, Assault-Square, Net, Chariot-Wheel, and Wild-Goose-Flight formations, Sunzi's Eight Formations can be known; from the Piercing-Center, Central-Yellow, Soaring-Dragon, Soaring-Bird, Linked-Horizontal, Grasping-Mechanism, Tiger-Wing, and Repelling-Assault formations, Kongming's [Zhuge Liang's] Eight Formations can likewise be seen. As for Li Jing's Center Army, Left Provost, Right Provost, Left First Wing, Right First Wing, Left Second Wing, and Right Second Wing, is this not called the Six-Petal Formation? And Great Black, Great Red, Green Snake, White Cloud, Left Thrust, Right Strike, Front Assault, Rear Assault, Crushing the Fierce, Deciding Victory, Breaking the Enemy, and Vanguard—are these not called the Twelve Formations?

Thus the military methods of successive ages have been set forth. As for courage, wisdom, and good fortune, these are the Three Grades of a general; courage, wisdom, benevolence, trustworthiness, and loyalty are the Five Qualities of a general. The Five Cautions and Five Dangers are reason, preparedness, resoluteness, vigilance, and simplicity; and recklessness unto death, clinging to life, quickness to anger, puritanical honor, and excessive compassion for the people. The Three Ways and Three Urgencies are regular troops, surprise troops, and ambush troops; and securing the terrain, having well-trained soldiers, and possessing sharp weapons. There are what are called the Three Offices of drums, gongs, and flags, and the Three Awesomenesses of war-drums and bells, banners and standards, and prohibitions and punishments; there are what are called the Four Pivots of morale, terrain, affairs, and strength, and the Five Drum-beats for marshaling troops, practicing formations, hastening to meals, enforcing strict orders, and marching in ranks. Banners of distinct shapes and colors, the tallies of commands, the measures of advancing and retreating, the advantages of long and short weapons, and trustworthiness in rewards and punishments—how is the training of the Five Instructions carried out? Training the eyes, training the ears, training the mind, training the hands, and training the feet—what are the commands of the Five Trainings like? The Five Matters refer to the Way, Heaven, Earth, the General, and Method; the Five Methods refer to measurement, estimation, calculation, weighing, and victory. Are not local, inside, doubled, doomed, and surviving spies the Five Spies? Are not burning personnel, stores, baggage, arsenals, and formations the Five Fire Attacks? As for other matters—such as the Seven Administrations of men, rectitude, rhetoric, artifice, fire, water, and weapons; the Four Categories of military texts on strategic calculation, disposition and momentum, yin-yang, and technical skills; the Three Arts of deciding victory through disposition, momentum, and true conditions; and the Nine Terrains such as contentious ground, intersecting ground, and baggage ground [?]—all these principles of commanding troops can be enumerated one by one…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
矣我
朝擇將用兵超軼前代內而衛國都外而捍疆場士氣銳鎧仗
精使將得人兵練有法則雖荒遠之地岩險之邦如前之陣
勢講而行之無施不可若夫料敵制勝隨時應機責在主
帥愚生管見軍旅未閑惟執事進而教之幸甚
punctuated: 矣。我朝擇將用兵，超軼前代，內而衛國都，外而捍疆場，士氣銳，鎧仗精。使將得人，兵練有法，則雖荒遠之地、岩險之邦，如前之陣勢，講而行之，無施不可。若夫料敵制勝，隨時應機，責在主帥。愚生管見，軍旅未閑，惟執事進而教之，幸甚。
translation_en: … Indeed! In selecting generals and deploying troops, our dynasty surpasses previous eras. Internally, it guards the imperial capital; externally, it defends the frontiers. The morale of the soldiers is keen, and their armor and weapons are finely wrought. If the right men are obtained as generals and the troops are trained with proper method, then even in desolate and distant lands or precipitous and perilous territories, should the battle formations mentioned above be studied and put into practice, there is nowhere they cannot be successfully applied. As for assessing the enemy to secure victory and responding to opportunities according to the moment, the responsibility rests with the commander-in-chief. Such is the narrow view of this ignorant student, who is unversed in military affairs; I pray only that Your Excellency will bring me forward and instruct me, which would be my greatest fortune.

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試小錄後序
景星慶雲麒麟鳳凰人知其為文明之祥太平之瑞也而
不知賢才輩出弼亮化工鼓舞至治有關乎氣運之
盛實
天下國家之祥瑞焉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝受
天明命統有萬方大興學校設置賢科當時賢俊奮登
際雲龍風虎之亨嘉固泰山磐石之基業
列聖相承益隆化理敷求賢哲茂篤成功迄今迨將百
===
年我
皇上纘承丕緒誕敷文教華夷率俾海岳效靈是固
聖化之自然亦賢才翊賛之所致也然猶慮用賢未廣於
是三年大比開取士之額以網羅天下豪傑益欲恢
宏至治垂萬億年太平之統迺景泰四年適藩鄉舉
得士之文且賢者凡若干人小錄成僉謂宜序惟治
道固本乎賢才而賢才實關乎氣運方今
氣運全盛之日正賢才效用之時生斯世也與斯選也
何其榮且幸歟雖然繼今以往尚當益勵廼學懋廼
punctuated:
福建鄉試小錄後序

景星、慶雲、麒麟、鳳凰，人知其為文明之祥、太平之瑞也，而不知賢才輩出，弼亮化工，鼓舞至治，有關乎氣運之盛，實天下國家之祥瑞焉。洪惟我太祖高皇帝受天明命，統有萬方，大興學校，設置賢科。當時賢俊奮登，際雲龍風虎之亨嘉，固泰山磐石之基業。列聖相承，益隆化理，敷求賢哲，茂篤成功。迄今迨將百年，我皇上纘承丕緒，誕敷文教，華夷率俾，海岳效靈。是固聖化之自然，亦賢才翊賛之所致也。然猶慮用賢未廣，於是三年大比，開取士之額，以網羅天下豪傑，益欲恢宏至治，垂萬億年太平之統。迺景泰四年，適藩鄉舉，得士之文且賢者凡若干人。小錄成，僉謂宜序。惟治道固本乎賢才，而賢才實關乎氣運。方今氣運全盛之日，正賢才效用之時。生斯世也，與斯選也，何其榮且幸歟！雖然，繼今以往，尚當益勵廼學，懋廼
translation_en:
Postface to the Brief Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

Auspicious stars, felicitous clouds, the qilin, and the phoenix—people know these to be omens of cultural flourishing and portents of great peace, yet they do not realize that when worthy talents emerge in succession to assist in the work of transformation and inspire the highest governance, it is bound up with the flourishing of the cosmic destiny and is truly the auspicious portent of the empire and the state.

Reflecting broadly on how our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), received the bright mandate of Heaven and united the myriad regions, he greatly promoted schools and established the examination categories for the worthy. At that time, worthies and men of outstanding talent rose up and ascended, meeting a propitious era when clouds follow the dragon and winds follow the tiger, and consolidating a foundation as firm as Mount Tai and great bedrock. Successive Emperors inherited the line one after another, further exalting transformative governance, widely seeking out the worthy and wise, and richly consolidating their achievements. Now, nearly a hundred years having passed, His Majesty the Emperor has succeeded to the great patrimony and broadly spread civil교 (cultural teachings), so that Chinese and non-Chinese alike submit and follow, and the seas and mountains manifest their numinous efficacy. While this is assuredly the natural outcome of sacred transformation, it is also brought about by the supportive assistance of worthy talents.

Even so, still concerned that the employment of worthies was not yet sufficiently broad, at the triennial Grand Competition he expanded the quota for selecting scholars in order to gather in the outstanding heroes of the empire, desiring all the more to enlarge supreme governance and hand down a lineage of great peace for ten thousand myriad years. Now, in the fourth year of the Jingtai reign (1453), on the occasion of the Provincial Examination in this province, a certain number of scholars who are both literary and worthy have been obtained. The brief record having been completed, all said that it ought to have a postface.

Indeed, the way of governance is assuredly rooted in worthy talents, and worthy talents are truly bound up with the cosmic destiny. Right now, a day when the cosmic destiny is in full flourishing is precisely the time for worthy talents to render their service. To be born in this age, and to be included in this selection—how glorious and fortunate it is! Even so, from this time onward, they should all the more encourage their learning and exert themselves in their…

title: 景泰四年福建鄉試錄
text:
德捷
春官對
大廷以黼藻
鴻猷笙簧治道為我
國家賢良之輔俾世之人目為文明之祥太平之瑞如
景星慶雲之昭于雲漢麒麟鳳凰之出於郊藪其荣
其幸不既又大乎哉序以伺之
景泰癸酉秋八月既望
山東兗州府東平州儒學學正楊玘序
punctuated:
德，捷春官，對大廷，以黼藻鴻猷，笙簧治道，為我國家賢良之輔，俾世之人目為文明之祥、太平之瑞，如景星慶雲之昭于雲漢，麒麟鳳凰之出於郊藪，其荣其幸，不既又大乎哉！序以伺之。
景泰癸酉秋八月既望，山東兗州府東平州儒學學正楊玘序。
translation_en:
…virtue, triumph in the Metropolitan Examination under the Ministry of Rites, and respond to the Emperor in the Great Court, so as to embellish the grand plan of state and give harmonious voice to the Way of governance, serving as worthy and capable coadjutors to our dynasty. Thus you will cause the people of the world to regard you as auspicious signs of flourishing culture and felicitous omens of Great Peace—like auspicious stars and propitious clouds shining in the heavens, or unicorns (qilin) and phoenixes (fenghuang) appearing in the suburban marshes. Will not the glory and the good fortune then be even greater! I write this postface and wait to see it fulfilled.
On the sixteenth day of the eighth month in the autumn of the guiyou year of the Jingtai reign (September 18, 1453), written as a postface by Yang Qi 楊玘, Director of Studies of the Confucian School of Dongping Subprefecture in Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong.
